versions.title: Readable weapon selection
versions.notes: - Mark the equipped weapon with [selected] instead of a star that could display as a missing-glyph box. Update the weapon-count tooltip to match.

versions.title: Main menu and onboarding
versions.notes:
- Start on a main menu with New Game, Load Game, Story, How to Play, Settings, Version History, and Exit.
- Browse the complete version history from the main menu as well as Escape.
- Read the city backstory and a scrollable guide before starting.
- Adjust shared audio settings from the title screen or pause menu.
- Return to the main menu from Escape without losing the current session; Resume continues it. Starting over asks before discarding unsaved progress; canceling a title-screen load returns to the menu.
- World simulation stays paused while browsing the menu.

versions.title: First playable survival sandbox
versions.notes:
EXPLORATION & SURVIVAL
- Explore a bounded city with 48 enterable buildings, two-room interiors, themed furniture, and proximity roof cutaways.
- Search outdoor and indoor supply crates; harvest trees and salvage wrecked cars.
- Manage health, nutrition, rations, sprinting, and escalating nighttime danger.
- Fight zombies and faster ferals with mouse-aimed combat and visible hit/damage feedback.

WEAPONS & CRAFTING
- Hatchet, wood-only club, spear, renewable wood-only bow/arrows, scavenged pistols and rifles.
- Finite ammunition, crafting costs, carried weapon quantities, and equipped-weapon indicators.
- Ranged weapons fire over placed defenses; city walls remain cover. Spears reach through barricades.

BUILDING & BASE DEFENSE
- Build barricades, shelters, gates, farms, and ammunition-fed turrets.
- Placement previews and collision checks; Shift-click repeat placement; R rotates barricades/gates.
- Open/close gates with E, repair barricades with V, and demolish placed structures with Shift+X for condition-based material refunds.
- Shelter zones exclude enemy spawns but can be overrun; turrets need ammunition.
- Grow renewable food in farms and plant saplings for renewable wood.

SURVIVORS
- Recruit survivors, escort them to shelter, and take guards on expeditions.
- Spaced follower formations; point at a nearby ally and use T to follow/hold, G to equip, or U to reclaim a weapon.
- Health bars, numeric HP, targeted-ally status, J feeding, and gradual shelter recovery when threats are absent.
- Armed survivors defend the group and share your ammunition supply.

MAP, FEEDBACK & AUDIO
- District minimap and Q radar scans showing enemy/friendly last-known positions with range, fade, and cooldown.
- Recent interaction messages and a scrollable 500-event history saved with your game.
- Original positional sound effects, ambient drone, and persistent volume/mute controls.

SAVES & MENUS
- Separate Save Game and Load Game screens through Escape or F5/F9.
- Named snapshots without a fixed slot cap; explicit confirmations for overwriting and loading.
- Persistent world depletion, construction, allies, inventory, and interior loot; older-save migration.
- Pause, field guide, restart after death, and this in-game version log.

PROTOTYPE LIMITS
- Single-floor interiors and local AI steering; full pathfinding is not yet implemented.
- No multiplayer, controller support, world streaming, or indoor base construction.
- Code-drawn art and synthesized audio; balancing and listening-based mix review remain ongoing.

versions.title: Sound, growing crops, and clear roads
versions.notes:
- Add original synthesized wind, gunshots, dry clicks, hit confirmation, swings, gathering, crafting, building, and damage sounds. Nearby survivors and turrets have positional gunfire.
- Add a saved audio volume slider to the title and pause menus; zero mutes all sound. Wind pauses with gameplay.
- Farm plants grow continuously from green shoots to golden grain over their 60-second cycle. Aiming at the bed shows progress and harvest readiness; harvesting replants immediately.
- Face building entrances toward the main road and move rows clear of the crossroad, including roofs and awnings. Rotate indoor supplies with the buildings.
- Migrate occupants and placed structures near old building plots when loading older saves; retain resource IDs and crop growth.

**Limitations:** Audio is synthesized rather than recorded. Browser playback requires an initial user gesture. AI still uses direct steering rather than navigation meshes.

versions.title: An overgrown autumn county
versions.notes:
- Refresh the world with weathered surface shading, mixed evergreen/autumn trees, ground cover, layered rock mountains, roadside shoulders, and utility poles.
- Add pitched roofs, chimneys, framed windows, awnings, facade trim, interior shelving, floorboards, and warm ceiling lights.
- Give survivors and infected clothing details, backpacks, boots, and walking limb animation. Add a gloved first-person hand and a distinct hatchet edge.
- Rebalance sky/ambient light and material reflections; blend dusk and dawn with cooler night skies and warm indoor lighting.
- Batch repeated static scenery and grass to reduce draw calls. Preserve existing save IDs, world generation, collisions, and gameplay rules.

**Limitations:** Procedural low-poly art, not photorealism. Added trim, vegetation, poles, and pitched roofs are decorative; existing collision shapes remain. Browser performance still needs hardware-specific playtesting.

versions.title: Clearer gun feedback and menu shortcuts
versions.notes:
- Remove arrow glyphs from Begin Expedition and Resume so web fonts cannot display missing-character boxes.
- Press C again to close crafting and resume; typing C in save names does not close the save browser.
- Pistol shots show a muzzle flash, recoil, and nearby ammo count. Confirmed hits show a large hit marker and damage; lethal hits show KILL.
- Empty trigger pulls show a red EMPTY prompt without firing feedback. Misses show FIRED instead of a hit marker.

**Limitations:** Feedback is visual; sound effects are not included. Browser pointer-lock policies still apply when resuming from crafting.

versions.title: Mouse capture and compact saves
versions.notes:
- Use unscaled mouse movement for aiming, keep yaw bounded over repeated turns, and discard capture-transition and oversized motion events.
- Press P to pause/resume. Escape releases the cursor and leaves the game paused; Resume requests capture on the initial button press.
- Pause when focus or pointer lock is lost. Browser gameplay waits for pointer lock and returns to the pause screen if the browser refuses it.
- Place the save-name field beside Create Save, with compact save rows showing names and timestamps on the left and Overwrite/Load on the right.

**Limitations:** Browser policy still controls pointer lock; embedded hosts must allow it. Save compatibility and gameplay systems are unchanged.

versions.title: Named expeditions and survivor equipment
versions.notes:
- Create separate named saves, browse names and UTC timestamps, and confirm before overwriting or loading.
- Open Save Game with F5 and Load Game with F9, or use the menus. Existing single-slot saves appear as Legacy quicksave.
- Give your selected spear or pistol to a recruited survivor with G; reclaim their weapon with U. Swapping returns their previous weapon.
- Craft spare weapons and see carried quantities in the HUD. Equipped survivors visibly carry weapons, use spear reach or pistol gunfire, and share your ammunition.
- Preserve survivor equipment in every save. Older saves load with survivors unarmed.

**Limitations:** No save rename/delete controls or autosave. Your starting hatchet stays with you. Empty survivor pistols fall back to close-range melee. Existing bounded-map and steering-AI limitations remain.

versions.title: The Quiet After — initial prototype
versions.notes:
- Explore a first-person 3D forest and town with enterable supply buildings, roads, and wrecks.
- Harvest wood and metal, search supply crates, and manage health, nutrition, and stamina.
- Fight infected with a hatchet, crafted spear, or pistol. Sprint, jump, and use a flashlight after dark.
- Recruit survivors, command them to follow or hold, and help them recover near a shelter.
- Craft barricades, shelters, farms, and turrets with validated placement. Grow food and load turret ammunition.
- Survive day/night cycles with more dangerous infected at night. Scan nearby contacts with local radar.
- Save and restore expeditions, including depleted supplies, inventory, survivors, structures, and world time.
- Includes a title screen, pause menu, crafting menu, field guide, and scrollable version log.

**Limitations:** Prototype: bounded, fixed-seed map; direct-steering AI; finite wood and metal; one save slot. No audio, multiplayer, controller support, or full feature parity with 2D Deadblock.

versions.title: Shared job board
versions.notes:
- Every shelter beacon has a Job board: anyone writes a task ("200 stone", "light the north road"), takes one, and marks it done.
- A finished task goes in the chronicle and a toast says who did it. Done tasks come down after 3 days; a board holds 20.
- In co-op the host keeps the boards, so everyone sees the same tasks.

**Limitations:** Friends see the board as it was when they opened it; reopen it to see newer changes.

versions.title: Build permissions
versions.notes:
- Co-op hosts can set what each friend may do, from any beacon menu: Full builder (the default), Builds outside shelters (nothing within 24 blocks of a beacon), or Guest (looks only: no building, breaking or crates).
- Friends are told their level when they join and whenever it changes, and their game stops a refused edit before it's made.
- Levels are saved by name, so a friend keeps theirs next time.

**Limitations:** Lockers still have their own owners on top of this. Levels go by the name a friend joins with.

versions.title: Traps
versions.notes:
- Spike pits (6 sticks and a plank): stakes that cut whoever steps in, 2 a second, and slow them.
- Bear traps (3 iron and a scrap, at the workbench): snap shut for 4 damage and hold whoever stepped in for 3 seconds. Right-click a sprung trap to set it again.
- Tripwires (2 sticks, 3 plant fiber, a scrap): ring a bell and tell you how far away and what crossed. They hurt nobody.
- Traps don't tell friend from Ashen: you and your friends get caught too. Followers and animals walk around them. Tips say so the first time you craft one and the first time you set one down.

**Limitations:** In co-op each player's own game catches them, and the host's game catches the Ashen, followers and animals.

versions.title: The Ashford Gazette
versions.notes:
- Every seventh dawn the Ashford Gazette comes out: a headline from the week's biggest news, a few lines from the chronicle, a follower's quote, a WANTED (a Named Ashen on the prowl, or the mayor's bounty) and tomorrow's weather.
- Read it in the journal's new Gazette tab, or from any beacon (The Ashford Gazette). The last four issues are kept.

**Limitations:** In co-op the host's game prints the paper; friends see an empty tab.

versions.title: Restart Ashford's grid
versions.notes:
- Once Ashford is reclaimed, its dead substation turns up beside the square, with a journal note.
- Repair it (8 steel ingots, 6 wire, 2 rubber) and power it (3 a second, only at night): after dark Ashford's windows light up and a lamp glows over every street corner, a landmark you can see from far off.
- The first night it runs, the radio picks it up and the chronicle remembers it. It's a quiet machine.

**Limitations:** The far-terrain ring doesn't draw the lit windows; the corner lamps are what shows from a distance. In co-op the lights follow each game's own power readings.

versions.title: Children and elders
versions.notes:
- About one in seven survivors you find in ruins, cities, metro stations and on the road is a child, and as many are elders. Kids are smaller; elders stoop.
- They can't fight: no weapons, bolts, jobs (beyond a child's gathering), stances or expeditions, and they run from the Ashen nearby. A tip explains the first time you take one in.
- Posted at a shelter, a child gathers berries and plant fiber into the crate there.
- An elder teaches: you earn 15% more XP within 24 blocks of their post, and followers posted there become seasoned after four days instead of five.

**Limitations:** Survivors you already met keep their age (adults). In co-op, friends see kids and elders at full size.

versions.title: Follower squads
versions.notes:
- A Squad button on the follower panel: up to three followers in your squad.
- The whistle key (U, rebindable) orders the whole squad at once, cycling Come (follow close), Hold here (guard where they stand) and Trail (follow about 8 blocks behind).
- The status line shows your squad and its order: "Squad: Mara, Deng · Trail". The squad is saved.

**Limitations:** In co-op, a friend's whistle only reaches the host's followers with Hold here (they can't follow a friend yet).

versions.title: Follower loadouts
versions.notes:
- The beacon menu has a Loadouts page: one row per job. Pick a job while holding a sword, axe or crossbow to set its weapon, or a stack of bolts to set how many bolts it carries (up to 64); anything else clears it.
- Each dawn, followers posted at that shelter with that job top up from crates within 12 blocks of the beacon: a missing weapon is fetched, bolts are filled to the number you set.
- If the crates run short, a toast says what was missing ("short of 15 bolts").

**Limitations:** Followers carry only a weapon and bolts, so that's what a loadout sets (no tools for farmers yet). The host sets loadouts in co-op.

versions.title: Auto-crafter
versions.notes:
- An auto-crafter (4 steel, a workbench and 2 wire, at the workbench). Crouch and right-click it holding what it should make: bolts, wire, planks, anything you craft by hand or at a workbench.
- Powered (2 a second), it crafts one batch every 4 seconds from its 9 input slots and any crate touching it, into its 3 output slots (the last row of its window).
- Hoppers and pipes can feed its input and pull from its output, so a base can keep itself stocked.
- Aim at it to see what it makes and what it's short of. It's a loud machine at night (wall it in to muffle it).

**Limitations:** One recipe per crafter; it picks the first recipe that makes the item. It draws power only while it has what it needs.

versions.title: Livestock pens
versions.notes:
- A feed trough (4 planks, at the workbench) with a 3-slot bin. Fence in the ground around it (walls count, 24 blocks across at most) and it's a pen.
- Penned deer, boar, sheep and horses eat wheat, berries or potatoes from the trough: they go tame and breed on their own in spring and summer, up to 8 animals to a pen.
- Penned sheep grow their wool back twice as fast. Every two boar or deer in a pen leave a manure in the trough at dawn; manure fertilizes farmland like ash dust.
- Hoppers can fill a trough with feed. Aim at one to see how many animals the pen holds and how much feed is left, or why it isn't a pen yet.

**Limitations:** A pen is the ground at the trough's own level; fences on a slope may leave gaps. Animals in a pen still need you nearby for the world there to run.

versions.title: Beehives
versions.notes:
- A beehive (8 planks, at the workbench): set it under open sky with at least 3 flowers within 6 blocks (berry bushes, growing crops or leaves) and every half day it makes a honey and a beeswax, up to 4 of each. Right-click to take them; hoppers can pull them out. Bees rest in winter.
- Hives keep count while you're away: come back after a few days and they've filled up.
- Honey is food that never spoils; bread and honey make honey bread (11 food, then a while of sprinting for free).
- Candles (a beeswax and a plant fiber make two): a small light of 10 blocks that needs no power and can't be wired.
- Aim at a hive to see what it holds and why it's idle.

**Limitations:** Hives work only where the ground around them is loaded when they check in; nothing tells you how long until the next batch.

versions.title: Undo
versions.notes:
- Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac) takes back your last place or break, up to ten steps: a placed block comes back to your pack, and a broken one goes back in the world (its drop leaves your pack).
- A whole line, wall or floor from the build tool undoes as one step.
- It only undoes your own edits, and only if nothing changed there since. Crates, machines with a bin, crops, saplings and doors can't be undone, and neither can a break whose drop you've already used.

**Limitations:** The undo list isn't saved and is just for you; in co-op an undo is an ordinary edit (lockers apply).

versions.title: Line and box tools
versions.notes:
- Hold Left Alt (rebindable; a Build button on touch) and right-click to start a line of the block in your hand, then look where it should end: a ghost shows the blocks and how many you have.
- The mouse wheel, or another right-click, switches between Line, Wall (up to 8 high) and Floor. Let go of the key to build, up to 64 blocks at once, nearest first, until you run out.
- It works with plain solid blocks (planks, stone, brick, concrete and the like); doors, crates, machines and the like still go one at a time. A tip explains it the first time.

**Limitations:** One block type per drag, along the world's axes.

versions.title: Calmer horror
versions.notes:
- A new setting, Calmer horror, for younger players or anyone who'd rather build: a screamer's scream becomes a quiet note at the top of the screen instead of a shriek.
- The Ashen's groans and hits (and nests' and the Colossus's) play softer and lower, they look greyer, and their hit flash is pale instead of red.
- A fallen Ashen crumbles into a puff of grey ash where it stands instead of toppling over.
- It only changes how the game looks and sounds on your device: the Ashen are just as dangerous, and friends in co-op keep their own setting.

versions.title: Motion comfort
versions.notes:
- New comfort settings beside Field of view: Head bob (the view and the item in your hand), Camera shake, and a Steady center dot.
- Camera shake is new too: a small kick when something hits you, recoil from the crossbow, a dip on hard landings, and the ground shaking when a burrower comes up or the Colossus wakes. Turn it off and the view stays still.
- The steady center dot sits in the middle of the screen whatever the view does, which helps if first person makes you queasy.

**Limitations:** Settings are per device.

versions.title: Smaller saves
versions.notes:
- Saves store your building and digging far more compactly: each changed block is a couple of bytes, and the whole save squeezes them together. Long worlds with big builds save several times smaller.
- The first time you save an older world after this update, a note says how much the save shrank.
- The console has /savesize: the save's size on disk and its biggest parts.
- Nothing you built or dug is ever dropped to make a save smaller, and older saves still load.

**Limitations:** Saves written by this version can't be opened by older versions of the game.

versions.title: Far terrain
versions.notes:
- Past your render distance, a flat low-detail ring of land now runs out to four times as far: hills, mountains, water and biome colors from the world's own shape, so mountains and coastlines stay on the horizon.
- Cities show as a skyline of simple blocks, one per building.
- It's built off the main thread, rebuilt every 64 blocks you travel, and fades into the horizon haze (fully hidden in storms and underwater).
- Settings, Far terrain, turns it off; the slowest devices get it off when settings are suggested.

**Limitations:** The far ring shows the land as the world generated it: your builds, craters and ruins don't appear in it.

versions.title: Crate labels and find item
versions.notes:
- Named crates show their name floating above them when you're within 8 blocks.
- The inventory screen has a Find item box: type part of a name and the pack dims everything else, and the line under the hotbar lists the crates and machine bins within 32 blocks that hold it (name, how many, how far).
- Found containers glow through walls for 20 seconds so you can walk straight to them.
- In co-op the host answers the search, and a locker only shows up if its owner lets you open it.

**Limitations:** Followers' hands and jeep racks aren't searched.

versions.title: Quarry drill
versions.notes:
- A quarry drill (6 steel, 2 iron, a wrench, at the workbench): powered, it mines the 3x3 column under it block by block, top down, into its 9-slot bin. Hoppers can pull from it.
- It stops at bedrock or water, when its bin is full, or while anyone stands in the shaft, and won't dig inside a city or within 16 blocks of a shelter.
- Aim at it or open it to see how deep it is and what it found ("Depth 14 · 38 cobblestone, 6 iron ore").
- It draws 3 power a second while it digs, nothing once it stops. The first time you carry one, a tip warns that the shaft it leaves is open and deep.

**Limitations:** In co-op only the host's aim text shows the depth (friends can still open the bin).

versions.title: Ash as fertilizer
versions.notes:
- A broom (3 sticks, 2 plant fiber): for a day after an ash storm, roofs and roads under open sky are dusty, and sweeping one gives 1-2 ash dust. Ash ground can be swept once a day.
- Ash dust on farmland ashes it: the next two growth stages of the crop there run half again faster, then the soil goes back to plain farmland.
- Four ash dust in a running water pump: every crop its sprinklers reach grows faster for a day.
- Nine ash dust make an ash pile block. The aim text shows dusty, swept and ashed ground.

**Limitations:** Swept marks aren't saved, so a reload lets you sweep the same roof again until the dust blows away.

versions.title: Legacy worlds
versions.notes:
- Every world you play is remembered on this device: the journal has a new Past lives page with each world's days survived, cities reclaimed and followers saved.
- Each world leaves an heirloom, the best tool or armor its player carried, named after the world (say, "Ashfall 2's Steel Pickaxe").
- The New World screen lets you start with one heirloom from a past life, at full durability, in your pack.

**Limitations:** Past lives are kept per device and browser (not in saves), so exporting a save doesn't carry them. Co-op joiners don't bring an heirloom.

versions.title: Metro stations
versions.notes:
- Where a metro tunnel reaches a city's edge, there's now a station: a taller hall with raised platforms either side of the rails, lamps still burning, a ticket office with a crate, and stairs up to the street beside the highway.
- Someone is usually waiting on the platform (talk to them, as in the ruins). Coming near a station puts it on your map as "<City> Station".

**Limitations:** Stations are carved when ground is first generated, so in older worlds only tunnels you haven't been near yet get them (the welcome message says so).

versions.title: Catch-up for late joiners
versions.notes:
- A friend who joins under half the host's level earns double XP until they reach half (the join message says so, and another tells them when they've caught up).
- Name a crate near a beacon "Joiner's crate": each new friend who joins gets a copy of what's in it, once. The crate keeps its things.

**Limitations:** The host's level is read when the friend joins; it doesn't follow the host's later levels until they rejoin.

versions.title: Touch controls, part two
versions.notes:
- New touch buttons: Sprint (hold it while you move the stick), Scout (toggles scout mode) and Sets (cycles your saved hotbar sets).
- Tap the look side with two fingers at once to open the map.
- Settings has Touch button size and Touch button opacity sliders.

**Limitations:** Not yet tried on a real phone (it's in PLAYTEST.md).

versions.title: Winter that bites
versions.notes:
- In winter, snow slowly settles on open natural ground around you (a thin layer you walk through and build over), and open water freezes to walkable ice, so no fishing through it. Spring melts both.
- Winter brings blizzards anywhere, not only in the frozen north. Out under the sky in one without a warm meal, you're Cold (shown in the status line) and lose 1 health every 20 seconds.
- The day-before-winter toast and a new journal note, Winter that bites, warn you first; the cold never bites before you've been told.

**Limitations:** Only the host's game lays snow and ice (friends see it through the world). Snow and ice laid are capped at 6000 blocks a winter.

versions.title: Guard dog
versions.notes:
- Stray dogs roam the streets of some cities (Ashford's always). They run from the Ashen.
- Feed one cooked meat three times and it's yours (one dog each): it follows you and catches up if you get far ahead, barks at Ashen within 16 blocks (with where they are), and sniffs out hollow walls and cache crates within 6.
- Your dog is saved with the world, eats cooked meat to heal, and can die if the Ashen get their teeth into it.

**Limitations:** Co-op friends see your dog but it only barks and sniffs in your game.

versions.title: Roadside events
versions.notes:
- Long trips along a highway now and then (once a day at most) meet something waiting 70 to 100 blocks up the road: a stalled car with a survivor beside it, an overturned truck with two crates spilled on the shoulder, or a pack of Ashen crossing the road.
- It's marked on the minimap (an arrow on the rim until it's in view) and in the status line with its distance and direction, so nothing ambushes you. Wait for a pack to cross or leave the road and go around.
- The first of each kind comes with a tip.

**Limitations:** In co-op only the host's trips meet roadside events.

versions.title: Ash surges
versions.notes:
- Now and then (at most every 6 nights, never on or right after a blood moon) the radio names a reclaimed city near you: tomorrow night the ash pushes back, and a pack marches on its main square. A journal note explains it the first time.
- Be there and hold the square: if 3 Ashen reach it, it falls. Nobody there? The square's lights, turrets and guards decide it.
- Held, it goes in the chronicle. Lost, the city is contested again until you relight its square. A new World option, Ash surges, turns them off.

**Limitations:** In co-op only the host's game runs surges, and a friend's map keeps showing a lost city as reclaimed until they rejoin.

versions.title: Tracks in the ash
versions.notes:
- Ashen walking on ash, snow or sand leave footprints. They fade at noon, so the morning after a bad night you can follow a trail back to where they came from: a nest, a building, a crater.
- The first morning there are tracks near you, a toast and a journal note explain them.

**Limitations:** Tracks are only left near you (within about 64 blocks) and aren't saved. In co-op each player sees the prints their own game's Ashen leave.

versions.title: Loud machines
versions.notes:
- At night, running machines make noise: generators and biomass burners while they burn, electric furnaces and grinders while they work, and turrets when they fire. Ashen within about 24 blocks (32 for turrets) come to see.
- Wall a machine in with stone, brick or concrete on all four sides and over the top and it's muffled. Look at a machine: it says Loud or Loud (muffled).
- The first night one of your machines runs, a toast and a journal note explain it, and that night stays quiet. A new World option, Machine noise, turns it off.

**Limitations:** Only machines within about 96 blocks of the host make noise. Noise brings the Ashen after you, not to the machine itself.

versions.title: Painted glass and banners
versions.notes:
- Painted glass: 4 windows and a dye make 4 panes of red, orange, yellow, green, white or black glass (by hand). They're see-through and tint the light like stained glass.
- Banners: 3 cloth, a stick and a dye make a banner on a pole in one of the six colors. Each banner flies as a little flag in its color on your map and minimap, and the journal's Shelters tab says which color flies over a shelter.
- In co-op, friends see your banners on their maps too (they come with the world).

versions.title: Shared sleep and personal lockers
versions.notes:
- Co-op: lying down in a bed no longer skips the night for everyone. Friends see "Mara is ready to sleep (1/3)" and press Y (Settings can rebind it) to agree from wherever they are; the night passes once everyone who isn't downed agrees. Playing alone, sleep works as before.
- Locker (4 iron ingots and a crate at a workbench): a crate only its placer can open or break. Crouch and right-click your locker to add or remove friends.
- Fix: Halcyon's locked lab drawers now open with a right-click when you carry the right badge (v0.13.73 and v0.13.74 left them shut).

**Limitations:** Lockers only lock in co-op; playing alone they're plain crates. Hoppers and pipes can still move items in and out of a locker.

versions.title: Named Ashen: Dr. Sall
versions.notes:
- Once you've found Halcyon, the radio names Dr. Sall, Halcyon's night chemist, and a journal note says she walks the streets outside Halcyon Labs at night from three days later.
- She keeps her distance and lobs jars of gas: a green cloud that slows you and costs about 1 health a second while you're in it (a tip explains it the first time). She slips away at dawn.
- Kill her and she's gone for good, leaving her lab badge. It opens the chemists' drawer in Halcyon Labs, one floor above the security drawer, with her notebook and loot.

**Limitations:** Only Halcyon Labs in ground your world hasn't generated yet has the locked drawers. In co-op only the host hears the warning, and her gas only reaches the host.

versions.title: Named Ashen: Chief Okafor
versions.notes:
- Once you've seen a military base and it's day 8, the radio names Chief Okafor, Halcyon's head of security, and a journal note says which base he walks and from which night (three days later).
- He walks that base at night: tougher than a brute, and he still has the door codes. Wooden and iron doors open for him; steel doors hold. He slips away at dawn instead of burning.
- Kill him and he's gone for good, leaving his security badge in a bag where he fell. It opens a locked drawer in Halcyon Labs (ground floor, beside the researcher's chest) with his last log and military loot.

**Limitations:** Only Halcyon Labs in ground your world hasn't generated yet has the locked drawers. In co-op only the host hears the radio warning and gets the journal note.

versions.title: Expeditions
versions.notes:
- Send an expedition from a Shelter Beacon's menu: two or three followers with the Guard job posted there set out for a city you know, and come back at the dawn after next.
- Weapons, ammo, seasoned guards and good health help; Halcyon is dangerous, a reclaimed city is easy. The menu shows each city's danger and the odds.
- They come back with loot in the beacon's crates, a new survivor for the shelter, or hurt with nothing. Nobody dies out there, but while they're away they don't guard the shelter. It goes in the chronicle and their histories.

**Limitations:** One expedition per shelter at a time. In co-op only the host can send one.

versions.title: Handcars on the metro rails
versions.notes:
- Handcar (6 iron ingots and 4 planks at a workbench): put it on the rails in a metro tunnel under a highway and ride it between cities. W pumps it up to 14 blocks a second, S slows and backs up, Shift steps off; it stops where the tunnel ends.
- Its lamp lights the tunnel, and Ashen in the dark ahead show as two glowing eyes. Going fast knocks common Ashen aside; a brute stops you dead. A tip on the first ride says to keep the lamp on.
- Left-click a handcar to pick it up. It's saved with the world.

**Limitations:** Friends in co-op don't see your handcar (like jeeps).

versions.title: Paraglider
versions.notes:
- Paraglider (6 cloth and 2 steel ingots at a workbench): hold it, jump off something tall, and keep holding jump once you're falling to open it. You drift down slowly, about 4 blocks forward for every block down, steering by looking.
- Let go of jump to fold it. No fall damage from a glide, and the Ashen can't follow. A first-time tip explains it.

**Limitations:** Friends in co-op don't see your canopy. No durability.

versions.title: Molotovs
versions.notes:
- Molotovs: smelt sand into a glass bottle, then add cloth and coal (by hand). Throw one and it bursts into fire: 6 damage nearby, Ashen in it keep burning, and a nest within reach burns as if you'd used a torch.
- Wood and leaves near the burst catch fire and it spreads like wildfire, so mind your walls and the forest. Stone and water stop it, and the Wildfire world option turns it off. The first one you get comes with a tip.
- Holding a molotov or a throwing dagger shows a dotted arc of where it will land.

**Limitations:** No sense of dry country beyond what burns: wildfire's own rules decide how far it spreads.

versions.title: Seasoned followers and grave visits
versions.notes:
- A follower who keeps the same job for five days becomes Seasoned at it: a step quicker at the work, and a seasoned guard hits harder. It shows in the journal and their history, and fades after five days on another job.
- Stand at a fallen follower's grave as dawn breaks and their friends nearby stop grieving. They remember the visit, and the chronicle notes it.

versions.title: World options per system
versions.notes:
- The pause menu has World options: turn wildfire, burrowers, seasons, or ash storms off (or back on) for this world, any time. All on by default.
- Wildfire off: lightning and fire set nothing alight, and fires burning now go out. Seasons off: it's always summer. Ash storms off: none come. Burrowers off: no Ashen dig up in the deadlands.
- In co-op the host's world options count for everyone.
- Tips and Difficulty now share a row in the pause menu.

**Limitations:** Not on the New World screen; change them in the game.

versions.title: Well rested and diet variety
versions.notes:
- Sleep in a real bedroom (a roof, walls all round with the door shut, and a light within 5 blocks of the bed) and you wake well rested: stamina comes back 30% faster and you earn 10% more XP until noon. A tip after your first sleep says what counts.
- Eating the same food again the same day fills 25% less each time (down to 40%), with a tip the first time.
- Three different foods in a day give a balanced diet until dawn: you get hungry 20% slower.

versions.title: Welcome back card
versions.notes:
- Loading a world an hour or more after you last saved it shows one card of where you left off: how long you've been away, what to do next, your quests, where your followers are, the last few chronicle lines, and the last few messages.

**Limitations:** Not shown when joining a friend's game.

versions.title: Hotbar sets and pick block
versions.notes:
- Hotbar sets: Shift+B saves your hotbar as one of three sets, and B swaps to the next, pulling its items from your pack and putting what was on the hotbar into it. Anything missing shows as a faint outline.
- Pick block: Ctrl + middle click puts the block you're aiming at into your hand from your pack, or tells you it isn't in your pack. It can also have its own key in Controls.

**Limitations:** No set buttons in the inventory screen or on touch controls yet.

versions.title: Searched marks
versions.notes:
- A ruin crate's lid comes off the first time you open it, so you can tell which you've been through.
- When every ruin crate in a city building is open (basements and hidden rooms count), the building is searched: a toast says so and the map greys it out with "searched".
- Each city's map label counts them, like "4/9 buildings searched". Shared with friends in co-op.

**Limitations:** Crates opened before this version keep their lids on. Friends who join later only see buildings searched after they joined.

versions.title: Toast history
versions.notes:
- The journal has a Messages tab: the last 40 pop-up messages with the day and time they came, newest first, kept in your save.
- A message that names a place you know (a city, shelter, marker, named crate, or landmark) has a Route button that sets your route there.

versions.title: Help search jumps to the match
versions.notes: - Clicking a search result in Help now opens the article scrolled to the line that mentions what you searched for, highlighted for a couple of seconds, instead of the top of the article.

versions.title: Dyes and paint
versions.notes:
- Six dyes, made by hand: red from ashberries, orange from scrap (rust), yellow from wheat, green from plant fiber, white from cotton, and black from ash.
- Paint 4 planks or 4 concrete with a dye: painted planks and concrete in all six colors, so bases and villages can have color.
- Painted blocks show in their color on the map, so you can tell shelters apart from far off.
- Brutes pound painted walls like plain ones, and a hammer mends them with the same painted block.

**Limitations:** Cloth isn't dyed, and painted blocks are flat colors without the plank or concrete texture.

versions.title: Carry a downed friend, and the morning report
versions.notes:
- Co-op: press F beside a downed friend to pick them up and carry them to safety. You walk at 60% speed and can't attack; F again sets them down so you can revive them.
- Their downed timer keeps running while you carry them, so don't go far.
- Co-op: at dawn everyone sees a morning report with each player's night (Ashen put down, friends revived, blocks built, and their closest call). It's kept in the journal too.

**Limitations:** Your first morning report after joining or loading counts from then, not from dusk.

versions.title: Two-player locks
versions.notes:
- Military bases now have a deep armory: a tunnel under the yard down to a sealed vault gate, with four military crates behind it.
- There's no key. The gate opens once both of the base's pressure plates, one in the barracks and one by the watchtower, are held at the same time.
- Playing alone? A follower counts: set one to guard on a plate and stand on the other yourself.
- A journal note explains it when you first come near the tunnel.

**Limitations:** Only military bases in ground your world hasn't generated yet have one. Once open, the gate stays open.

versions.title: Followers remember
versions.notes:
- Each follower keeps a short history of what you've been through together (taking them in, patching them up, a night you held, a blood moon at their shelter, a request you answered, a cure) and a mood toward you. The Followers tab shows both.
- Now and then a follower near you brings one of those memories up.
- A follower who falls leaves a grave with their name where they died. Right-click it to write an epitaph.
- Followers who were near a fallen friend grieve for a day: their morale drops a step.

**Limitations:** Followers met before this version start with no memories. In co-op the host's game keeps them.

versions.title: The world chronicle, and cured survivors remember
versions.notes:
- A new journal tab, Chronicle: each dawn it writes one line about the day before (the Ashen you put down, what you built, how far you walked, and anything big: a city reclaimed, a storm, a radio tower repaired, an achievement, a cure). A long world reads like a story.
- Survivors you cure sometimes remember where they hid supplies before they turned (a military crate out in the world, marked on your map), or something about Halcyon (four new notes).

**Limitations:** The chronicle keeps the last 400 days. Its first line in an existing world counts from when you loaded it.

versions.title: The radio tower network
versions.notes:
- Each radio tower now has a dead console at its foot. Repair it with 6 wire, 6 scrap, and a battery to put the tower back on the air.
- A repaired tower puts every place within 300 blocks on your map.
- While you're within 300 blocks of a repaired tower, supply planes drop their crate at its foot.
- Shelter beacons within 300 blocks of one count as on a road, so caravans can run from them.
- Every week at dawn the network sends a report: how many towers are up, this week's supply planes, and how much is still unmapped.

**Limitations:** Consoles only stand at towers in ground your world hasn't generated yet. A tower maps the places around it (cities, ruins, landmarks), not every block of ground. In co-op each player's repairs are their own.

versions.title: Lightning and wildfire
versions.notes:
- Summer days can bring a thunderstorm. Thunder and a status-line countdown warn you a minute ahead, and a journal note explains it the first time.
- Lightning strikes near you during the storm. It sets logs, leaves, planks, and boards alight, and hurts if you're right where it lands.
- Fire creeps slowly from block to block and burns them away. Stone, brick, concrete, and ash never burn.
- The rain at the end of the storm puts out fires under open sky. A water bucket puts out a fire and any around it, and you can knock flames out by hand. Standing in fire hurts.

**Limitations:** In co-op the host's game runs lightning and fire (friends see the flames, but not the flash). Fires burn on from the start after loading a save.

versions.title: Seasons
versions.notes:
- The year now turns: spring, summer, autumn, and winter, two weeks each. The status line shows the season and its day.
- In autumn crops grow at 60% speed; in winter they stop, unless there's glass over them (a window block as the first thing above) or the greenhouse dome is built.
- Winter covers the grass in snow and frosts the tree tops.
- A journal note explains it the first autumn, and a toast warns the day before winter.
- Tame animals breed only in spring and summer, and silverfin only bite then.

**Limitations:** The season comes from the world's day count, so an existing world starts in whatever season its day falls in.

versions.title: Touch controls
versions.notes:
- Phones and tablets get touch controls: slide a finger on the left side to move, drag on the right to look, and round buttons to hit, use, jump, sneak, open your bag, the map, and the menu.
- Tap a hotbar slot to pick it. While a menu or panel is open, a Back button at the top right closes it.
- Settings > Touch controls: Auto (phones and tablets), On (also works with a mouse, to try it on a computer), or Off.
- On a phone or tablet the first launch starts with a render distance of 4 chunks.
- Help > Survival explains the controls.

**Limitations:** Checked with a mouse and in tests, not yet on a real phone. Sprint, scout mode, and other keys without a button still need a keyboard or controller.

versions.title: "What next?" and the death recap
versions.notes:
- A small line under the compass now suggests one next step for where you are in the game: a workbench, an iron pickaxe, finding Ashford, a lit shelter, then Halcyon and its lab.
- It goes away once you've reached Halcyon Labs, and Settings > "What next?" line turns it off.
- The death card now says what hit you and for how much, and where ("Killed by a brute (6 damage) in Ashford"), with one tip for that kind of death.

**Limitations:** The next step reads what you've done in this world (crafting, cities found, your shelter), not what you're doing right now.

versions.title: Co-op roles
versions.notes:
- Pick a role: Medic, Engineer, Scout, or Quartermaster, each with one small perk on top of your skills.
- Medic revives a downed friend twice as fast. Engineer gets half as much wire again when crafting it. Scout's scout mode sees half as far again. Quartermaster's crafting uses crates twice as far away.
- Choose it in Settings > Co-op role or on the Join panel, or swap at any shelter beacon (Your role). It's kept in your settings, and solo players can take one too.
- In co-op your role shows beside your name in the pause menu's player list.

**Limitations:** The Quartermaster's perk is crafting reach, not an extra crate row: crates are a fixed 9 slots.

versions.title: Jeep upgrades
versions.notes:
- New block: the garage (8 cobblestone, 4 iron ingots, 4 planks). Park a jeep within 10 blocks and right-click it to fit upgrades.
- Plow (6 iron ingots): shoves the Ashen out of the way as you drive. Brutes stand their ground.
- Armor plates (4 steel ingots): you take half damage while driving.
- Roof rack (a crate, 2 iron ingots): a 9-slot crate on the roof. Crouch and right-click the jeep to open it.
- Headlights (a floodlight, a battery): a beam at night, and no Ashen rise on the road ahead of you while you're moving.
- Upgrades don't slow the jeep, they're saved with it, and picking it up keeps them (the rack's load comes with you).

**Limitations:** In co-op each player's jeeps stay in their own game, as before.

versions.title: Elevators
versions.notes:
- New: elevator rails (2 iron ingots make 4) and the elevator car (6 iron ingots, 2 wire).
- Stack rails in a column, wire power to them, and right-click the side of a rail with the car to set it there.
- Stand on the car and hold jump to rise or crouch to go down, 3 blocks a second. It uses 1 power a second while it moves, stops where the rails end or the shaft is blocked, and settles on a whole level.
- Crouch and right-click the rail to take the car back. Cars are saved with the world. Help > Electrical explains it.

**Limitations:** No floor buttons or call switches, and followers don't ride it. In co-op the host's game moves the cars.

versions.title: Sprinklers and irrigation
versions.notes:
- New: the water pump (3 iron ingots, a wire, a bucket). Set it beside water and power it (0.5 a second) and it feeds the water pipes joined to it.
- Water pipes (an iron ingot makes 4) join up like item pipes; a pump feeds up to 48 of them.
- Sprinklers (an iron ingot and a pipe) on those pipes water the farmland within 4 blocks, so crops there grow as fast as crops beside water. No more walking buckets to a far field.
- Right-click a pump or sprinkler to see whether it's working. Help > Electrical explains it.

**Limitations:** Sprinkled crops count as watered, nothing more. In co-op the host's game runs the pumps.

versions.title: Searchlight turret
versions.notes:
- New power block: the searchlight (a floodlight, 2 iron ingots, 2 wire, at a workbench). It uses 1.5 power a second, only at night.
- A powered searchlight sweeps the dark around it in a slow circle, once every 8 seconds, and locks onto the nearest Ashen within 24 blocks.
- An Ashen in the beam moves at 70% speed, and followers with crossbows shoot it before anything else.
- Right-click one to see whether it's sweeping or locked on. Help > Electrical has the details.

**Limitations:** Only the 4 searchlights nearest you shine at once (the others still lock on and slow the Ashen). In co-op the host's game locks on; friends see the sweep.

versions.title: Block health and repairs
versions.notes:
- What the Ashen chew through now keeps its damage: boards, wooden doors, and windows show cracks as they're worked on, and the cracks stay between attacks and in your save.
- Brutes also pound on plank, brick, cobblestone, and concrete walls until they give (planks in about 25 seconds, brick 50, concrete 70). Steel doors and natural stone hold. The brute warning in the journal says so.
- Aiming at a cracked block shows what's left of it, like "Brick  ·  70% strength".
- New: the hammer (3 iron ingots, 2 sticks, at a workbench). Right-click a cracked block with it to mend it with one of its material (planks for boards and wooden doors).
- The Shelters page warns about damaged blocks near each beacon. Help > Cracks and the hammer explains it all.

**Limitations:** Mining doesn't wear blocks; only the Ashen do. In co-op the host keeps the wear and shares it every half second.

versions.title: Milestone projects
versions.notes:
- A Shelter Beacon's menu has a new Projects page: four big builds, each done once per world.
- Starting one lays it out beside the beacon as a blue ghost. Builders posted nearby put it up from their crate, a third at a time, and say when each stage is up.
- Water tower: crops within 24 blocks of any shelter beacon count as watered. Greenhouse dome: those crops grow at the lit rate, day and night.
- Radio station: you hear the dusk broadcasts without carrying a radio. Highway depot: caravans run twice as often, and jeeps go 10% faster on roads.
- A finished project helps every shelter and is saved with the world. Help > Milestone projects explains them.

**Limitations:** Projects need a follower with the Builder job. In co-op only the host starts them, and the radio station and depot's jeep speed are the host's.

versions.title: Islands offshore
versions.notes:
- Small islands now rise out of the open sea past the shorelines: a sand rim, grass, and berry bushes.
- Each has a red-and-white lighthouse. Climb the ladder inside to the lamp platform 22 blocks up, high enough to scout from; islands show up as landmarks.
- A hermit lives in a hut by the light and can be recruited; his crate holds the lighthouse keeper's log.
- A wreck lies half-sunk in the shallows east of each island, its bow out of the water and a crate in its flooded hold.
- A reason to build a boat outside the swamps. Help > Boats mentions them.

**Limitations:** Islands appear only in sea not yet generated in older worlds. The Ashen can still spawn on an island's dark ground at night.

versions.title: Hidden rooms
versions.notes:
- Some city buildings hide a closet behind a false wall in a back corner of the ground floor. It looks like the rest of the wall, but it knocks hollow when you hit it; break through for the crate inside.
- Some basements have a storeroom behind a rusted-shut door, with a military crate and more. Only a wrench pries it open: hold attack for 4 seconds.
- Some taller flat-roofed buildings have a rooftop garden: rows of crops gone to seed, free to harvest.
- The first crate you open in a city holds a scrawled note about hollow walls and gardens; a later one, a building super's ledger about the storerooms.

**Limitations:** Hidden rooms appear only in city ground not yet generated in older worlds. A window can give a closet away.

versions.title: Dams and hydro power
versions.notes:
- Dams now stand in some of red rock canyon country's empty cells: a concrete wall holding back its own reservoir, a spillway pouring into a plunge pool, a powerhouse below, and steps up to a railed walkway 12 blocks up (high enough to scout from).
- The powerhouse's hydro turbine is dead until you bring it 8 wire, 8 scrap, and a battery. Restarted, it makes 10 power a second, day and night, for anything wired to it. Run wires or power poles back to a base. It shows in the power graph as Hydro Turbine.
- Dams are landmarks on the map and have a codex page; Help > Electrical explains the turbine.

**Limitations:** Dams appear only in canyon ground not yet generated in older worlds; ground you changed near one may look different. The turbine can't be moved, so its power has to travel.

versions.title: Power graph
versions.notes:
- The pause menu has a Power graph button (beside Shelters), which opens the journal's new Power tab: what every network made, by source (solar, wind, water, generators, biomass), and used, by machine kind, as lines over time with a white total.
- Pick how far back to look: 10s, 30s, 1m, 5m, 10m, 30m, 60m, 2h, or 5h. The legend lists each line's average.
- Machines on a network that's short of power count as using nothing (they stand idle).

**Limitations:** The graph covers the whole world and only what happened since you loaded (it isn't saved); the game pauses while the journal is open. In co-op it's the host's: a friend's tab says so.

versions.title: Backup generators, biomass burner, power poles
versions.notes:
- Generators have a mode button in their window: Always (as before) or Backup. A backup generator waits until its network's batteries drop under 25%, then burns until they're back to 60% (with no batteries, only while the network needs more than it makes). Solar by day, fuel for the gaps.
- Biomass Burner (8 cobblestone, 2 iron, 2 wire): 2 power a second, burning crops, seeds, leaves, plant fiber, berries, sticks, and saplings. Hoppers and belts can feed it, and it has the same Always / Backup button.
- Power Pole (3 logs, 2 wire): joins every power block within 6 blocks and every other pole within 12 into one network, no wires needed. Hold a pole or wire to see the links.
- Help > Electrical explains all three; PLAYTEST.md has a power-pole balance item.

**Limitations:** Pole links are only drawn while you hold a pole or wire. In co-op, a friend's mode switch is checked and kept by the host.

versions.title: Berry bushes and near shadows
versions.notes:
- Berry bushes no longer have dark sides in daylight: the side tint for grass, snow, and the like now only applies to plain-colored blocks, not textured ones.
- Sharper, steadier shadows near you: at render distance 8 or more the sun uses four blended shadow splits (two below that, for speed), and shadows sit closer to the walls that cast them, so tall buildings shade the street beside you properly.

**Limitations:** Not tuned by eye on every GPU: if shadows shimmer or show stripes, lower the render distance below 8 for the old two-split shadows.

versions.title: Reclaim a city
versions.notes:
- Every city but Ashford has a heart nest on the top floor of its tallest building (a highrise where it has one). While you are within 24 blocks it lets out an Ashen every 10 seconds. It takes three torch burns, and each burn tears a brute loose.
- Reclaim a city by burning its heart nest, burning every nest in its buildings, and lighting its main square (where the two boulevards cross by the mayor's hall; the map marks it while you are in the city).
- A reclaimed city never spawns Ashen, turns green on your map, and three survivors move into its square. Stats shows World reclaimed (cities out of the ones you know), and a new achievement marks the first.
- Ashford has no heart and no nests: lighting its square is enough. It is the guided start's new last step, after Reach Ashford, and a journal note explains the whole loop.
- The quest list shows a city's progress while you are in it. In co-op, progress is shared.

**Limitations:** Older worlds: city ground you haven't changed may grow a heart nest on its tallest building. Nests you burned before this version count once you're back near them.

versions.title: Skyscrapers
versions.notes:
- Cities other than Ashford now have highrises near their center: one building across four lots (about 35 blocks wide), 8 to 18 stories, with setbacks and an antenna like Halcyon's towers.
- Highrise and Halcyon tower stories are split into rooms: some are open plan, some a grid of rooms, some offices either side of a corridor. Every wall has a doorway.
- The upper floors of other buildings four or more stories tall get an inner wall with a doorway, and a second wall on every other floor.

**Limitations:** Older worlds: city ground you haven't changed may rebuild with highrises and rooms; ground you changed keeps your edits. Ashford's skyline is unchanged.

versions.title: Base overview
versions.notes:
- The pause menu has a Shelters button, and the journal a Shelters tab: one card for every Shelter Beacon, with how far it is, its followers and their jobs, their morale, the power there, and the food in its crates.
- Each card warns about what needs you: an unlit beacon, unhappy followers, no food, power running short, or an Ashen nest within 48 blocks.
- Route on a card draws a route line to that shelter.

**Limitations:** Damaged walls aren't listed yet. In co-op, a friend's cards leave power and food to the host's game.

versions.title: Codex
versions.notes:
- The journal (J) has a Codex tab: a page for every block, item, creature, and place, with its picture, what it's for, and what it's made from and into.
- Pages fill in as you find things: carry something, come within 20 blocks of a creature, or stand in a biome, city, or ruin. Each page says the day and where you first found it.
- Things you haven't found show as ? under their category, with a count of how many are left.

**Limitations:** Pages for things found before this version fill in the next time you carry or see them. Creatures and places have no picture yet.

versions.title: Save versions
versions.notes:
- Load World shows which version each world was made on, and each save says which version made the world and which last saved it.
- The playtest checklist has a v1 readiness section: when to run the full pass and what it covers.

**Limitations:** Worlds made before this version show "made on before v0.13.33"; there's no way to know their first version.

versions.title: Rename a world
versions.notes:
- Load World on the title screen has a Rename button on each world. Type the new name and press Enter (or Rename); Cancel or All worlds leaves it as it was.
- Every save of that world (its exit save, quicksave, and autosave too) takes the new name. Your saves, their files, and the seed don't change, and Continue shows the new name.

**Limitations:** Renaming is on the title screen only, not in the pause menu's Load World. A blank name does nothing.

versions.title: Burrowers
versions.notes:
- At night in the deadlands, Ashen now dig up through dark ground near you every minute or so (more often on Harsh, less on Calm).
- Each one gives warning: a deep rumble, dust puffing up from the ground, and a toast, four seconds before it breaks the surface. The first one also adds a journal note.
- A lit floor stops them, as do floors you've built and claimed ground. Light the spot during the rumble and the burrower turns back.

**Limitations:** Burrowers only dig around you, not around a co-op friend. They come up as ordinary Ashen.

versions.title: Fishing
versions.notes:
- A fishing rod (3 sticks and 2 plant fiber, by hand). Aim at a lake, river, the sea, or the swamp and right-click to cast a bobber; when it dips, right-click within about a second to reel in. Too slow and the fish gets away, but the line stays cast.
- Raw fish cook into cooked fish in a furnace (and a shelter kitchen). Two cooked fish and a baked potato make fish chowder, a meal that lets you sprint free for 150 s.
- Silverfin are rare, and bite most around dawn and dusk. Grilled, one lets you see in the dark for 120 s. Now and then you reel in a stick or scrap instead.

**Limitations:** Rods don't wear out. The line itself isn't drawn, just the bobber. Followers don't fish.

versions.title: Biome weather
versions.notes:
- Swamp fog: a pale green haze over the swamps, mostly at night and in the mornings, that hides what's coming until it's close.
- Canyon sandstorms, mostly in the afternoons: an orange haze, driving grit, and a howling wind that spins wind turbines faster.
- Blizzards in the frozen north: a white-out, and out under the open sky the cold makes you hungry faster (a warm meal stops it).
- Each rolls in over a few seconds as you cross into that country and clears as you leave. A toast says what's blowing, and the status line names it.

**Limitations:** Biome weather is rolled per half day, not by season (the world has no seasons yet). Wind turbines read the weather where you are, not where they stand.

versions.title: Conveyor belts
versions.notes:
- Conveyor belts (an iron ingot, 2 scrap, and rubber make 4 at the workbench): flat belts that carry items you can see along the floor at 4 blocks a second, toward their yellow arrow. They run away from you as you lay them and follow a line around corners.
- Point a hopper at a belt and it loads it every quarter second, twice a pipe's pace. The end of the line drops into the crate or machine it points at; with nothing there, items queue up and wait.
- Right-click a belt holding something to put one item on it, or empty-handed to take one off. Breaking a belt gives back what was on it. Help has a Conveyor belts section.

**Limitations:** Belts are flat: they don't climb or drop a level, and they don't carry you. Items on belts run in the host's game; co-op friends don't see them.

versions.title: Suggested settings and save storage
versions.notes:
- Suggested settings: the first time you play on a device, a few seconds of frame timing pick render distance and texture distance (and retro blocks on the slowest devices). A toast says what changed; Settings can change it back.
- If the frame rate stays low for a while, a toast offers to lower render and texture distance, and the pause menu has a button that does it.
- Load World shows how much storage your saves use and, in the browser, how much of its allowance the site uses, with a warning when it's nearly full.
- A reminder that saves live only in this browser, and Export All Worlds: every save in one file that Import a Save takes back.

**Limitations:** The storage figure for the whole site comes from the browser's estimate, which can be rough. Export All Worlds is on the title screen's Load World, not the pause menu's.

versions.title: Route line
versions.notes:
- The map has a Route button beside every marker, shelter, and city, and Route here for a spot you click. A blue line on the map and minimap leads the way.
- For long trips the route follows the highways between cities when that beats cutting across country, and the toast says how much of it is on roads and which cities it goes through.
- The line re-plans from where you are as you travel and clears when you arrive (or with Clear route). It's saved with the world.

**Limitations:** Routes know the highways, not city streets, rivers, or cliffs: the cross-country stretches are straight lines.

versions.title: Co-op shelters and spectating
versions.notes:
- The host's Shelter Beacon menu can make a friend a co-owner of that shelter (and take it back). Co-owners can travel there, paying from their pack, and give the host's followers within 24 blocks of it orders: guard where they stand, a job, or a stance. Friends can only travel to shelters they co-own.
- Hand over: look at a friend within 4 blocks and press F (rebindable) to pass them the stack in your hand. If their pack is full, what doesn't fit comes back.
- While you're down or dead in co-op, the camera follows a friend who's still up, and G pings where it looks.

**Limitations:** Co-owners give orders from a short menu, not the follower panel, and can't make the host's followers follow them. Co-owners are kept by name.

versions.title: Blueprints
versions.notes:
- A Blueprint (a cloth and a charcoal, crafted by hand) copies something you built: right-click two opposite corners, up to 16 blocks a side. It keeps the blocks you placed, not the ground.
- Right-click the ground with a filled blueprint to lay it down as a faint blue ghost. A follower with the Builder job posted within 48 blocks fills it in from their crate, bottom up, a few blocks each visit, before starting any new house. They tell you what they're short of.
- Crouch + right-click with the blueprint clears a ghost near you, or wipes the blueprint when no ghost is near. Blocks already built stay. The inventory tooltip shows a blueprint's size.

**Limitations:** Blueprints can't be turned; a ghost is laid down facing the way it was copied. Builders skip cells something else fills, and never break blocks. In co-op, only the host can lay ghosts down.

versions.title: Village life
versions.notes:
- Followers posted near a finished village house now live there, two to a house.
- Their day: up and out of the house after dawn, at their post and job through the day, a visit to the nearest Shelter Beacon around midday, and back indoors when night falls. Each one keeps a slightly different clock, so they don't all move at once.
- Followers on the guard job keep watch at their post all night. Followers open doors as they walk.
- The follower panel says when someone is at home or visiting the shelter.

**Limitations:** Followers walk in straight lines with simple steering; one who can't find the way while you're far off just turns up where they were going.

versions.title: Shelter upgrades
versions.notes:
- A Shelter Beacon's menu now sells upgrades, paid from your pack and the crates beside it. Each helps the followers posted within 24 blocks.
- Watchtower: followers there spot the Ashen twice as far off and go after any on the hunt. Infirmary: they heal 2 health every 10 seconds, and you heal twice as fast nearby. Kitchen: each dawn it cooks raw meat and tubers in the beacon's crates and bakes wheat into bread.
- Break a beacon and its upgrades stop; put it back on the same spot and they work again.

**Limitations:** In co-op, only the host can build upgrades.

versions.title: Traveling trader
versions.notes:
- Once a shelter has three or more claimed zones around it, a traveling trader comes to its beacon at dawn every few days (from day 3) and leaves at dusk. A gold marker on the map shows where.
- Right-click them for four trades, each up to three times: your surplus for seeds, saplings, steel, batteries, wire, and medkits. They take payment from your pack and crates within reach.
- The trades change with every visit. A journal note explains the first one.

**Limitations:** In co-op, the trader only visits the host's shelters, and only the host can trade.

versions.title: Follower traits and requests
versions.notes:
- Every follower has a trait, shown in their panel and the journal's Followers tab: green thumb, sharpshooter, night owl, or nervous. Each makes some jobs quicker and others slower, and sharpshooters hit harder while nervous followers hit softer.
- Now and then at dawn a guarding follower asks for something small: a bed of their own, a shield, a proper meal, or news from a city you haven't found yet.
- Right-click them holding it (or after finding a new city) for XP, and every follower posted nearby is in better spirits for three days.

**Limitations:** In co-op, only the host's followers make requests.

versions.title: Cure darts
versions.notes:
- After you deliver the counter-agent to Ashford, a new workbench recipe appears: two bolts and a medkit make two cure darts.
- Wear an Ashen down to half its health, then right-click it with a cure dart: it turns back into a survivor who follows you, ready to send to a shelter. The Colossus and the First are too far gone.
- Curing an Ashen gives XP, counts as a recruit, shows as "Ashen cured" in your stats, and earns a new achievement, Second Chance.

**Limitations:** In co-op, you can only cure the Ashen in your own game (the host's Ashen are the host's to cure).

versions.title: Halcyon's clinics and offices
versions.notes:
- In Halcyon, some ordinary buildings are now Halcyon offices, with a filing crate in the back corner holding staff notes.
- The first office crate or Halcyon Labs chest you open holds a Halcyon staff keycard.
- In other cities, a few plain concrete buildings are Halcyon clinics, with a locked terminal in the back corner. It can't be broken; open it with the staff keycard (it isn't used up) for medicine, steel, a piece of good gear, and a clinic's note.

**Limitations:** In older worlds, clinics and offices only appear in ground you haven't been to yet. In co-op, only the host can unlock a terminal.

versions.title: Bounty board
versions.notes:
- A bounty board hangs on the lobby wall of Ashford's mayor's hall, with three jobs a week: clear a named building in another city of Ashen, bring back lab parts, or rescue a survivor from a far city.
- Bounties pay more XP than shelter quests and rare things: steel, a leather backpack, medkits, rounds. They don't use up your 3 shelter quest slots.
- Hand lab parts in at the board. A rescued survivor finds you when you reach their city; walk them back to the hall alive.

versions.title: Supply drops and the radio
versions.notes:
- About three days a week a plane comes over by day and drops a supply crate 50 to 100 blocks from you, under a tall red flare you can see from far off. A warning says which way it's falling, and the map marks it.
- The crate holds the good stuff: medkits, food, rounds, bolts, batteries, iron and steel. The landing is loud: the Ashen around come running and a few more rise nearby.
- A radio (an iron ingot, 2 wire, a battery) in your pack picks up a broadcast at dusk: the time of tomorrow's supply plane, or a fragment of Halcyon's last days.

**Limitations:** In co-op, only the host sees the plane, the flare, and the warnings; a guest still finds the crate.

versions.title: Car salvage
versions.notes:
- A wrench (2 iron ingots and a stick, at a workbench) breaks car wrecks and rusted metal fast and strips them for parts: scrap, wire, rubber from the tires, and now and then cloth.
- Rubber and a scrap make 6 wire, and a jeep can be built with 4 rubber instead of 2 cloth and 2 of its iron ingots.
- The first time you carry a wrench, a tip says what it's for.

versions.title: Ashen nests
versions.notes:
- Some dark buildings in other cities hide an Ashen nest on the ground floor. While you're near, it lets an Ashen out every 30 seconds, day or night.
- Tools won't cut a nest: hold a torch and right-click it to burn it, for 25 XP.
- The first nest you see up close adds a journal note. Scout mode marks the nests you've come near with a red X.

**Limitations:** In older worlds, nests only grow in ground you haven't been to yet.

versions.title: Boarded windows
versions.notes:
- Boards: 2 planks and a stick make 3, by hand. Nail them across a window or doorway; they go up square to where you look.
- The Ashen claw through boards slowly (about 12 seconds, a brute about 4.5), and every second of it is a loud crack of wood.
- When something is tearing at your boards within 32 blocks, a toast says how far and which way.

**Limitations:** In co-op, guests don't hear the clawing (the host does, and the boards break for everyone).

versions.title: Difficulty presets
versions.notes:
- Pick Calm, Normal, or Harsh from the pause menu. It's saved with each world and you can change it any time.
- Calm: half as many Ashen and half as often, their hits at half strength, and hunger at 60%. Harsh: half again as many Ashen, hits half again as hard, and hunger at 140%.
- In co-op the host's world sets it for everyone. Help's Survival tab explains it.

**Limitations:** Worlds saved before this version start on Normal.

versions.title: Help search, quick stack, and sort
versions.notes:
- Help has a search box: type a word like "battery" to see every line in every tab that mentions it, and click one to open its tab.
- Quick stack (Z, or the new button in the inventory) moves everything in your pack, not the hotbar, into crates within 8 blocks that already hold that item.
- Sort buttons in the inventory and in crates merge stacks and put them in order. The hotbar stays as it is.

**Limitations:** In co-op, quick stack works for the host only.

versions.title: Tips and the night coach
versions.notes:
- The first time you carry a new kind of item (wire, seeds, a battery, a lead, a bucket, and more), a tip card says how to use it, with more in Help.
- Before your first night, the night coach warns that it's coming, shows the spawn marks around you for half a minute, and says which way your bed or shelter is.
- The world waits while a tip is open. Tips can be turned off per world, from the card or the pause menu, and back on from the pause menu.

**Limitations:** Worlds saved before this version skip tips for what's already in your pack and the night coach if you've seen a night.

versions.title: Chat history, note badge, crouch-placing
versions.notes:
- The console closes after you press Enter, leaving the reply up for a few seconds. Enter (as well as / and T) opens it again.
- Up and Down in the console bring back lines you sent before, like a terminal.
- A new journal note shows a toast and a badge above the hotbar until you open the journal, which opens straight to Notes.
- Crouch + right-click places a block against something you'd otherwise use, like a solar panel or a crate (Shift still works too).

versions.title: Ladders and ziplines
versions.notes:
- Ladders (7 sticks make 3) hang on a wall: walk into one to climb, sneak to hold still, let go to slide down. No fall damage on a ladder, and the Ashen can't climb them.
- Ziplines: string rope (4 plant fiber) between two zipline posts (2 iron ingots and a stick), one at least 2 blocks lower, up to 48 blocks apart. Right-click the high post to ride down; jump or Shift lets go.
- Ziplines are saved with the world and shared in co-op. Help has a page on both.

versions.title: Threaded web build
versions.notes:
- An optional threaded web build (in the threaded folder) streams chunks on worker threads, so the world loads faster and smoother.
- It needs a cross-origin isolated page: the co-op server sends the headers, and elsewhere its service worker adds them.

**Limitations:** Browsers that can't isolate the page should use the plain build.

versions.title: Smooth block lighting
versions.notes:
- Torchlight now spreads through the world block by block and fades with distance, baked into the ground and walls, glowing warm at night.
- It crosses chunk borders and stops at solid walls. Fewer point lights, so big bases stay smooth.

versions.title: More sound
versions.notes:
- Ash storms patter with grit like rain, muffled under a roof, with gusts of wind.
- Distant groans carry at night.
- Footsteps ring on metal, as well as wood, stone, and soft ground.

versions.title: Guided start and photo mode
versions.notes:
- A new world's first steps are starter quests with small rewards: gather wood, make a workbench, light a torch, reach Ashford.
- Photo mode (F2): hide the HUD and your hand, fly a free camera, and set the time of day.

versions.title: Controls and readability
versions.notes:
- Rebind keys in Settings > Controls and readability, and play with a controller.
- A text and HUD size setting and a high-contrast HUD.
- Spawn marks show shapes as well as colors: an X for any hour, a ring for night.

versions.title: A shared map table
versions.notes:
- Share maps at a map table: add what you've mapped and copy what friends added.
- Pick each kind on its own (explored ground, markers, shelters, cities, landmarks), so you only take the waypoints you want.

**Limitations:** In co-op, maps no longer fill in automatically; use a map table.

versions.title: Landmarks and scout mode
versions.notes:
- Cities, craters, and big ruins join your map once you've actually seen them: on your screen, with nothing in the way.
- Radio towers and billboards to climb. From up high, press V to scout: question marks over the places around you; aim at one to survey it onto your map.

**Limitations:** Radio towers and billboards appear only in ground your world hasn't generated yet.

versions.title: New biomes
versions.notes:
- Flooded swamps with towns on stilts.
- Red rock canyons with cliff ruins.
- The frozen north, where whole cities lie buried in snow.
- Each has its own blocks (mud, red rock, red sand, adobe, ice) and its own finds in crates.

**Limitations:** The new biomes appear only in ground your world hasn't generated yet.

versions.title: Places worth a detour
versions.notes:
- Rare military bases with a locked armory: find the keycard in the barracks.
- Overgrown stadiums with deer on the pitch.
- Old metro tunnels under the highways between cities, with ramps up beside the road.

**Limitations:** New places appear only in ground your world hasn't generated yet.

versions.title: Meals, nearby crates, and a death penalty
versions.notes:
- Meals from several ingredients fill you more and give short buffs: free sprinting, warmth in ash storms, or night vision.
- The crafting window counts what's in crates near you.
- An optional death penalty (Settings, off by default) drops your pack in marked sacks where you fall.

versions.title: Wind and water power
versions.notes:
- Wind turbines make power day and night under open sky, more the higher you build them and in ash storms.
- Water wheels make power while water touches them.

versions.title: Wired controls
versions.notes:
- Switches, levers, and pressure plates on wires turn lamps, doors, turrets, and fences on and off.
- Motion lamps stay dark until something moves nearby.
- An alarm siren warns you when the Ashen come near your base at night.
- Automatic doors open for you and your followers and stay shut for the Ashen.

**Limitations:** Saves from before this version are converted when you load them (item ids moved to make room for more blocks).

versions.title: Gun turrets
versions.notes:
- Gun turrets need no power, only rounds (a scrap and a coal make 8).
- They shoot the nearest Ashen they can see, faster than a bolt turret, and hoppers can keep them loaded.

versions.title: Caravans
versions.notes:
- With two Shelter Beacons on a road, a Carrier follower runs caravans between them every few minutes, even while you're away.
- Food evens out between the two shelters, and crates named Caravan are carried across.

versions.title: Needs and jobs
versions.notes:
- Followers want food in their crate, a bed, and light: well-kept ones work faster and fight harder; unhappy ones slow down and grumble in your journal.
- New jobs: a guard who patrols a ring around their post, a medic who heals hurt followers, and a smith who mends worn tools and armor left in the crate.

versions.title: A growing village
versions.notes:
- Builder followers put up small houses from planks and bricks in their crate.
- They build only inside zones you mark with build markers, on flat open ground, clear of anything you built and of keep-clear markers.
- Hold a build marker and right-click a follower's house to move it or take it down.
- Each finished house takes in two survivors who come looking for a place to stay.

versions.title: Achievements
versions.notes:
- Seventeen achievements, from your first night to the cure, listed in a new Achievements tab in the journal.
- A toast when you earn one, and the day it happened.

versions.title: Hoppers
versions.notes:
- Hoppers move items one at a time from the crate or furnace above them into what their spout faces, with no power.
- Item pipes carry them on to the nearest crate, furnace, grinder, generator, or turret that takes them.
- Right-click a hopper to see where it sends things.

versions.title: Steel and backpacks
versions.notes:
- Steel: an iron ingot and a coal in an electric furnace make a steel ingot.
- Steel tools, armor, and a steel door that brutes can't bash down.
- Cloth and leather backpacks add one or two pack rows. Deer, boars, and horses drop leather.

versions.title: The counter-agent
versions.notes:
- A sealed inner vault under Halcyon Labs, behind a door that opens only when you wire power to it.
- Opening it wakes the First, and the last specimens break out of their tanks.
- Put the First down to take the counter-agent, then carry it to Ashford's mayor's office for the ending. Then keep playing.

**Limitations:** The inner vault appears only if the lab's chamber hasn't been generated in your world yet.

versions.title: Ash craters
versions.notes:
- Three deep ash craters in the deadlands around Halcyon, with a crate at the bottom of each.
- An Ash Colossus sleeps in each one: huge, unburned by the sun, and shown with a boss bar when it wakes. Your journal warns you as you near a crater.
- Put it down and the crate holds its hoard. Cleared craters stay cleared, for co-op friends too.
