**Limitations:** Craters appear only in ground your world hasn't generated yet.

versions.title: Blood moon raids
versions.notes:
- Each blood moon sends a pack at your followers' shelter, marked on your map.
- Raiders that reach the beacon carry off supplies from the crates beside it; lights, shock fences, turrets, and armed followers keep it safe.
- If you're away, the shelter's defenses decide the night. A report goes in your journal at dawn.

versions.title: Ash storms
versions.notes:
- Ash storms two or three times a week: grey skies, thick ash, close fog, and a howling wind.
- You're warned a few game hours ahead, and the status line counts down to the storm and to its end.
- Out under open sky a storm slowly hurts you; any roof keeps you safe.

versions.title: New Ashen and noise
versions.notes:
- New kinds of Ashen as the nights pass: runners (fast, weak, night only), brutes (huge, and they break doors and windows), and screamers (one shriek calls every Ashen nearby).
- The first time each kind is near, it keeps its distance and your journal warns you.
- Noise draws the Ashen: sprinting, breaking blocks, and firing a crossbow.
- Hold C or Ctrl on the ground to sneak: slower, but quiet, and the Ashen notice you at half the distance.
- /spawn takes runner, brute, and screamer.

versions.title: Claimed ground
versions.notes:
- Ground you claim through quests stays safe: no Ashen rise on its open ground at night, even if a light goes out.
- Claimed zones are tinted green on your maps and counted in your stats (and shared in co-op).

**Limitations:** Caves and dark rooms under claimed ground can still spawn the Ashen.

versions.title: Co-op map and chat
versions.notes:
- Co-op chat: type in the console (T) without a slash and everyone sees it.
- Ping a spot for friends: middle-click or Alt-click in the world, or Alt-click the map. A beam with your name shows there and on their maps.
- Everyone's map fills in with ground any of you explore.

versions.title: Co-op polish
versions.notes:
- Co-op friends can use the host's furnaces, electric furnaces, and grinders, and everyone sees what's written on signs.
- Pick a name and color for co-op in Settings; they show over your head and in the pause menu.
- In co-op you go down instead of dying when a friend's around: they have 30 seconds to revive you by holding right-click.
- If the host leaves, you can keep playing your own copy of the world.

versions.title: Co-op creatures
versions.notes:
- In co-op everyone sees the same Ashen and animals, wherever they roam, and can fight them together.
- The kill, its XP, and its drops go to whoever lands the blow.
- The Ashen go after whichever player is nearest, and a friend's Ashen count toward your spawn cap so the swarm doesn't double.
- Followers and farm and zoo animals belong to the host's game; only the host can tame, lead, or recruit them.

**Limitations:** Furnaces and sign text aren't shared yet.

versions.title: Co-op
versions.notes:
- Play together in the browser: Pause > Host Co-op opens your world and copies an invite link; friends click it (or use Join Co-op with the room code).
- Friends play in your world with their own packs: you see each other, build and break together, and share crates, machines, and the time of day.
- Your world saves on your side; theirs doesn't save a copy.

**Limitations:** Only the host sees and fights the Ashen and animals for now (next update). Furnaces and signs aren't shared yet. The host's tab must stay visible, or the game pauses for everyone.

versions.title: Defenses
versions.notes:
- Floodlight: a big electric light that keeps the Ashen from spawning 40 blocks out.
- Shock fence: an electric fence that zaps and throws back any Ashen touching it, and carries power along the line.
- Bolt turret: load it with bolts and power it; it shoots the nearest Ashen it can see.
- The spawn scan's orange tiles now show through walls, so you can see where lights are still needed.

versions.title: Quests
versions.notes:
- Shelter Beacons have a quest board: three new quests a day from the people there, up to three at a time.
- Claim ground: light up a marked patch's open ground (caves don't count). It's outlined on your map.
- Hunt the Ashen, escort a traveler to another shelter or a mayor's hall, or carry a sealed letter there.
- Quests pay XP and supplies. Active ones show under the minimap and in the journal's new Quests tab.

**Limitations:** Claimed ground is a record for now; it doesn't change spawning beyond the light you placed.

versions.title: Gatherers
versions.notes:
- New follower job: Gatherer. They forage around their post into its crate, scrap and cloth near a city, sticks, fiber, berries, and stone in the wild, breaking nothing.
- Gatherers keep foraging while you're away, holding up to 48 items until you're back near their crate.

versions.title: Blood moons
versions.notes:
- Every 7th night is a blood moon: the sky and moon turn red and twice as many Ashen come, twice as fast.
- The journal's Stats page counts down to the next blood moon; Help explains it.

versions.title: World polish
versions.notes:
- Halcyon Labs' tunnel to the mountain now runs secretly underground, from the lab's lowest floor down to the vault.
- Ruined skyscraper tops no longer leave floating blocks; tall shelves stand on the floor.
- Up high you hear wind whistling past instead of waves; the waves stay at the beach.
- The spawn scan (Shift+G) marks dark open ground where the Ashen come out at night in orange; Hide spawn markings in the pause menu clears every mark.
- New setting: texture distance, how far blocks draw in full detail with textures.

**Limitations:** Worlds from before this update get a notice: ruined buildings and the lab tunnel changed shape.

versions.title: Notes in hand
versions.notes:
- Notes are items too: take the page from the chest and right-click it to read it in your journal.
- New worlds show corner hints for Help (H) and your notes (J) until you press each key.
- Torches light the mayor's hall columns and the office beside the mayor's chest; generated torches now give real light.
- The mayor's hall porch is level with the street, so there's no step to hop over at the door.

versions.title: Mayors' notes
versions.notes:
- New blocks: textured white Marble and Gold Trim. Every mayor's hall is rebuilt in them.
- Halcyon's mayor's hall is a grand hall across four lots, eight stories tall under a gilded dome.
- The journal (J) opens on Notes: papers you find in red Mayor's Chests and Halcyon Labs' Lab Chests.
- New worlds start with Ashford on your map and a note to visit its mayor's hall. Its notes point the way to Halcyon.
- Halcyon Labs only appears on your map once you've read Halcyon's mayor's confession.
- City surveys now come from the Mayor's Chest in each mayor's office.

**Limitations:** Older worlds' mayor's halls are rebuilt; walls you changed there may look different.

versions.title: Loading
versions.notes:
- Load World lists your worlds first; choose one to see its saves.
- Load World is in the pause menu too: it saves this world, then loads the save you pick, without the title screen.

versions.title: Fixes
versions.notes:
- Shadows no longer crawl into diagonal lines as the sun moves, and fade out near the horizon.
- A harvester with no chest touching it shows a pulsing red light and says it needs one.
- Lamps show their mode on the base: amber for always on, blue for night only.
- Roads meeting at an angle no longer leave a cliff where they cross.
- Cities you found in older versions are marked where they stand now (Halcyon included).
- Tab backs out of settings; clicking an item name in Help > Commands starts a /give for it.

**Limitations:** Highways near crossings may sit a block or two differently than before.

versions.title: Mountains and skyline
versions.notes:
- The biggest mountain ranges climb to about y 95, with snow above y 58.
- Wide caverns hollow out the insides of mountains.
- Halcyon's great towers now rise 17 to 26 stories, up to 78 blocks; its other skyscrapers reach 12 floors.
- Highways cut through high ground instead of climbing over peaks.
- Textured blocks no longer shimmer on big walls far away.

**Limitations:** Worlds from before this update get a notice: ground you changed on mountains may look different.

versions.title: A taller world
versions.notes:
- The world is now 128 blocks tall instead of 64, so you can build twice as high.
- Older worlds convert automatically when loaded; everything you built stays where it was.
- Clouds float higher, above where the new peaks and towers will reach.

**Limitations:** Terrain and cities still generate as before; the next update uses the new room.

versions.title: Halcyon's skyline
versions.notes:
- Halcyon's city blocks are superblocks, twice as large, with no streets inside.
- Great towers fill most of its downtown: about 35 blocks wide and 13 stories tall, with setbacks, terraces, and an antenna at the sky limit.
- Worlds saved before this update get a notice; Halcyon has been rebuilt.

**Limitations:** The world is 64 blocks tall, so towers stop at the sky limit.

versions.title: Textures
versions.notes:
- New textures for planks, logs, dead logs, grass, gravel, asphalt, car wrecks, rusted metal, and cobblestone.
- Natural blocks keep their slight color variation; blocks you place look uniform.
- Settings > Block textures: Textured, Retro (flat colors), or Custom, block by block.

**Limitations:** Far chunks still draw in flat colors.

versions.title: Map refresh
versions.notes:
- After an update that changes the world, your map shows out-of-date areas hatched in orange.
- They're remapped as you travel near them, or all at once with Refresh whole map on the full map.

versions.title: Quick fixes
versions.notes:
- Windows drop themselves when you break them.
- Solar panels work from 06:00 to 18:00: exactly 300 power a day.
- Right-click an electric lamp to switch it between always on and night only. Help's power numbers now match.
- If a creature you hit dies within 5 seconds (fire, a fall, a follower), you still get the XP.
- The jeep eases up one-block steps instead of popping up them.

versions.title: Farms, zoos, and parks
versions.notes:
- Abandoned farms dot the wilderness: fenced fields of crops, a farmhouse with food, a barn, and sheep in their pen.
- Cities can have zoos, four lots of fenced pens with deer, sheep, boar, and horses, and great parks with a pond, trees, and paths.
- Farm and zoo animals are there when you arrive, and come back if they wander off.

**Limitations:** Farm crops don't grow until you replant them yourself.

versions.title: Halcyon
versions.notes:
- Halcyon, the Metropolis, now stands about 2000 blocks from spawn, beside a mountain, in a wide ring of dead ash country.
- At its heart is Halcyon Labs, the source of the infection: a dark complex across several lots, with basements, specimen tanks, and crates.
- The lab's tunnel runs out of the city into the mountain, to a chamber and a vault deep underground.
- A grand highway, 11 blocks wide with two lanes each way, runs from Ashford all the way to Halcyon.
- This changes how the world generates, so loading an older world warns that Halcyon has moved.

**Limitations:** In worlds saved before v0.5.0, the old Metropolis's ground you changed stays as it was, and its buildings no longer generate.

versions.title: Waypoint management
versions.notes:
- The map's list is now Waypoints: your markers, shelters, and the cities you know, with filters for each kind.
- Shelters and cities can be taken off the maps with a tick box.
- Marker colors use a full color picker, with the presets, your five most recent colors, and colors you pin always a click away.

versions.title: Saves, sound, and city names
versions.notes:
- Save and world names can be as long as you like.
- No more phantom waves: the wind is quiet on the ground, and you only hear waves near open water.
- Cities have names. The starter city is always Ashford and the Metropolis always Halcyon; the rest are named by the seed.
- City names appear on the map, in the debug line, in survey results, and when you walk into a city.

versions.title: The Metropolis
versions.notes:
- Every world now has a Metropolis: one enormous city about 560 blocks from spawn, on the far side from the home city.
- Its downtown is packed with skyscrapers built to the height limit, plus a city hall, hospital, police station, and market. It's a late-game place to clear and resettle.
- Highways reach it, and it's labelled on your maps once you find it.
- This changes how the world generates, so loading an older world warns that the Metropolis now stands there.

**Limitations:** Towers top out at 9 stories, the world's height limit. In older worlds, ground you already changed there keeps your changes.

versions.title: X-ray spawn scan
versions.notes:
- The spawn scan (Shift+G) now also shows, through the walls for 30 seconds, every dark indoor spot within 24 blocks where the Ashen could spawn at any hour.
- It covers every floor of the buildings around you, basements, and caves, so you can tell at a glance whether a skyscraper is safe to settle.

**Limitations:** Open ground that's only dangerous at night isn't shown by the x-ray; press L for that.

versions.title: Connections and scrap
versions.notes:
- Wires connect to every power part beside them in all six directions, so you can see them climb walls and plug into machines. A wire on its own still lies flat.
- Fences connect to other fences and walls, with rails only where they join.
- New machine: the grinder (3 iron ingots, 2 cobblestone, 2 wire). On power it turns iron ingots into scrap, cobblestone into gravel, and gravel into sand.

versions.title: Horses
versions.notes:
- Wild horses roam the meadows. Tame them with wheat or ashberries.
- Craft a saddle (3 cloth, an iron ingot, 2 plant fiber) and right-click a tame horse to saddle it. Right-click it again to ride: W/S, A/D, Space to jump, Shift to get off.
- Horses can be led, tied to fences, penned, and bred like the other animals.
- New console command: /spawn sheep, deer, boar, or horse.

**Limitations:** A horse's coat is picked fresh each time the world loads.

versions.title: Taming and breeding
versions.notes:
- Sheep graze the meadows. Shear them for wool (2 iron ingots make shears); it grows back, and a wool makes 2 cloth.
- Each animal has a favourite food. Hold it and they follow you; feed it to a wild one to tame it.
- Leads (4 plant fiber and a cloth) let you lead any animal. Right-click a fence to tie it there, and fences keep animals penned in.
- Feed two tame animals of the same kind and a baby is born, which grows up over about ten minutes.
- Tame and tied animals stay in the world and are saved with it.

**Limitations:** Fences show rails on every side, even where no fence joins.

versions.title: The jeep
versions.notes:
- A drivable jeep: craft one at a workbench (8 iron ingots, 4 scrap, a battery, 2 cloth) and right-click the ground to park it.
- Right-click it to get in. W drives, S brakes and reverses, A/D steer, and Shift gets out.
- It climbs one-block steps on its own, so it can go off-road over rough ground. It's 30% faster on roads and crawls through water.
- Left-click a jeep to pick it back up. Parked jeeps are saved with the world.

**Limitations:** The jeep needs no fuel, takes no damage, and can't carry followers.

versions.title: City travel
versions.notes:
- Fast travel: place more Shelter Beacons, then right-click one to travel to another. A trip costs a food per 250 blocks, from the crates beside the beacon or your pack.
- Beacons have names and all show on your map. Any beacon can become your followers' shelter.
- Every mayor's hall keeps a City Survey in its vault. Read it to mark the nearest city you haven't found. Cities you walk into are marked too.
- Paved road: 2 asphalt and a concrete make 4 at a workbench. Walking on paved road or asphalt is 30% faster, so the highways are the quick way between cities.

**Limitations:** Followers don't travel with you; send them home to the shelter from the journal.

versions.title: Highways
versions.notes:
- Old highways now link each city to its nearest neighbors: cracked asphalt with a dashed center line that winds across the land.
- Highways cut through hills, cross water on causeways, and stay clear of trees and ruins. They show on your maps, so you can follow one to the next city.
- This changes how the world generates, so loading an older world warns that highways now cross it.

**Limitations:** In worlds saved before v0.3.0, chunks you already changed keep your changes, so a highway may stop at the edge of ground you built on.

versions.title: Glass and textures
versions.notes:
- Windows are see-through glass, with a frame and a few smudges so you know they're there. You can see into buildings now.
- Brick looks like brick: staggered courses with mortar between them.
- Concrete has grain, pits, and water stains instead of a flat color.
- Berry bushes are leafier, with red berries showing.

**Limitations:** Glass is drawn see-through, so very large glass walls can sort oddly against water behind them.

versions.title: Map and quick fixes
versions.notes:
- The full map zooms out to over 6000 blocks across, and you can keep walking while it's open.
- Click a spot on the map to read its coordinates. Teleport (/tp) puts the command in the console for you.
- New console command: /tp x z lands you on the ground there; /tp x y z goes to an exact spot.
- Flying with Shift is much faster (48 blocks a second), for exploring the world.
- The "won't drop anything" warning is now a centered subtitle under the block's name.
- Eating drops crumbs, and the food comes right up to your mouth.

**Limitations:** Fast flight can outrun the world loading on slower machines; the map only fills in where ground has loaded.

versions.title: Armor
versions.notes:
- Wooden and iron armor: a helmet, chestplate, leggings, and boots, crafted at a workbench.
- Wear it in the four armor slots beside your off-hand: right-click a piece in your hand, drop it in its slot, or shift-click it.
- Each armor point takes 4% off hits from creatures. A full wooden set takes 24%, a full iron set 52%. Falls, hunger, and drowning go straight through.
- Every hit wears each piece a little until it breaks: wood lasts 40 hits, iron 120.
- Your armor shows beside the health bar, and saves with the world.

**Limitations:** Armor doesn't show on your character, and followers can't wear it yet.

versions.title: Beds, crossbow, and feel
versions.notes:
- Right-clicking a bed asks what to do: sleep until dawn, set your spawn point here, or both. You can sleep somewhere without moving your spawn.
- With a crossbow in hand, a readout shows your scrap and wooden bolts and which it fires. Q switches.
- A redrawn crossbow icon.
- Aiming at a block your tool can't harvest warns that it won't drop anything, and its cracks glow red as you mine.
- Farmland is tilled into ridges and furrows, so it stands out from dirt.
- Eating raises the food to your mouth.
- The minimap slides smoothly as you walk instead of jumping.

**Limitations:** The bed menu is one more click than before when you just want to sleep.

versions.title: Furnaces and electricity
versions.notes:
- A stone furnace now needs 5 scrap metal for each iron ingot, so mining iron matters again.
- An electric furnace does better: 1 scrap makes an ingot, and 1 iron ore makes 2.
- The electric furnace's window says it's electric and shows whether it has power instead of an empty fuel slot.
- New Electrical tab in Help: solar output per second and per day, power per fuel item, battery size, chargers charging and discharging, what each machine draws, and how to set up a harvester.
- Wires stack straight up: right-clicking a wire while holding a wire (or any block) builds onto it. Use an empty hand to read its network.

**Limitations:** Scrap already smelting in a stone furnace waits until there are 5.

versions.title: Menus, keys, and saves
versions.notes:
- New keys: J opens the Journal and K opens Skills. The touchpad right-click key is now R.
- The Journal pauses the game while it's open. Opening it from the pause menu no longer leaves you without a cursor.
- Tab closes every screen, including the console, sign and marker names, and the crafting search, so you never need Escape (which frees the cursor in a browser).
- Unspent skill points show as a badge beside your level: "3 skill points · K to spend".
- Quitting writes an Exit save instead of overwriting the save you loaded. The pause menu's Save is now Quicksave, with its own slot, and autosaves get their own slot too.
- Days passed are counted, sleep included. They show in the Journal's stats and in the F3 info.

**Limitations:** Worlds saved before v0.2.2 estimate their days passed from time played.

versions.title: Boats
versions.notes:
- Boats: craft one from 5 planks at a workbench and right-click water to set it down.
- Right-click a boat to board it. W/S row, A/D steer, and Shift steps off onto the nearest shore. Boats stop at banks instead of running aground.
- Left-click a boat to pick it back up. Boats you leave on the water are saved with the world.

**Limitations:** Boats don't carry followers or cargo, and they stop at waterfalls and one-block drops rather than going over them.

versions.title: The grand boulevard
versions.notes:
- Every city now has a city hall at its heart: six stories of brick and concrete behind a columned portico, with a domed roof and flag, and the mayor's vault of military crates inside.
- Two wide boulevards, with two lanes each way around a planted median, run past the city hall.
- Fixed skyscraper stairwells leaving a hole from the roof down to the ground.
- Because cities generate differently now, loading a world saved before v0.2.0 shows a warning. Buildings you changed near a city may look different.

**Limitations:** Cities in existing worlds change where the boulevards and city hall now stand.

versions.title: Second hand
versions.notes:
- An off-hand slot (in your inventory; X swaps it with your hand). Carry a torch there to light the way as you walk.
- Shields: put one in your off-hand and hold right-click to block. Hits from in front do nothing and knock the attacker back.
- The scythe harvests and replants every ripe crop around the one you swing at.
- Help pages are laid out in sections with headings and bullet points.

versions.title: Keeping track
versions.notes:
- Manage map markers from the map: a list with coordinates where you can rename them, change their color, hide them from the minimap, or click one to pan to it.
- A journal (F, or from the pause menu): see where each follower is and what they're doing, call them to you, or send them to your shelter for a food item.
- Shelter Beacons set your followers' home: craft one at a workbench and place it at your base. Food in a crate beside it pays for sending followers home.
- A stats page: distance walked, Ashen killed, deaths, blocks mined and placed, followers, days survived, and more.

**Limitations:** Stats start counting from this version.

versions.title: Sorted
versions.notes:
- A cleaner crafting menu: pick a category (Materials, Building, Tools, Combat, Food & Farming, Healing, Light & Power, Utility) or search by name or ingredient.
- Cotton: find seeds in grass and crates, grow it on farmland, and spin 2 cotton into cloth by hand.
- Batteries can be made with charcoal. Help explains how a solar panel, batteries, and lamps keep the lights on at night by themselves.

versions.title: Commands
versions.notes:
- A console: press / or T and type a command. /fly, /morning, /noon, /night, /invincible, /spawn follower or /spawn ashen (optionally at x y z), /xp N, /give item_name N, and /help.
- Help has a new Commands tab listing every command and every item name /give understands.
- While you type in the console (or name a sign, marker, or crate), your keys no longer trigger game shortcuts.

versions.title: Sound returns
versions.notes:
- Fixed the game going silent in the browser after leaving the title screen (broken since v0.1.18). Music and sound effects play again in game.
- Hold Shift to fly faster.
- One coal or charcoal now smelts a full stack of 10 (fuel burns a touch longer).
- Map: drag to pan the full map (Re-center snaps back), sharper pixels when zoomed in, and no more black corners on the minimap.
- You wake at 06:30 after sleeping. Help says how much hunger sleeping costs.
- Tab closes Help even after clicking one of its tabs. Weapon and tool tooltips show how hard they hit.

versions.title: Worth the trip
versions.notes:
- Cities have more to explore: fallen towers (a mound of rubble inside broken walls, with crates caught in the collapse), fenced supply depots with rows of stacked crates and a guard hut, and more police stations downtown.
- More crates everywhere: a second stash on many floors, more rooftop caches, pantry shelves in basements, and kitchen crates in houses. Caches mix in food, medical, and military crates.
- Crates can now hold wire, batteries, buckets, throwing daggers, and plant fiber.

**Limitations:** Some lots in existing worlds change into the new kinds; places you've already built on or dug out can look odd where that happens.

versions.title: Lights on
versions.notes:
- Electric furnace: smelts on power from its network instead of fuel, and only draws power while it has something to smelt.
- Electric lamps: while powered they light up brightly and keep the Ashen from spawning within 28 blocks (more than twice a lantern's reach). Without power they go dark.
- Spawn scan (Shift+G): marks dark ground within 32 blocks where the Ashen could spawn tonight in orange on your minimap and map, so you know where to put lights.

versions.title: Carry water
versions.notes:
- Buckets (3 iron ingots, at a workbench): right-click water to scoop up a block, and right-click again to pour it somewhere else. Bring water to your fields; poured water stays put and never floods.
- The sea never runs dry: scooping from it doesn't leave a hole.

versions.title: Signs of life
versions.notes:
- Signs: craft two from 2 planks and a stick. On the ground a sign faces you; on a wall it hangs facing out. Write up to 60 characters, which show on the board, and right-click a sign to edit it.
- Name your crates: press Name this crate in a crate's window. The name shows in the window and when you look at the crate.

versions.title: Tidying up
versions.notes:
- Time stands still while the Help screen is open.
- Skill balance: damage is now +10% and move speed +5% per rank.
- Day and night change on the hour: night runs from 18:00 to 06:00.
- Fixed boxes showing instead of characters in the browser (next to your level, and in the Help recipe lists).
- You can aim past short crops and other small walk-through blocks at whatever is behind them.
- The Ashen no longer burn while standing in water.
- Fixed crate corners and torch lights flickering as you move.

versions.title: Mark the spot
versions.notes:
- Fixed followers and the Ashen getting stuck in water: they now climb out onto banks like you do.
- Map markers: craft two from a stick and two plant fiber, and place them anywhere. Each one shows on your minimap and map under a name; right-click a marker to rename it. Arrows on the minimap's edge point to markers out of view.

versions.title: Anyone out there?
versions.notes:
- Ping (G): spend a little hunger to mark every survivor still waiting nearby, even in ruins you haven't found, plus the Ashen, on your minimap and map for 25 seconds. Arrows on the minimap's edge point to survivors beyond it. It recharges in 10 seconds.
- A new Scouting skill adds 16 blocks to the ping's reach per rank (64 blocks to start).

versions.title: Farther views
versions.notes:
- Render distance now goes up to 32 chunks (512 blocks).
- Distant terrain is drawn in batches of 4×4 chunks, so big render distances need far fewer draw calls: on the test machine, 32 chunks went from about 37 to about 85 FPS, and 16 chunks got a little faster too.
- The world streamer does less work every frame once everything around you has loaded.

**Limitations:** Loading a 32-chunk view takes a while (about a minute on the test machine, and much longer in the browser, where everything loads on one thread).

versions.title: Where have I been
versions.notes:
- A map of where you've explored: press M for the full map, with zoom, showing your bed, the home city, and your followers.
- A minimap in the top right. A new Minimap setting shows it always or keeps it hidden until you press N, and N shows or hides it any time.
- The map updates as you build and dig, and it saves with the world.

**Limitations:** Places you visited before this version start unexplored.

versions.title: At a glance
versions.notes:
- Crates look like crates: banded chests with iron corners and a brass latch, in their own colors for military, medical, and food crates. They no longer blend in with planks.
- The furnace has a dark, sooty mouth on every side.
- The crosshair label says what right-clicking does, for example Crate · right-click to open or Wooden Door · right-click to close.
- New hand-drawn icons for every item that was still a placeholder circle: coal, charcoal, ingots, meat, berries, potatoes, fiber, bandages, cinders, cans, cloth, scrap, medkits, and bread. Crates, the furnace, and the power machines have icons too.

versions.title: Read the manual
versions.notes:
- A Help screen (H, or Help in the pause menu). It explains healing (you heal only while your hunger is at least 14 of 20), when day and night start, beds and sleeping, how far each light keeps the Ashen away, and what each tool is for.
- Help also lists every crafting recipe with the station it needs, every furnace recipe, and every fuel with how many items it smelts (each item takes 8 seconds of fuel).

versions.title: Orders
versions.notes:
- Follower stances, set from a follower's panel: Aggressive (seeks out nearby Ashen), Defensive (fights only what attacks them or you), or Passive (never fights, and runs from danger when hurt).
- Followers are now Defensive by default. Make one Aggressive for the old behavior of charging any nearby Ashen.

versions.title: Getting stronger
versions.notes:
- Experience and levels: earn experience by killing the Ashen and hunting, mining coal and iron, harvesting ripe crops, and crafting. A bar under the hotbar shows your progress.
- Each level gives a skill point. Press J to spend it on max health, stamina, move speed, or damage (up to rank 10 each).
- Your level and skills save with the world.

versions.title: Which way, and how long
versions.notes:
- A compass in the top left, and the clock now says whether it's day or night and how long until dusk or dawn.
- A pickup feed above the hotbar lists what you just mined or picked up; repeats add up and old entries fade away.
- In the inventory, hover a slot and press 1–9 to swap it with that hotbar slot.
- In the browser, the camera no longer flicks when the mouse capture hiccups: huge spurious jumps (and motion right after capture) are ignored.
- Followers never take fall damage (now checked by a test).

versions.title: Power to the ash
versions.notes:
- Electricity: craft wires, batteries, a fuel-burning generator, solar panels, and a battery charger at a workbench. Power blocks that touch form a network.
- Generators burn fuel from their bin only while the network needs power. Solar panels make power in daylight under open sky. Spare power charges the batteries in your chargers, and the batteries keep things running when it's dark.
- An automated harvester: while powered, it harvests ripe crops within 4 blocks into a crate touching it and replants them.
- Right-click a panel, wire, or harvester to see how its network is doing.

**Limitations:** Wires always look like a cross on the floor, whichever way they connect.

versions.title: Sticks and stones
versions.notes:
- Throwing daggers: whittle 3 from a plank and a stick, and left-click to throw them. Each one drops where it lands; walk over it to pick it back up.
- A boomerang (3 planks and a plant fiber, at a workbench): left-click throws it out, and it curves back to your hand, striking creatures on the way out and back.
- Wooden bolts (2 sticks and a plant fiber make 4) fire from the crossbow when you're out of scrap bolts. They hit softer and wander a little.
- Cloth can be woven from 4 plant fiber at a workbench.

**Limitations:** A boomerang still in the air when you save and quit is lost.

versions.title: Shut the door
versions.notes:
- Doors: craft wooden doors (6 planks make 2) or iron doors (4 iron ingots) at a workbench. They stand two blocks tall, face you when placed, and open and close with right-click.
- Closed doors keep the Ashen out. They can claw through a wooden door in about nine seconds; iron doors hold.
- Separate volume settings for creatures, ambience (the wind), and all other sound effects, alongside the overall and music volume.
- The bed has its own hotbar icon again.

versions.title: Things you can recognize
versions.notes:
- Beds look like beds: a wooden frame and headboard, a mattress, a pillow, and a red blanket.
- A burning furnace glows: its mouth lights up orange and it lights the room. It goes dark when the fuel runs out.
- Coal and iron ore show chunky deposits (black coal, rusty iron nuggets) that stand out from stone.
- Torches placed on a wall lean out from it.
- Felled trees tidy up: leaves no longer held up by a log fall away over a few seconds, sometimes dropping a sapling or a stick.

**Limitations:** Leaves already floating in older saves stay until a nearby log is broken.

versions.title: Pick your save
versions.notes:
- Save As now lists every save of this world, newest first. Overwrite one (press Overwrite, then Confirm) or type a name for a new save.
- Eating takes a short hold: keep right-click (or K) held for about half a second. Let go early and you keep the food.
- Planks, logs, and dead logs burn for 12 seconds, enough for a whole smelt.
- Wild tubers are now potatoes, and roasted tubers baked potatoes.
- Fixed the pause, settings, and death menus sitting off-center.

versions.title: Better swings
versions.notes:
- Your bare arm now swings from the shoulder and stays attached instead of drifting off.
- Tools swing from your grip: the pickaxe chops toward what you're aiming at and strikes point first, axes lead with the blade, and swords slash diagonally.
- New motions: placing blocks, planting, and seeding push forward; the crossbow kicks back when it fires.

versions.title: A song for the ash
versions.notes:
- Music, synthesized in the game like the sound effects: warm pads and a slow pentatonic melody in the wilds, cold drones and ringing bells in the cities, and a low, uneasy theme with a heartbeat at night.
- The music follows you, crossfading as you walk into a city or night falls, and a drum-and-bass combat layer swells in while the Ashen are hunting you.
- Calm music on the title screen. A new Music volume setting; music dips underwater and while you're down.

**Limitations:** Themes render in the background over the first few seconds of play, so music fades in shortly after you arrive.

versions.title: Mark the dark
versions.notes:
- Spawn marks: press L to see where the Ashen could spawn near you. Red tiles mark spots they can use at any hour (caves, dark city interiors), orange tiles dark open ground they take at night. Light a spot and its mark disappears; the marks follow you and update as you build.
- Fixed seeing into the ground through leaves that touch it.

**Limitations:** Marks cover 16 blocks around you, from 12 below to 8 above.

versions.title: The sprawl
versions.notes:
- The home city is now huge, about five times the area, and still a short walk from where you arrive. Wide avenues cross it every fourth street.
- Districts: a downtown of towers up to nine stories with plazas and fountains; residential streets of little houses along gravel alleys, apartment blocks, and parks; and an industrial edge of rusted warehouses and yards of shipping containers.
- Landmarks near downtown: a hospital (wards, a red cross on the roof, medical crates of bandages and medkits), a police station (cells, an armory of military crates, a basement), and a supermarket (shelf aisles and food crates).
- Interiors worth searching: furnished floors with beds, tables, shelves, and kitchens, and basements with crates under many buildings.
- More survivors shelter in the city, and more Ashen roam downtown.

**Limitations:** Worlds saved before v0.1.12 keep their edits, but the home city's new layout replaces the old one around them. Stairs are steep single-block flights.

versions.title: The camp
versions.notes:
- Look after your survivors: right-click one holding a bandage, medkit, or food to heal them.
- Arm them: hand over a sword, axe, or crossbow (they give back what they held), then bolts. Armed survivors hit harder and wear their weapons down; with a crossbow they keep their distance and shoot the Ashen they can see, closing in once the bolts run out. Their bolts don't earn you drops.
- Survivor panel (right-click with an empty hand): health, weapon, and bolts; Follow me, Guard here, a job, or take the weapon back.
- Jobs for guards, within six blocks of their post and a crate: farmers harvest ripe crops into the crate and replant, woodcutters fell trees into it and plant saplings, and cooks keep a furnace stocked with raw food and fuel from it and put the meals back. Jobs run while you're nearby.

**Limitations:** Survivors work only while you're within range of them. Farmers don't till new ground.

versions.title: Rest and roots
versions.notes:
- Sleep: right-click your bed after sunset to sleep until dawn, as long as no Ashen are close. Furnaces finish their work, crops and saplings grow, and you wake a little hungrier and a little healed. Using a bed still sets where you wake.
- Saplings: leaves sometimes drop oak or pine saplings. Plant them on grass or dirt; with light (open sky by day, or a torch) they grow into full trees in about four minutes, if there's room above.
- Export and import saves: Load World has Export on every save (a .ashfall download on web, a save dialog on desktop) and Import a Save… to bring one in as a new save, for backups or moving worlds between machines and browsers.

**Limitations:** Saplings grow only while you play. Dead trees don't drop saplings.

versions.title: Small comforts
versions.notes:
- Fly mode: C (or Ctrl) takes you down, and turning it on shows the controls.
- Sticks look like sticks, in the inventory and in your hand.
- The workbench is a table now, legs, shelf, and a saw and hammer on top, easy to spot from across a field. You still bump into it and use it the same way.
- Jumping no longer costs stamina.
- Separate horizontal and vertical look sensitivity in Settings.
- Sunlight no longer floods caves: surfaces under cover darken with how deep they lie below open sky, so caves and covered rooms are dim and torches matter. Torches and lanterns shine a little brighter to match.

**Limitations:** Cave darkness is baked when a chunk meshes, so opening a hole to the sky brightens the area below once it remeshes.

versions.title: Seeds in the ash
versions.notes:
- Farming: craft a hoe (wood, stone, or iron, at a workbench) and right-click grass or dirt to till farmland.
- Plant wheat seeds (from grass and ruin crates) or a wild tuber on farmland. Crops grow through four stages you can see; break ripe wheat for wheat and seeds, ripe tubers for three or four tubers. Three wheat bake into bread by hand.
- Water within four blocks nearly doubles growth, and light (open sky by day, or a torch or lantern) speeds it further; crops in the dark crawl.
- Crops keep growing on the farm clock while you're elsewhere and catch up when you return; they save with the world.
- The Ashen trample crops and churn farmland back to dirt, so light and fence your fields.

**Limitations:** Crops grow only while you play, not while the game is closed. No fences or scarecrows yet.

versions.title: The dead city
versions.notes:
- Ruined cities: one always lies a short walk from where you arrive (the opening message says which way), and more are scattered across the world. The land levels out into a grid of asphalt streets with painted lines, concrete sidewalks, and wrecked cars.
- City blocks hold ruined buildings up to seven stories, taller toward the center: brick or concrete walls with window bands, broken floors, stairs up through each floor, and jagged, collapsed tops. Crates wait on some floors, and military caches on some roofs. There are also overgrown parks, rubble lots, and parking lots full of wrecks.
- Survivors shelter on the ground floors of some city buildings.
- The Ashen haunt city buildings' shadowed interiors even by day, and more of them roam while you're in a city.
- New blocks: asphalt, road paint, windows (they shatter), and car wrecks (scrap and sometimes cloth).

**Limitations:** Worlds saved before v0.1.7 keep their edits, but cities now appear in their land. Building stairs are steep single-block flights.

versions.title: Playtest fixes
versions.notes:
- Several saves per world: Save and Save As… in the pause menu. Save As starts a new named save (say, "Before the bunker") and leaves the old one as it was; autosave follows the new one. Load World groups saves under their world.
- K does everything right-click does (use, eat, place, recruit), including hold to keep placing, for touchpads.
- Charcoal: smelt logs in a furnace for charcoal, which crafts torches (1 stick + 1 charcoal make 4) and burns as long as coal. Light for the first night without lucky mining.
- Climbing out of water: swim into a ledge with jump held and you haul yourself up, even from the surface.
- Tab opens the pause menu (as do P and Escape); the inventory is on E and I.

**Limitations:** Older saves appear as their world's "Main" save.

versions.title: The world finds its voice
versions.notes:
- Synthesized sound, built in the game with no audio files: footsteps that match the ground (soft earth, hard stone, crunching sand and snow, hollow wood), mining taps and breaking, placing, swings and hits, hurting, eating, splashes, the crossbow's twang, the Ashen's low groans nearby, and wind that rises as you climb.
- Breaking a block bursts it into little cubes of its colors. The view bobs as you walk, and your hand, tool, or block shows in the corner and swings when you mine, strike, place, or shoot.
- Animated water with rolling waves and shimmer; murky teal fog when your head goes under; leaves with a cut-out texture you can glimpse through; blocky clouds drifting high overhead, tinted by the hour.
- Far chunks build with a lighter greedy mesher that merges flat faces, so render distance now reaches 16 chunks (set it in Settings).

**Limitations:** Very long render distances take a while to stream in, especially on web. Far chunks drop ambient occlusion and leaf cut-outs, which the fog mostly hides.

versions.title: Ruins of the old world
versions.notes:
- Ruins rise from the land: collapsed houses, gas stations under rusting canopies, climbable watchtowers, and buried bunkers with concrete stairs. They span chunk borders, cut into hillsides, and keep the trees back.
- Loot crates: ruin crates fill with canned food, cloth, scrap, crossbow bolts, bandages, and more the first time you open them; bunkers' military crates hold medkits, crossbows, iron, and stacks of bolts. Craft your own crates (8 planks) for storage.
- The crossbow: hold left click to fire bolts that arc a little and hit for 9. Craft it from planks, cloth, and an iron ingot; make bolts from sticks and scrap.
- Survivors wait in some houses and gas stations. Right-click one to recruit them; they follow you and fight the Ashen at your side. Right-click again to post them as a guard, and again to bring them along. Ashen go after them too, and the fallen stay fallen.
- New materials: concrete, rusted metal (mine it for scrap, which smelts into iron), cloth (bandages, medkits), canned food, and medkits.

**Limitations:** Worlds saved before v0.1.4 keep their edits, but ruins now appear in their land too. Survivors fight only in melee.

versions.title: Embers kept
versions.notes:
- Title screen over drifting ash: Continue your latest world, start a New World with a name and seed (numbers, words, or blank for random), Load or delete saved worlds, Settings, and the Version Log.
- Named save slots keep the seed, your position and view, health, hunger, stamina, bed, inventory with tool wear, furnace contents, the time of day, and every block you changed. Only edited chunks are stored, as small compressed differences from the generated land.
- Autosave every three minutes, plus saving when you arrive in a new world, on Save & Quit, and when the window closes.
- Settings for render distance (3–10 chunks), mouse sensitivity, field of view, and volume, from the title screen or the pause menu. They apply immediately and are remembered.
- The pause menu gains Settings and Save & Quit to Title.

**Limitations:** Creatures aren't saved; the night resets around you on load. Volume has nothing to control until audio arrives.

versions.title: The Ashen walk
versions.notes:
- The Ashen: infected husks with ember eyes that rise on dark open ground at night and in caves at any hour. They chase you, hop one-block ledges, steer around obstacles, and claw through dirt, leaves, sand, and snow when they get stuck. Sunlight sets exposed Ashen burning and sends them fleeing.
- Melee combat: hold left click on a creature to strike. Damage depends on what you hold, with new wooden, stone, and iron swords hitting hardest. Hits knock creatures back, flash them red, and pop up damage numbers.
- Torches (stick + coal or cinder) and lanterns (iron ingot + torch at a workbench): walk-through light blocks with glowing flames and flickering light. No Ashen spawn within their reach.
- Deer and boar roam meadows and pine hollows by day. Deer bolt when you come close; boar charge back when hurt. Both give raw meat to cook in the furnace.
- Slain Ashen drop cinders: fuel for furnaces and torches.

**Limitations:** Creatures and world edits, torches included, last only for the session. Ashen pathing is greedy, so mazes and long walls can stall them. No sounds yet.

versions.title: Hunger under the ash
versions.notes:
- Health, hunger, stamina, and breath bars. Sprinting and jumping cost stamina, falls past three and a half blocks hurt, and you drown after ten seconds underwater. Starving hurts; staying fed heals.
- Death screen and respawning at your bed (right-click one to claim it) or the world spawn. You keep your pack.
- New items that aren't blocks: sticks, coal, iron ingots, plant fiber, bandages, berries, wild tubers, and raw and cooked meat. Right-click food to eat and bandages to heal.
- Inventory screen (E or Tab): 9 hotbar slots plus a 27-slot pack, with click, drag, half-split, place-one, and shift-click moves, and a recipe list for crafting.
- Wooden, stone, and iron pickaxes, axes, and shovels with mining-speed tiers and durability. Stone needs a pickaxe and iron ore a stone one, or nothing drops.
- Workbench for tools, furnaces, and beds. The furnace smelts iron ore, meat, tubers, cobblestone, and gravel, burning coal, wood, and sticks over time, even while you're away.
- Berry bushes in meadows and pine hollows. Leaves drop sticks and fiber, and grass sometimes turns up a wild tuber.
- Version Log screen in the pause menu.

**Limitations:** No animals yet, so raw meat can't be found until v0.1.2. Furnace contents and beds last only for the session.

versions.title: First light over the ash
versions.notes:
- Endless, seeded voxel world streamed in 16×64×16 chunks on worker threads, with meadows, pine hollows, ashlands, dunes, snowy peaks, shorelines, caves, ores, and three tree types.
- Face-culled meshing with baked ambient occlusion, per-voxel color variation, and translucent sea water.
- First-person walking, sprinting, jumping, swimming, and a debug fly mode.
- Hold-to-mine with per-block hardness, block drops, a 9-slot stacking hotbar, and block placement.
- Ten-minute day/night cycle with dusk-tinted sky, moonlight, matched depth fog, and drifting ash.

**Limitations:** No survival stats, crafting, enemies, or saving yet. Edits persist only while the session runs.

versions.title: Real squishing & order cards
versions.notes:
- The mortar has physics: ingredients tumble into the bowl and roll around. Grab the pestle by its handle and bring it down hard: three good smashes squish an ingredient flat. Sideways pushes just shove things along.
- Order cards: each waiting customer's order hangs on a rail on the wall. Tap one to make it the current order.
- Which Ingredients? spell (3 feathers): jars the current order needs glow.
- Best Ingredients spell (4 feathers): the jar tray lights up the ones that suit the current order.

**Limitations:** Ingredient spells need a current order picked on the rail.

versions.title: Stems & hats
versions.notes:
- Blue roots have a stem at one end: cut it off first (at mark 1), then cut the rest to size. A piece with the stem still on doesn't belong in the brew.
- The ruler now goes to 10.
- Hats: pick the wizard hat or the silly pinwheel hat (it spins) on the title screen.

**Limitations:** Only the blue root has a stem so far.

versions.title: Clock ticks & hardcore heat
versions.notes:
- Cooking time is now in clock ticks: the bigger wall clock has numbers 1–12, the hand moves one number per tick, and the face pulses at each one. The Stomach Ache Potion needs 2 ticks of heat.
- Heat counts by the level the thermometer has reached (4.9 is still 4), and time spent below a recipe's heat doesn't count.
- Hardcore mode (title screen): no thermometers, only flame color.
- Thermometer spell (3 feathers): brings the thermometers back for the day.
- Sweet Spot spell (5 feathers): thermometers mark the heat each brew needs.
- Casting a day-long spell that's already working doesn't use feathers.
- The clock moved next to the cauldrons so the jar tray can't cover it.

**Limitations:** The Blue Potion now cooks for 2 ticks (30 s) instead of 20 s.

versions.title: Feather spells
versions.notes:
- Tap the duck to open the feather mat. Tap spots to lay feathers down; when they make a spell's symbol, it's cast.
- Mistake Sight (3 feathers): notes say what went wrong with a brew. Without it, a mistake only turns the brew murky. On by default while debugging.
- Which Potion? (4 feathers): customers describing a problem narrow it down to two potions.
- The duck has 12 feathers a day; its tail thins as you spend them, and they grow back the next day.

**Limitations:** Losing feathers is only cosmetic for now.

versions.title: Choosing & cutting
versions.notes:
- Each jar holds a mix of its ingredient in different colors, spot counts, and sizes. Tap a jar to tip it out on a tray and pick the right ones.
- Cutting board with a ruler: drop a root on it and tap the ruler to cut at that mark. Bigger roots are longer.
- Recipes can name the color, spots, size, or piece length they need; the Stomach Ache Potion takes any ashberries.
- Mistakes say exactly what was off, like the wrong color or a piece of the wrong length.
- The flask rack moved onto the shelf to make room for the cutting board.

**Limitations:** The Blue and Green potions are still placeholders.

versions.title: What ails you
versions.notes:
- About half of customers describe their problem instead of naming a potion, so you work out which one helps.
- Each recipe page now says what the potion is for.
- The wrong potion for a described problem gets "That won't help with my problem."

**Limitations:** The Blue and Green potions still use placeholder ailments.

versions.title: Juggling & days
versions.notes:
- Two cauldrons, each with its own fire, bellows, and thermometer.
- Up to three customers wait at the window at once. Each slowly loses patience (watch their faces) and leaves if it runs out.
- Handing a real potion to the wrong customer: they say what they wanted instead, and it's thrown out.
- Days: the wall clock runs a 3-minute shift and the sign flips to Closed at the end. You can still serve whoever's waiting; once they're gone, the day ends.
- End-of-day summary: customers served, potions thrown out, and customers who left. Then on to the next day.
- Placeholder Blue Potion (heat between 3 and 6, 2–5 stirs) and Green Potion (very hot, 4+ stirs), with Blue Root and Green Leaf.
- The recipe book now sits on the shelf.

**Limitations:** Days don't carry anything over yet.

versions.title: The stomach ache potion
versions.notes:
- Customers come to the serving window and ask for a potion by name, one at a time.
- Recipe book on the counter: tap it to read how each potion is made.
- Stomach Ache Potion: squish 3 ashberries, put them in the cauldron, keep it at 5/12 heat or more for 30 seconds, stir at least 3 times, and pour it into a flask.
- Ingredient shelf, mortar and pestle (tap the pestle to pound), and a rack of empty flasks.
- Cauldron: pump the bellows to heat it, and it cools slowly. Flame color and the thermometer show the heat. Drag in circles to stir; each stir is counted and the swirl shows your speed. Tap the handle to tip it out.
- Mistakes show right away: the brew turns murky and a note says what went wrong.
- Drop a flask on the customer to hand it over. A wrong one is thrown out and they keep waiting. The bin takes anything.

**Limitations:** One cauldron and one customer at a time; no timers or days yet.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- Title screen with Open the shop and Version Log.
- Shop scene: the duck alchemist in a wizard hat behind the counter, an ingredient shelf, and a cauldron, all smooth 2D placeholders.
- All on-screen text comes from data/text.csv, tagged as AI- or Josh-written. Press F2 to mark AI text with [AI]; tools/audit_text.gd lists it.
- All art loads through data/art.csv. Set a row's path to a file to replace its placeholder.
- Mouse and touch both work. 1280×720 layout that stretches to fit the window.
- Web export to Exports/Potion Maker/v0.1.0.

**Limitations:** No customers or brewing yet; those start in v0.1.1.

versions.title: Camera fix
versions.notes:
**Camera fix (P2, reported by Josh from the web build).**

- **Bug:** randomly, the view flickered and the camera snapped to a different direction while playing the web build. Josh's guess was right: it's the pointer lock. On web, when pointer lock engages or re-engages (initial click, closing a menu, the browser recentering the cursor, focus changes), the browser fires a mouse-motion event whose delta is the recenter jump — potentially hundreds of pixels — and `player.gd` applied `event.relative` to the camera unfiltered.
- **Fix (in `player.gd`):** a pointer-lock spike guard for mouse look — (1) the first motion event after every transition into captured mode is dropped; (2) motion is ignored for 150 ms after capture or window-focus return; (3) any single event with a jump over 400 px on either axis is discarded as an artifact; (4) each event's look step is clamped to 150 px, so genuine fast flicks still register but can never teleport the view. No engine or export changes; the single-threaded preset is unchanged.
- Version bumped to 0.1.3 everywhere (VERSION, GameState.VERSION, HUD corner, in-game changelog); Web export preset now points at `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival/v0.1.3/`.

versions.title: Bugfix + save-slots update
versions.notes:
**Bugfix + save-slots update**, scoped from Josh's first playtest of the web build (2026-10-07 evening):

- **P0 — Ambient drone removed.** v0.1.1's synthesized ambient loop (a constant 55/110/165 Hz tone on the Music bus) is gone — there is no background tone at all now. All short SFX stay. The Music bus and slider remain in Settings, relabelled "reserved for future music".
- **P1 — Restart after death fixed.** The death restart polled `Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_R)` every frame and re-fired `reload_current_scene()` until the scene swapped, on top of a partial hand-reset of GameState. Now: a dedicated `restart` action with a just-pressed edge trigger, a `_restarting` guard, one deferred reload, and a new `GameState.reset_run()` that resets all run state (day 1, 08:00, kills/recruited/trees/crafted = 0). The death panel also has a visible **Restart (R)** button. `player.take_damage` no longer touches the pause flag — the HUD owns pausing.
- **P1 — Menu is Tab or Esc; C is crafting only.** New `menu` action on Tab + Escape; the old Tab crafting binding is deleted. Tab is handled in the HUD's `_input` (before GUI focus navigation, marked handled) because in a browser Esc exits pointer lock — Tab is the reliable menu key on web. Tab does not steal focus while typing a save name.
- **P1 — Melee rebalance (both directions).** Player reach: Fists 2.0→2.8, Bat 2.4→3.2, Spear 3.2→4.0, and zombie hits are measured to the zombie's surface (centre distance − 0.5) instead of its centre. Zombie attack range 1.6→1.25, attack cooldowns 0.9/1.0→1.2 s, and zombies now stop advancing 1.3 from their target instead of shoving into it. Net effect: every melee weapon can hit a zombie from outside its attack range.
- **P1 — Real pause in menus.** Any open panel (pause menu, crafting, help, settings, save, load, console, version log, death) now pauses the whole SceneTree — the world, zombies, survivors, and clock all freeze. The HUD layer runs with `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` so menus stay interactive; saving/loading from a panel closes panels and unpauses first, then runs deferred, so the game resumes into the loaded state.
- **P1 — Named save slots.** The single `user://savegame.json` slot is replaced by named files in `user://saves/<name>.json` (same payload plus a `slot_name` field). Names are sanitised (letters/digits/space/`_`/`-`, max 24 chars, empty rejected with a toast). Pause menu → Save Game (name field + click an existing name to overwrite) and Load Game (every slot listed with its Day and time, Load + Delete per slot). **v0.1.1's single save is not carried over.**
- **P2 — Quicksave slot.** F5 quicksaves and F9 quickloads the slot named `quicksave`; it appears in the Load list like any other slot. (On web, F5 reloads the page — use the pause-menu panels there.)
- **P2 — Renewable farms.** Harvesting now yields 2–3 Food **plus seeds back**: 1 guaranteed seed + a 50% chance of a bonus seed, so a harvest always pays for its own replanting. Survivor farm-work harvesting uses the same yield, and both toasts show "+N Food, +M Seed(s)".
- **P2 — Craftable Farm Plot.** The crafting panel gained a Farm Plot recipe (3 Wood) that crafts and places a plot in front of you, exactly like the Barricade Kit flow (same code path as build mode, so save/load respawn works). Build mode's variant list already included it and is labelled clearly in the help text.
- **P2 — H is now Help (was all-Guard); all-Guard moved to J.** `help_toggle` is bound to F1 **and H**; the global Guard order moved from H to **J** (G = all Follow unchanged).
- **P2 — Command console.** Press \` to open the console (a panel — the game pauses while it's open). Commands: `give <item> [amount]` (wood, scrap, food, medkit, bandage, ammo, seed; weapons bat/spear/pistol/rifle grant ownership; amount 1–999, default 1), `god` (toggle invincibility, also `god on`/`god off`/`invincible`), `help`, `clear`. Unknown commands print the command list.
- **P2 — God mode.** `god` toggles a session-only invincibility flag on the player: `take_damage` (including starvation) is a no-op while it's on, a "🛡 GOD MODE" indicator shows top-left, and it is **never written to save files**.
- **P2 — Version log viewable in-game.** Pause menu → Version Log opens a scrollable panel with the changelog. It renders an embedded `CHANGELOG_TEXT` constant in `hud.gd` — a condensed, synced copy of this file (loose `.md` files are not packed into the `.pck`, so the runtime never reads VERSION_LOG.md).
- Version bumped to 0.1.2 everywhere (VERSION, GameState.VERSION, HUD corner); Web export preset points at `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival/v0.1.2/` and stays single-threaded (`thread_support=false`, see the fix entry below).

versions.title: Small update
versions.notes:
**Small update** (Josh chose v0.1.1 numbering for this one — a small update, not a v0.2.0). The three open TODO features from v0.1.0:

- **Save / load a session (P1):** F5 saves, F9 loads, plus Save/Load buttons in the pause menu; toasts confirm, and loading with no save says so instead of failing. One JSON slot at `user://savegame.json` (with a version field and a corrupt-file guard) capturing: day/time and stats; player position, health/hunger/stamina, current weapon and magazine ammo; inventory (resources + owned weapons); survivors (name, recruited state, order, guard position, HP, position, tint); zombies (position/HP/speed); trees and pre-placed loot containers by spawn index (felled/searched state + respawn timers); farm plots and player barricades (cleared and respawned from the save). Known limits: loot containers dropped by dying zombies have no spawn index, so they are left as-is on load; in the web export, use the pause-menu buttons because F5 reloads the browser page. Orchestration lives in `main.gd` (group `save_manager`); each entity script exposes `get_save_data()` / `apply_save_data()`.
- **Audio settings + sound (P2):** New `default_bus_layout.tres` (Master + Music + SFX buses, wired in `project.godot`). Pause → Settings (Audio) has Master/Music/SFX sliders + per-bus mutes, applied immediately via AudioServer, persisted to `user://settings.cfg`, and loaded/applied at startup from the GameState autoload. Since the game previously had no audio at all, `scripts/sfx.gd` synthesizes everything in code (no audio files): swing, gunshot, hit, zombie-death, pickup, crafting, confirm, and UI-click sounds on the SFX bus, plus a quiet seamless ambient loop on the Music bus.
- **Full help menu (P2):** F1 (or pause → Help) now opens a scrollable help menu replacing the compact side panel: goal, the full controls table, survival mechanics, day/night, scavenging and trees, crafting summary, weapons, building and barricades, farming, survivors and orders (including G/H globals), save/load, and settings. Mouse is freed while it is open; F1, the Close button, or Esc closes it.
- Version bumped to 0.1.1 everywhere (VERSION, GameState.VERSION, HUD corner, welcome toast); Web export preset now points at `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival/v0.1.1/`.

See [README.md](README.md), [PROMPTS.md](PROMPTS.md), and [SPENDING.md](SPENDING.md).

versions.title: Initial release
versions.notes:
**Initial release.**

- Engine: Godot 4.7 (Forward Plus, GDScript)
- 3D open-world procedural city: road grid, sidewalks, 20+ buildings with windows, streetlights, abandoned cars, Central Park
- First-person player: WASD + mouse look, sprint, jump, health / hunger / stamina
- Zombies: wander / chase / attack player, survivors, and barricades; more frequent and stronger spawns at night; day/night cycle with day counter
- Scavenging: loot containers (crates, backpacks, etc.) with random food / scrap / ammo / medkits / bandages / seeds / wood, empty state + respawn
- Trees: chop for wood, shake, fall, stump, respawn
- Inventory: wood, scrap, food, medkits, bandages, ammo, seeds + owned weapons
- Crafting: Wooden Bat, Spear, Pistol, Rifle, Barricade Kit, Medkit, Bandage, Reinforced Barricade
- Weapons: melee swing + ranged hitscan, ammo + reload (R), switching 1–4, view-model with swing/shoot animation
- Barricades: build mode (B, V to cycle variant), ghost preview, HP, zombie damage, repair with wood
- Farming: farm plots (pre-placed garden + placeable), plant with seeds, growth stages, harvest for food
- Survivors: recruit (first free, then 1 food), Follow / Guard / Stay / Work Farm orders (aim + 1–4), global G = all Follow, H = all Guard, name + order + HP above head, survivors fight zombies
- Healing: Q heal self, F heal targeted survivor, X eat food
- HUD: bars, day/time, resources, weapon/ammo, crosshair, interact prompt, toasts, crafting panel, help panel, build indicator, pause + death screen (R restart), version corner "Dead City Survival v0.1.0"
- Tracking files added: VERSION, VERSION_LOG.md, PROMPTS.md, SPENDING.md, TODO.md
- Web export preset added (Web → `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival/v0.1.0/`)
- **Validation (2026-10-07):** Project imported and ran headless in Godot 4.7.2 with no script errors (300 frames), and a real Web export was generated successfully with Godot 4.7.2 + official export templates (index.html / index.js / index.wasm 38 MB / index.pck). Export binaries are recorded in `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival/v0.1.0/README.md`; the .wasm/.pck binaries themselves are not stored in git via Pip's connector (it transfers text; a 38 MB binary is outside that path) — regenerate any time with Project > Export > Web, or commit the generated files with a normal git client.
- **Post-release note (2026-10-07):** the v0.1.0 web export's text files — `index.html` and the two audio worklet `.js` files — were pushed unzipped into `Exports/Games/DeadCitySurvival/v0.1.0/` in the repo at Josh's request. The binaries (`.wasm`, `.pck`, `.png`) and the 308 KB `index.js` are still not in git (connector binary/size limits, see above).

See [README.md](README.md), [PROMPTS.md](PROMPTS.md), and [SPENDING.md](SPENDING.md).
