versions.title: Pollution patch
versions.notes:
"Pollution" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md). This is the run's builder's-choice version, and the final version of the run (v0.1.3–v0.1.8).

- **The choice, and why:** the remaining TODO items were weighed as the run's last slot. Multilayer building (P2) and trains, pipes/fluids, and multi-tile buildings (P3) are all multi-version structural projects — starting one as a single final version would ship it half-proven. **Pollution (P3)** is the one remaining item that is self-contained in a single version, and it was picked because it deepens the system the run just built (v0.1.6 evolution) instead of adding a parallel one, reuses the v0.1.7 statistics surface, gives the factory a real long-term tradeoff (output vs. biter pressure), and is fully harness-testable.
- **Pollution (new GameState state, saved):** working machines emit pollution at per-second rates (`POLLUTION_RATES`: furnace 0.020, boiler 0.015, miner 0.010, assembler 0.008, lab 0.005), counted in `main.simulate`'s per-building loop whenever a machine's `is_working` is set. The current level decays by 0.2% of itself per second (`tick_pollution`), so a small base stays near zero while a large factory's cloud lingers. GameState tracks both the current level and the lifetime emitted total. This implements the TODO P3 wording "pollution that scales biter waves with factory output" through the evolution channel: `pollution_factor()` = 1 + min(level, 100)/50 multiplies the time-based evolution creep (×1 clean, ×2 at 50, ×3 at the cap), and evolution in turn scales biter toughness, wave size, and speed — factory output now literally angers the biters faster. Nest kills and science consumption add their own evolution on top, unchanged.
- **UI:** the HUD top bar shows "Pollution: N" next to Evolution, the v0.1.7 Statistics panel gains "Pollution (current)" and "Pollution emitted (all time)" lines from `stats_text()`, and the Help text documents the system.
- **Save format:** saves gain `pollution` and `pollution_emitted`. v0.1.0–v0.1.7 saves still load (clean sky, nothing emitted).
- **Harness note (two adaptations):** the v0.1.7 checks that asserted the literal version string "0.1.7" (const + HUD label) now assert the durable invariant — the HUD corner label shows whatever `GameState.VERSION` currently is — with the literal asserted per release by that release's own checks (v0.1.8 (a) asserts "0.1.8"). No behavioural checks changed.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **300/300 checks passed** (all 285 v0.1.7 checks plus 15 new: version literal, the pollution factor curve at 0/50/100/500 including the ×3 cap, absorption decay math and its zero floor, machine emission over 3 simulated seconds against the boiler/miner world, the statistics pollution lines, the ~×3 evolution creep at 100 pollution, the top-bar readout, pollution save/load restoration against in-between mutations, and legacy saves without pollution keys loading with a clean sky). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.8/README.md`.

versions.title: Statistics + autosave patch
versions.notes:
"Statistics + autosave" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Statistics (new GameState state, saved):** a `stats` record in `scripts/game_state.gd` tracks `items_produced` (a per-item dict; the total is derived from it, so the two can never disagree), `biters_killed`, `buildings_placed`, `buildings_deconstructed`, `nests_destroyed`, `shots_fired`, and `playtime_seconds` (accumulated in `main.simulate`). Production is counted at the point of production: miner output and hand mining in main, furnace smelts and assembler crafts in their machine ticks, and hand-craft completions inside `GameState.tick_crafting` itself so every driver of the queue counts them exactly once. Placement counting sits in `place_building` behind a `count_stat` flag that save-loading passes as false (restoring a world is not placing), and deconstruction counts only the refunding player paths (hold channel / demolish mode) — biter destruction passes `refund=false` and does not count. Kills are counted at the two kill sites (turret tick, engineer shot), shots at the two firing sites (a shot that finds no target or no ammo does not count). Nest destruction counts in `damage_nest`.
- **Statistics panel:** the pause menu gains a **Statistics** button opening a scrollable panel rendered from `GameState.stats_text()` — headline counters, then the per-item production breakdown (most-produced first, name breaks ties, so the order is deterministic). The Help text documents it.
- **Autosave:** every 300 s of play, main writes the save slot `autosave` (it appears in the pause menu's save list like any named save) and shows a brief "Autosaved." hint via a quiet save path. The autosave timer advances only while no modal is open, so a due autosave is **deferred** to the next quiet moment — it never fires under a menu and is never dropped. Restarting a world resets the timer.
- **Settings:** `user://settings.cfg` gains a `game` section holding `autosave_enabled` (default on), persisted by the same settings holder that keeps the audio keys (`scripts/sfx_player.gd`); loaded at startup, saved on change from the pause menu's **Autosave** checkbox. Settings files written by v0.1.3–v0.1.6 lack the key and default to on.
- **Save format:** saves gain `stats`. v0.1.0–v0.1.6 saves still load (statistics start from zero; `stats_from_dict` also normalizes JSON float round-trips back to ints).
- **Harness note (one adaptation):** the v0.1.6 evolution round-trip check compares against the literal 0.42 pinned earlier in the run, but the new stats sections simulate longer before the round-trip — including a deliberate nest kill (+0.02 evolution) — so the harness now re-pins evolution to 0.42 immediately before saving. The check still verifies that the saved value round-trips exactly.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **285/285 checks passed** (all 239 v0.1.6 checks plus 46 new: stats structure and counters-so-far, hand-craft production counting, placement/deconstruction counters incl. biter destruction NOT counting as deconstruction, playtime accumulation, turret and engineer kill/shot counters, the nest counter, autosave firing on its interval, deferral under an open menu with the timer held, firing at the next quiet moment, the toggle off path, settings persistence of both toggle states, stats panel rendering, stats (de)serialization defaults and float normalization, the playtime m:ss format, stats save/load restoration against in-between mutations, and a legacy save without a stats key loading zeroed). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.7/README.md`.

versions.title: Biter pathfinding + evolution patch
versions.notes:
"Biter pathfinding + evolution" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Biter pathfinding (grid A\*):** biters no longer beeline into whatever building blocks them. Each biter carries a waypoint path computed by `find_biter_path` in `scripts/main.gd` — a deterministic A* over the 56×56 grid where cells holding a `blocks_biters()` building are obstacles (belts, poles, splitters, and underground belts are walked over, exactly as before) and the goal cell is always enterable. The biter steers between waypoints; when it gets within attack range of its target (nearest building or the player, unchanged) it attacks as before. Paths are recomputed on spawn, when the ~2 s repath timer expires, and when the next waypoint is blocked by a building placed after the path was computed — staggered to at most **4 recomputes per tick** so a full wave cannot hitch the game; a biter that misses its recompute keeps its old path or the straight-line behaviour for that tick. **No path -> fallback:** when A* finds no route (e.g. the target is sealed inside a complete wall ring), the biter uses the original straight-line movement and chews the blocking building, so a perfect ring is a delay, not an exploit.
- **Evolution (new GameState state, 0..1, saved):** grows **+0.0002/s** with elapsed time, **+0.02** per nest destroyed (in `damage_nest`), and **+0.001** per science pack consumed by a lab (either colour). The HUD top bar shows **"Evolution: NN%"**. Effects: newly spawned biters get toughness ×(1 + evolution) in `spawn_biter` (HP, damage, and base speed scale via the existing toughness formula), `wave_size` adds `floor(evolution × 4)` on top of the base curve (up to +4), and biter movement speed scales ×(1 + 0.2 × evolution) at move time. Evolution never decreases.
- **Harness note:** the v0.1.4 underground pair at (20,10)/(23,10) sits ~9 tiles from a nest, and with the longer v0.1.5/v0.1.6 sections an ambient biter could chew through an end (80 HP) before the save round-trip — the harness now clears biters and re-places a missing end (placement re-pairs it) before saving, and asserts the pair is intact. Gameplay behaviour is unaffected; this is test housekeeping for a pre-existing exposure that the added sections happened to trip.
- **Save format:** saves gain `evolution`. v0.1.0–v0.1.5 saves still load (evolution defaults to 0).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **239/239 checks passed** (all 222 v0.1.5 checks plus 17 new: biter paths to and attacks its target building with pathing active, A* routes through a wall column's gap cell and never steps on a wall, the goal cell is enterable even when it holds a building, a fully sealed goal yields no path, spawned-biter HP scales ×1.5 at 50% evolution, wave size gains +2 at 50%, a nest kill adds exactly +0.02, a consumed science pack adds +0.001 while completing Logistics, evolution creeps with time, the top bar renders "Evolution: 42%", the underground-pair save-prep guard, and save/load preserving evolution). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.6/README.md`.

versions.title: Green science + tier-2 research + steel patch
versions.notes:
"Green science + tier-2 research + steel" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Research costs are per-pack-type now:** `TECHS` costs changed from a single red-science count to a dict keyed by science item (`{"red_science": n, "green_science": m}`). Tier-1 techs (Automation, Military, Logistics, Power Efficiency, Reinforced Walls) cost red science only, with their numbers unchanged. GameState tracks two progress counters (`research_progress` for red, new `research_progress_green` for green); switching tech resets both. `tech_state` now supports multiple prerequisites (a tech's `prereq` may be an array of tech ids).
- **Green Science Pack (new item):** hand recipe in the Science tab — 1 inserter + 1 conveyor belt, no tech gate, 2.5 s — and the same recipe in assemblers. Assemblers accept building items as recipe inputs (the assembler's `can_accept` already keyed off the recipe's input table; the piercing recipe is additionally gated in the assembler tick so a research-locked recipe idles even if set). Labs accept and buffer both pack types (20 each); each lab consumes whichever pack type the active research still needs (red preferred when both are needed). The research panel shows both costs and per-type progress ("Red 20/20, Green 5/10"), the HUD top bar and lab panel use the same per-type text, and the lab panel gained Insert Green Science +1/+5 buttons. The old harness check that read Military's cost as an int was adapted to the dict form.
- **Steel Processing (new tier-2 tech; prereq Automation; 20 red + 10 green):** furnaces gain a second smelt — **5 iron plates -> 1 steel plate, 8 s, 1 coal** (the classic 1-coal-per-smelt rule). A shared `furnace_job` helper in `scripts/main.gd` picks the running smelt (steel wins when researched and 5+ plates are buffered, otherwise the first classic ore smelt), and drives the furnace tick, the status text (including "collecting iron plates for steel: N/5"), and the panel progress bar (which now follows the running smelt's duration instead of a fixed 1.6 s). Furnaces accept iron plates as feed only once the tech is researched; the furnace panel gains Feed Iron Plates +5/+10 buttons then.
- **Piercing Ammo (new tier-2 tech; prereqs Military + Steel Processing; 30 red + 20 green):** unlocks the **Piercing Rounds Magazine** (hand + assembler: 1 steel plate + 2 iron plates, 2.0 s; 1 magazine = 10 rounds). Turrets buffer both magazine types and load **piercing first** when dry (24 damage per shot vs 12 regular); the engineer's gun does the same (60 vs 34). Each turret remembers which type its loaded rounds came from (`ammo_type`, shown in its panel with damage and range), and the player HUD shows "(piercing)" next to the loaded rounds. Turret/piercing state is saved.
- **Fast Logistics (new tier-2 tech; prereq Logistics; 20 red + 20 green):** `belt_speed_mult()` returns 1.5 with the tech (Logistics alone stays 1.25), so belts, splitters, underground transit, and inserters all speed up together.
- **Reinforced Turrets (new tier-2 tech; prereq Military; 25 red + 15 green):** turret max HP 250 -> 375 and range 7.5 -> 8.5 (both read from GameState helpers). On completion, already-placed turrets are upgraded and repaired to full, exactly like Reinforced Walls handles walls; new turrets are placed reinforced.
- **Save format:** saves gain `research_progress_green`, `player_ammo_type`, and a per-building `ammo_type`. v0.1.0–v0.1.4 saves still load (green progress defaults to 0; magazine types default to regular).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **222/222 checks passed** (all 176 v0.1.4 checks — one adapted to dict research costs — plus 46 new: recipe/tech-cost data and gates incl. the dual prerequisite, belt-speed stacking x1.0/1.25/1.5, green science hand-craft and assembler production from building items, assembler rejection of non-input items and its piercing gate, lab dual-pack completion of Steel Processing with both counters resetting, the furnace plate gate and the 5-plates + 1-coal -> steel smelt, Piercing Ammo completing on both pack types, piercing hand-craft and assembler production after research, turret piercing-first loading with the regular magazine untouched, piercing player damage (60) and loaded-type memory, Reinforced Turrets upgrading an existing turret to 375/full with range 8.5 and new turrets placed at 375, and save/load preserving the player/turret magazine types and tier-2 research). versions.title: Splitters + underground belts patch
versions.notes:
"Splitters + underground belts" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Splitter (new building):** hand recipe in the Buildings crafting tab — 4 iron plates + 2 iron gears, no tech gate, 1.5 s craft time. It reuses the belt's one-item buffer mechanics (`belt_item` in `scripts/building.gd`), so belts, inserters, and miner eject all feed it with no special cases, and inserters can take its buffered item back out (belts, splitters, and underground ends are one "belt-like" family for inserter source/target rules in `scripts/main.gd`). Its tick advances the item at belt speed, then delivers **round-robin — front, then left, then right relative to facing**: each delivery tries outputs starting at the round-robin pointer, the first building that can accept takes the item, and the pointer advances past it; if all three outputs are blocked the item is held. Passive — **0 power draw**, like belts. Visual: a belt-style flat base in a distinct green with raised side blocks and the travelling plate/item meshes; no working lamp (documented as not required for a passive building). The building panel shows the buffered item and the last output used.
- **Underground belt (new building, one item type for both ends):** hand recipe in Buildings — 5 iron plates + 2 iron gears, no tech gate, 2.0 s. **Pairing model (the documented simplification):** each end has a role, entrance or exit. Placing an end that lies in the front line (straight row/column, same facing) of an unpaired entrance within **4 tiles** makes it that entrance's **exit** and links the pair both ways; otherwise the new end is an **entrance**, and if an unpaired exit already sits in its own front line within 4 tiles they pair up (orphaned exits can be re-paired). An already-paired entrance is never stolen. **Flow:** the entrance accepts items like a belt; on its tick, with a linked exit and nothing in transit, the item goes underground and surfaces on the exit after **distance ÷ (1.4 × belt-speed multiplier)** seconds; the exit then outputs forwards exactly like a belt (it is part of the belt tick). If the exit is occupied when a transit completes, the item waits inside — **queue of 1 in transit per entrance** (the entrance may buffer one further item meanwhile). Deconstructing either end unlinks the pair (the survivor keeps its role, unpaired) and refunds 1 item per end as normal, plus any in-transit item. The role is shown by a marker post on the building (orange = entrance, cyan = exit) and in the building panel (role, linked cell or "unpaired", item in transit). While the underground ghost is up, a pairable hover cell shows **"Will link to underground entrance/exit (N tiles)"** in the hover readout and the ghost's secondary marker highlights the partner cell. Single placement only — drag-place stays belts/walls only (these types are excluded from the drag list, so dragging with one selected is a no-op, not a crash).
- **Both buildings:** normal `can_place` validation, rotation with R (both are directional), minimap/big-map colours (splitter green, underground belt purple), inventory-menu placement (they are not added to the number-key hotbar), building-panel support, hover readout ("Splitter - Working", "Underground Belt - Unpaired entrance (no exit)", and so on via the shared status derivation), deconstruct refunds of the building plus its buffered item, and no power draw. Biters walk past them like belts (they do not block).
- **Save format:** building records gain optional splitter fields (round-robin pointer, last output) and underground fields (role, partner cell, in-transit item and remaining time). Links are rebuilt on load and validated for mutuality, so a one-way link cannot survive a load. v0.1.0–v0.1.3 saves still load (new fields default cleanly).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **176/176 checks passed** (all 138 v0.1.3 checks unmodified, plus 38 new checks: both recipes exist in Buildings with no tech gate; splitter round-robin distribution over front/left/right acceptors including the wrap-around 4th item, hold-when-blocked, and inserter extraction; underground pairing in line within 4 tiles, no pairing at 5 tiles, transit delivery through the exit onto a belt into a chest, deconstruct-the-exit unpairs the entrance with refund, re-pairing with a fresh exit; hand-craft enqueue of both buildings; and a save/load round-trip preserving the splitter buffer and the pair's roles and links). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.4/README.md`.

versions.title: Audio + build QoL patch
versions.notes:
"Audio + build QoL" patch, shipped under Josh's self-directed iteration mandate of 2026-10-10 (see PROMPTS.md):

- **Procedural event SFX (new `scripts/sfx_player.gd`, no new autoload):** main creates an `SfxPlayer` node in code — a pool of 8 AudioStreamPlayers playing AudioStreamWAV streams synthesized in code (16-bit PCM sine/square/noise bursts with envelopes, different pitch and shape per event). Events wired at their real call sites: place building, deconstruct complete (hold channel and X demolish), craft queue item finished (main now consumes the completed-output list returned by `GameState.tick_crafting`), player and turret shooting, biter hit, biter killed, research complete, wave incoming warning, victory sting, UI click (every HUD button, via the shared button factory), and error buzz (no inventory to place, miner off-patch / occupied placement, unaffordable craft queue, failed building feed, out of ammo). HARD RULE kept: event sounds only — there is no ambient or background loop of any kind (a constant ambient drone was a P0 player complaint in a sibling game).
- **Audio settings in the pause menu:** a Master volume slider (0-100, driving the SFX pool's volume and the Master bus) and a Mute checkbox. Both persist in `user://settings.cfg` (ConfigFile, section "audio"), loaded at startup and saved on change — they are NOT stored in game saves.
- **Drag-place belts and walls:** with a belt or wall ghost selected, holding left-click and moving across cells places a continuous line — each newly entered cell (plus any cells skipped between frames, interpolated along the dominant axis) that passes `can_place` and where the player still has the item is placed, consuming 1 item each. Belt facing follows the drag direction (dominant axis of the movement into the cell; last movement direction wins). The place sound is throttled to at most one per 0.06 s. A simple click still places exactly one; drag-place inherits placement's existing precedence over the deconstruct/hand-mine/shoot channels and stops cleanly when inventory runs out or the button is released.
- **Hover readout:** a dedicated HUD label above the hotbar (separate from the hint line, so transient hints are never overwritten) updated from `_update_hover`. A resource patch cell reads "<Resource> patch" (for example "Iron Ore patch"), a building cell reads "<Building Name> - <status>" reusing `building_status` (the same derivation as the building panel), and empty cells are blank — the chosen option, so the line stays out of the way on bare ground.
- **Save compatibility:** no save-format changes; v0.1.0-v0.1.2 saves still load. Audio settings live outside saves.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import (exit 0, 0 errors), 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **138/138 checks passed** (all 114 v0.1.2 checks unmodified, plus 24 new checks: sfx player exists, all 11 named events resolve to generated AudioStreamWAV streams with length > 0, muted playback is a no-error no-op, settings round-trip at volume 0.4 + muted true, hover text for patch/furnace/empty cells, and drag-place over a 4-cell run with facing, inventory, out-of-items, and occupied-cell cases). Single-threaded Web export — see `Exports/Games/BeltAndSteam/v0.1.3/README.md`.

versions.title: Second playtest batch
versions.notes:
Second playtest batch (twelve items from Josh's playtest of the v0.1.1 web build):

- **Hold-to-deconstruct:** with nothing selected, holding left-click on a building channels a 0.8 s deconstruction — an overhead progress bar (dark backing, orange fill, facing the camera) shows the hold; releasing, moving to another cell, selecting a ghost, or opening a panel cancels with no effect. Completion refunds the building item, any belt item, and all buffer contents (the existing `remove_building` refund). X demolish mode remains as the instant alternative. Left-click precedence is now: place > repair > deconstruct > hand-mine > shoot — clicks on buildings/patches no longer fire shots.
- **Hand mining:** holding left-click on a bare resource patch channels 0.7 s per item of that patch's resource. Patches are infinite, as they already were for miners.
- **Crafting queue (replaces instant crafting):** hand recipes have craft times; clicking a recipe consumes the cost up front and queues it (FIFO — only the front item progresses, leftover tick time carries over). The crafting panel lists the queue with a live percentage on the front row; clicking any queued row cancels it and refunds the full cost, including the in-progress item. A compact queue strip above the hotbar shows the front item and how many are queued. The queue is written into saves.
- **Inventory menu (E):** lists everything carried; building stacks are buttons that select that building for placement (click again to deselect), materials are shown with counts, research-locked buildings say what they need, and the Repair Pack row toggles repair mode.
- **Building interaction panel (E or right-click on a building):** name and cell, HP bar, a live status line derived from the building's real state (Working / Idle / No power / No fuel / Output blocked / No recipe / missing inputs), all buffer contents, machine progress for furnaces and assemblers, the current research for labs, loaded shots for turrets, and — for assemblers — the recipe picker, which now lives in this panel. Non-pausing; refreshes live.
- **Manual fueling / quick-insert:** the building panel carries Feed Coal +1/+5 for boilers and furnaces (the boiler case was the request — it is how you bootstrap power before any inserter exists), Load Ammo +1/+5 for turrets, and Insert Red Science +1/+5 for labs, all respecting the buildings' normal buffer caps.
- **Working indicator:** machines get a status lamp — green while working (state tracked from the actual simulation ticks), red when blocked (unpowered powered-machine, or a boiler without coal), grey when idle. Animated cues: the miner drill rotates while mining, and the furnace flame's emission flickers while smelting.
- **Health bars for everything:** one shared overhead bar component (visible only while damaged, fill colour runs green to red) attached to every building, every biter, every nest (which keeps its text label too), and the engineer (the HUD HP readout also remains).
- **Repair packs:** new hand-crafted item (2 iron plates + 2 copper cable, Intermediates). Selecting it in the inventory enters repair mode; holding left-click on a damaged building repairs at 40 HP/s, one pack restoring up to 100 HP with fractional credit kept across buildings. Clamps at max HP (Reinforced Walls respected for walls); a healthy building reports "already at full health" and consumes nothing.
- **Starting kit:** 10 power poles at game start (was 8).
- **Scrollable menus:** crafting and research lists, help, version log, the save-slot list, the recipe list, and the new inventory and building panels all scroll inside their fixed-size panels.
- **No more tofu-box symbols:** every pictograph/emoji was removed from the game's UI strings (the web export's font cannot draw them, so they showed as boxes with numbers). The HUD now uses plain words — "Power:", "Research:", "Nests:", "Time:", "HP:", "[locked]", "> " selection markers, "->" arrows.
- **Save compatibility:** v0.1.1 and v0.1.0 saves still load (craft queue defaults empty; building HP was already serialized in v0.1.0 and still is).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: clean import, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness **114/114 checks passed** (all 60 v0.1.1 checks, with the instant-crafting ones rewritten against the queue, plus 54 new checks for this batch). versions.title: Playtest-fix patch
versions.notes:
Playtest-fix patch (from Josh's first playtest of the web build):

- **Ammo economy fixed (headline):** ammo magazines are no longer gated behind Military research — the hand-craft recipe (C → Military) and the assembler recipe both cost **2 iron plates** (down from 4) with **no tech requirement**. Military research now unlocks the Gun Turret only (tech text updated; the assembler recipe picker no longer locks ammo). The engineer's gun now fires **rounds**: 1 magazine = 10 rounds, and a magazine is only consumed when the gun runs dry — the same per-magazine yield turrets already had (was: a whole magazine per player shot, so the starting 6 magazines were 6 shots; now 60). Loaded rounds are shown in the HUD inventory panel and persist in saves.
- **Wave pacing:** first wave now arrives at **5 minutes** (was 90 s), later waves every **2 minutes** (was 90 s). Wave sizes are gradual — 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4… capped at 10 (was 3, 4, 5…) — and biter toughness scales more gently (+5% per wave, was +15%). Nest ambient spawns slowed: first spawn at 60 s, then every **40 s** (was 18 s), and only while fewer than 8 biters are alive in total (the old cap counted all biters against a 24 limit).
- **Belt items clearly visible:** the item cube on a belt is now 0.52×0.30×0.52 (was 0.34×0.22×0.34), sits on a thin dark base plate that travels with it, and its material uses **emission** in the item's colour so items pop at normal camera distances.
- **Placement preview with direction/flow:** the placement ghost is now a small rig — footprint box (green/red validity as before) plus a bright yellow-white **direction arrow** for directional buildings (belt, inserter, miner, assembler, furnace, turret), a translucent cyan **destination marker** on the front/output cell, and — for inserters — a fainter marker on the back/pickup cell. Arrow and markers track the hover cell and rotate when you press R. The pole coverage ring is unchanged.
- **Save compatibility:** v0.1.0 saves still load — `player_rounds` defaults to 0 and `wave_timer` defaults to the wave interval when the fields are absent; both are written by v0.1.1 saves.

versions.title: Region perks you pick

versions.title: The Blight moves on
versions.notes:
- Blight nests don't like green land. When 6 in 10 land tiles around a wild nest (a 25-tile square) are green, it gets restless: it stops attacking, and 3 days later it leaves.
- It heads for the nearest smog wreck at least 40 tiles from your buildings and settles beside it, or leaves the valley if there's no such wreck.
- A nest's hover shows how green its land is and when it leaves; the forecast shows the day it goes, and the map draws a dashed path to where it's heading.
- A card explains it once any nest's land is 4 in 10 green, before anything moves, and warns that a far wreck near a future outpost could end up with a nest beside it.

**Limitations:** Combat worlds only. Tame and Bloom Nests stay put (taming a restless nest calls off its move). The land is checked once a minute.

versions.title: Packed lunch
versions.notes:
- Packed lunch: put a dish on the hotbar and right-click it to eat one for a boost. Shift-right-click now empties a dish's slot.
- Oven-baked dishes (bread, cake, pizza...) make you salvage 1.5× faster; fruit dishes (apple pie, tarts, jam, juice...) walk 1.25× faster; soups and stews craft 1.5× faster; anything else, walk a little faster.
- A boost lasts 2 minutes, 3 for Fine dishes and 4 for Excellent ones. One at a time: a new lunch replaces the last.
- A badge under the clock shows the boost and the time left, and the hotbar tooltip says what each dish would give.

**Limitations:** Ingredients (flour, dough, sauce, sugar...) can't be eaten. Time asleep counts, so a lunch is gone by morning. Walking and salvaging boosts are your own; in co-op with a shared backpack the craft queue takes the best craft boost anyone has.

versions.title: Bee swarms
versions.notes:
- Once each spring, on a day of their own, a busy hive (6 or more flowers around it and 10 honey in it) swarms. It's a friendly event: the hive it leaves keeps going.
- If an empty hive (one that hasn't made any honey yet) stands within 12 tiles, the swarm moves in and you get a full colony with 10 honey for free.
- Otherwise it settles in the nearest grown tree within 20 tiles as a wild colony: a golden comb in the branches that pollinates beds within 3 tiles, as long as the tree stands (up to 10 wild colonies).
- Wild bees join the Wildlife page. A card explains swarms the first spring you own a hive, and hive and tree hovers say what's going on.

**Limitations:** A hive swarms at most once a year. Without seasons a swarm day comes every 16 days. Wild colonies don't make honey you can collect.

versions.title: Solar over beds
versions.notes:
- New: the Solar Frame (1 Solar Panel and 4 planks, comes with Solar research). Put it up over a Garden Bed from the bed's window, or hold one and click the bed.
- A frame makes 80% of a Solar Panel's power when a power pole reaches the bed, and the bed keeps growing underneath.
- Its shade helps on dry days: a thirsty bed under a frame grows at 3/4 speed instead of half, like a bed sheltered by a hedge (the two don't add up).
- Taking the bed up gives the frame back. The bed's hover and the power network's window count frames.

**Limitations:** Hail doesn't crack frames. Blueprints copy the bed but not its frame. A watered bed gets the power but doesn't need the shade.

versions.title: Dirty water
versions.notes:
- Smog over a lake now dirties the water drawn from it. When the smog over a pump's water (or a ditch's lake) passes 10, the beds that water reaches grow slower, up to 30% slower in thick smog. Clean water from anywhere else (another sprinkler, a rain barrel) wins.
- A card explains it as soon as the smog over water you use reaches 5, before anything slows.
- New: the Sand Filter (2 glass, 4 sandy soil, 2 pipes). Build it into a pipe line like a pipe and it cleans the water for everything on that line. Reed Beds on the shore still clean the lake itself.
- A pump's hover shows how clean its water is, beds watered with dirty water say how much slower they are, and an alert marks pumps drawing dirty water.

**Limitations:** Ditches can't be filtered; clean their lake instead. Only pumps and ditches are affected: rain barrels and rain are always clean.

versions.title: Fertigation
versions.notes:
- New: the Mixing Tank (research, $300, after Sprinklers). Put it on a water line, touching the pipes, and fill it with Fertilizer or Manure (20 at most, by hand or inserter).
- Every Sprinkler on that line then fertilizes the beds it waters as well: they grow at full speed whatever the soil, without using up the beds' own fertilizer.
- The tank uses one feed for every 200 water its sprinklers spray. Its window and hover say how many sprinklers it's feeding; sprinkler and bed hovers say when they're fertigated.

**Limitations:** Ditches don't carry it, only pipes. One fed tank is enough for a whole line; with more than one, the first with feed supplies it and the others wait their turn.

versions.title: Green roofs
versions.notes:
- Green roofs: open any machine 2×2 or bigger and add a green roof for a sapling and a bag of soil. A sod roof grows on top over 2 days.
- A grown roof soaks smog (more on bigger buildings) and greens the land under the building, which counts toward the greening bonus, regions and the valley's climate.
- Hovering a roofed building shows how its roof is coming along.

**Limitations:** Not on the farmhouse, cottages, the Seed Vault, greenhouses, solar panels, the museum or the lodge. The roof is lost if the building is taken down, and blueprints don't copy it.

versions.title: Wind carries smog, smog preview
versions.notes:
- In worlds with weather, each day the wind blows one way (about one day in five is calm). Smog drifts faster downwind and slower upwind, so it piles up on the downwind side of a burner or furnace. No smog is added or lost, it only moves.
- The forecast and the top-left status say the wind in words, for example "a breeze from the west". Chimney smoke leans with it.
- A card explains wind the first time you hold or own a building that makes smog, before any of your smog has drifted.
- Smog preview: hold a smog maker and a red square shows where its smog will mostly settle today, leaning downwind, with red marks on the beds, trees and green land inside. The tooltip counts them.

**Limitations:** The preview square is a guide (8 tiles round the building, shifted up to 5 tiles downwind), not an exact smog map; the Smog map layer shows the real thing. Worlds without weather have no wind.

versions.title: Ripe timers and belt lanes in the hover
versions.notes:
- Alt view shows "1:20" over growing beds (time until ripe at today's speed), "ripe" over ripe ones, and "fruit in 6 h" over grown fruit trees.
- Hovering a bed says when it'll be ripe; a fruit tree says when it bears next; a Farm Tower says when its next harvest is due.
- Hovering a belt shows each lane: how full it is, what's on it, and whether it's moving or backed up (and for how long).
- Alt view marks belts in red ("stuck") when a lane hasn't moved for 30 seconds, so the jam in a long line is easy to find.

**Limitations:** Ripe times assume today's weather, soil and smog stay the same. Belt rates per minute still need a wired condition (as before).

versions.title: Camp tent
versions.notes:
- New: the Camp Tent (8 planks, no research), a 2×2 tent you can put up anywhere. Sleep in it with Z or its Sleep here button, so long trips no longer end with a walk home at dusk.
- It has a 4-stack chest for your things (inserters can use it too).
- One tent each: put up another and the old one comes down, with its things moved into the new one and the tent back in your backpack. In co-op you can only sleep in your own.

**Limitations:** Bugs can bite a tent like any building. If the blight knocks you out you still wake at the farmhouse.

versions.title: Plan before you can afford it
versions.notes:
- Hold Shift while placing (click or drag) to lay down a ghost of the building in your hand, even if you don't have one yet. Anything you've unlocked can be planned; drag a line of belts or a row of beds the same way.
- A "Still to build" list (top right, under pinned recipes) adds up the planned buildings you're short of and what's missing to craft them. Its Craft button crafts what you're short of, parts first, the same as clicking the recipe.
- Click a ghost with an empty hand to build it once you have the building, as before. Settings can hide the list.

**Limitations:** Ghosts laid by a Shift-drag don't turn the corners of a belt line; turn them with R after building. The list counts the recipe's direct ingredients, not what those are made from.

versions.title: Recent and starred recipes, ratio helper
versions.notes:
- The crafting menu has a Recent & starred row at the top: the last six things you crafted, with any you star first (up to 12). It follows the search box.
- Alt-click a recipe in the crafting menu to star it (a yellow corner), Alt-click again to unstar.
- Ratio helper: machine recipe tooltips and the item lookup say how many machines keep each other busy, for example "1 Prep Table keeps 2 Electric Ovens busy" or "2 Mills keep 1 Prep Table busy".

**Limitations:** Ratios use base recipe times and machine speeds: modules, quality, power shortfalls and burner fuel aren't counted. Recent and starred recipes are kept per browser, not per world.

versions.title: Arrival scene and follow a friend
versions.notes:
- A new world now opens with a 15-second fly-over: the camera drifts from a smog wreck, over the dry riverbed, and settles on your farmhouse with "Bring the valley back". Any key or click skips it, and Settings can switch it off. Tutorials don't have it.
- Co-op: click a friend's farmer with an empty hand, or press Follow by their name in the co-op box, to ride their camera and see what they're building. Any key or click brings you back.

**Limitations:** Following is view only: your farmer stays where you left them, and your own camera comes back when you press a key.

versions.title: Soil life
versions.notes:
- Soil life: every Garden Bed keeps an earthworm count from 0 to 100. Beds left planted gain worms, and mulch and compost add more; empty beds and heavy smog lose them.
- Lively soil grows crops up to 15% faster and greens its tile sooner, so beds you look after get better over time.
- The soil view (G) shows "worms 42" over every bed, and hovering a bed shows its soil life.
- Co-op: a farm copied from the host's snapshot now has exactly the host's greenness, so crops on both sides grow in step (it was rounded before, which could make a rejoined friend's farm drift).

**Limitations:** Soil life is per bed, not per tile: open ground doesn't keep worms.

versions.title: Outpost sleep: investigation
versions.notes:
- No change to play: this release adds an outpost benchmark for testing (tests/bench_outposts.gd) and the findings of the outpost sleep investigation.
- Result: far outposts cost no more per tick than the same outposts packed together, so putting them to sleep isn't worth it. What grows with distance is the smog and greening updates, which sweep the empty land between outposts; a cheaper fix for that is now an idea for a later round.

**Limitations:** Nothing changes in game; outpost sleep itself won't be built (chunk 190 is skipped).

versions.title: While you were away
versions.notes:
- While you were away: joining a friend's world again shows a card of what changed since your last visit: what each friend built (by name), regions restored, money in and out, and anything that needs a look.
- Loading your own save a day or more (real time) after you saved it shows a short Welcome back card: the day, your money, regions restored, the next chapter goal and open alerts.

**Limitations:** Buildings from before this version don't remember who built them, so they never show on the card. Money goes back a week at most.

versions.title: Ride the cart
versions.notes:
- Ride the cart: stand beside a Farm Cart or a barge and press Y to climb aboard; you ride along its route and press Y again to hop off anywhere, landing beside the rails or the bank.
- At a Cart Station or a sending Barge Dock with one parked, Y waits aboard: you leave with the next cart or barge that sets off.
- A cart that parks (or a barge that sinks in a flood) sets its riders down safely beside it. Before a flood no barge leaves, and the message says so. In co-op, friends see you ride along.

**Limitations:** You can't sleep while riding. In combat worlds, bugs can still reach you on the way.

versions.title: Remote view from the map
versions.notes:
- Click a building on the map (M) to open its window from afar, if a Roboport covers it: change the recipe, filters, schedules and conditions, or read why it's idle.
- A remote window says so in its title and has a "Take a look" button that shows the spot live on the map. Putting items in or taking them out still needs you (or a drone) there.
- Pointing at a building on the map says whether it can be opened remotely.

**Limitations:** Without a Roboport network over it, you have to walk there, so the early game still walks.

versions.title: Valley chapters
versions.notes:
- Valley chapters: the game is split into six chapters (First harvest, Power, The village, The first region, The river, The Vault), each with three or four goals and a money reward.
- After the first-day checklist, the panel at the side of the screen shows just the current chapter's next goal; click it to open the new Chapters tab in the Collection book (J), with every goal ticked as you go.
- Finishing the last chapter earns the Keeper's hat.

**Limitations:** In co-op, chapters are shared by the whole world and the reward goes into everyone's purse. Worlds from before this version start at the first chapter they haven't finished, without paying for the ones already done.

versions.title: Balance report
versions.notes:
- No change to play: this release adds a balance report for testing (tests/balance.gd) that lists money per minute for every machine recipe and flags the ones that lose money or break even.
- Its first findings (Cherry Jam and the two berry juices sell for less than their fruit; Sugar and Honey Tart break even) are written up for a later price pass.

**Limitations:** Prices aren't changed yet; the report uses base prices, not today's demand.

versions.title: Change layer
versions.notes:
- A new map layer, "Change since dawn": tiles that turned greener today show green, tiles that withered show red, and the rest of the map dims, so you can see at a glance where you're winning against smog.
- The legend counts how many tiles greened and withered, and pointing at a tile says how much it changed since dawn.

**Limitations:** It compares with this morning, not a full day back; the minimap doesn't show it.

versions.title: Why can't I place this?
versions.notes:
- A red placement ghost now says why under the cursor: someone's standing there, you don't have one, rubble or a rock in the way, water (build a bridge), a ditch, the old riverbed, unexplored land, a nest, needs the shore or a river bank, a pump needs water behind it, and so on.
- Clicking or dragging onto a spot that won't take the building shows the reason once as a message, instead of nothing happening.
- The Forester's line says when there's no room to plant in its square.

**Limitations:** Claimed plots never block building by hand, so they don't show a reason.

versions.title: Share a strain or a valley
versions.notes:
- Strain codes: in a Seed Lab, copy a bred crop's strain as a short code (BWS1:...) and send it to a friend; they paste it in their Seed Lab and Import it. Each trait keeps the better of the two levels.
- Valley codes: the farmhouse window copies this world's code (BWV1:...), its seed and world settings, challenge included. Paste one on the new-world screen to start the same valley.

**Limitations:** Codes only carry the start of a valley, not anyone's farm.

versions.title: Year in review
versions.notes:
- Year in review: on the first morning of each new year (four seasons, or 28 days without seasons) a scrapbook page goes into the Collection book's new Scrapbook tab, with a picture of the valley as it was.
- Each page has the year's top dish, what you earned, the regions you restored, new wildlife, your best fair ribbon and your zero-smog days. A card explains it the first time.

**Limitations:** Pictures are saved on this computer (like the time-lapse), so a friend in co-op sees the pages but their own pictures.

versions.title: Valley challenges
versions.notes:
- Valley challenges on the new-world screen, each with one twist: Drought Valley (no lakes but the little starting pond), Long Winter (you arrive in winter, and every winter lasts twice as long), Islands (three times the lakes, half the rubble) and No Burners (nothing that burns fuel; you start with solar panels and an electric furnace).
- The goal is Valley in Bloom, and the screen keeps your best day for each challenge.

**Limitations:** No Burners still lists burner research in the shop; buying it does nothing there.

versions.title: Comfort settings
versions.notes:
- A Comfort section in Settings. Reduced motion turns off greening sparkles, region bursts, harvest pops, rainbows and swaying grass, and the camera snaps instead of gliding.
- Pause when the tab or window is hidden (single player) opens the pause menu as soon as you switch away.
- Status colours: Normal, Blue / orange (colour-blind friendly) or High contrast, for the Idle map layer, building ghosts (can / can't build) and cart signal lights.
- Bolder text, and Click once to take apart: one right-click starts taking things apart (as if holding the button), another stops.
- Fixed: the v0.1.160 entry in this list was missing a field, which made the version list error.

**Limitations:** The palettes don't reach the soil view, power overlay or alert buttons yet.

versions.title: Pause and game speed
versions.notes:
- Single player: Backspace stops the clock but not you. While paused you can still walk, build, plan and open windows, and everything you do happens at once. A Paused banner shows at the top.
- = cycles the game speed between 1×, 2× and 3× (a badge shows it). Sleeping uses its own fast-forward and puts the speed back to normal, as do loading and starting a world.
- Both keys can be rebound. In co-op they do nothing, since everyone's clock has to stay in step.

versions.title: Rotate the camera
versions.notes:
- Turn the camera a quarter at a time with comma and period (rebindable in Settings, Keys). It eases round, and walking (keys, gamepad and touch stick) follows it, so up is always up the screen.
- A small compass shows which way north is while the camera is turned. The game remembers your turn, and photo mode puts it back when you leave.

**Limitations:** The map and minimap stay north-up.

versions.title: Harvest pop, dawn chorus and rainbows
versions.notes:
- Harvest pop: picked crops and fruit hop out of the bed in a little arc to the farmer, and a run of harvests shares one toast that counts up ("+36 Wheat") instead of stacking.
- Dawn chorus: birds sing at sunrise, from one to four of them, more over green, clean land with many kinds of plants. Not in winter or in the rain.
- Rainbows: on a clear morning after a rainy day, a rainbow hangs in the sky over green land.

**Limitations:** Only harvesting by hand pops; taking dishes out of machines doesn't yet.

versions.title: Display signs
versions.notes:
- Display Signs: wire one to a chest, machine or belt the same way as an inserter condition, pick the item, and it shows the count ("128 Wheat", or items a minute on a belt) in big letters over the sign.
- Zoom the map in and the signs' numbers show there too. Blueprints and copy-paste carry what a sign counts.

**Limitations:** The text updates once a second.

versions.title: Cart signals
versions.notes:
- Cart Signals (with Farm Carts research): put one beside a Cart Rail and that rail becomes a gate splitting the line into blocks. A cart waits at the gate while the block past it has another cart stopped in it (loading at a station, or queuing), so several carts can share one line and take turns at the platform.
- Carts passing through a block never hold anyone up, two carts each waiting for the other's block both go, and after 30 seconds a cart goes anyway, so a line can't lock up. The signal's light shows red while it's holding carts back.

**Limitations:** Blocks aren't tinted in Alt view; hover a signal to see whether it's red or green.

versions.title: Frozen ponds
versions.notes:
- Frozen ponds: on snowy winter days and on the coldest days of each winter (the forecast says Freezing) small ponds ice over. An Offshore Pump on a frozen pond runs at a quarter speed, unless a working Boiler stands within 2 tiles to keep the water open. Big lakes and rivers never freeze.
- A Frozen ponds card as soon as you own a pump on a small pond, before the first freeze.
- Cut ice: hold right-click on a frozen pond for a block of ice. An Icebox without power melts one block every 5 minutes to stay cold.

**Limitations:** Frozen ponds don't show on the map; the pale ice is only in the world.

versions.title: Hail
versions.notes:
- Hail: now and then summer rain turns to hail (in the forecast a week ahead, and announced the evening before). It can crack the glass of Greenhouses and Solar Panels: a cracked greenhouse stops growing, a cracked panel makes no power, until you repair it with 1 glass pane.
- A Hail and glass card the moment you own a greenhouse or solar panel, before hail can ever reach them.
- Hail Shutters research ($400, after Solar Panels): shutters close over every greenhouse and panel on hail days, so nothing cracks.

**Limitations:** Cracked glass doesn't look different yet: the hover, window and a Repairs needed alert say so.

versions.title: Zero-smog days
versions.notes:
- A Smog ledger tab in the Production window: all the smog your buildings have made against what your valley's beds and trees could soak up, today so far, and a badge for each of the last two weeks.
- A day your plants could soak up more than you made is a zero-smog day (and a new Clean air achievement at 7). Seven in a row and an eagle comes back to circle over the valley.

**Limitations:** A day with no smog made at all doesn't count as clean: it's a goal for replacing burners, not for an empty farm.

versions.title: Eco-tourists
versions.notes:
- Eco-tourism (research, $800, after the museum): a 2×2 log Lodge. Once regions are restored, hikers come to walk your green land and pay $25 a night each: 2 for every restored region (up to 6), more the greener the lodge's region is and the more kinds of crop and fruit tree grow there.
- Smog at the lodge, or a smog wreck within 20 tiles, sends them all home. The lodge's window explains tonight's count. By day the guests stroll round it.

versions.title: Beavers
versions.notes:
- Beavers come back once the river flows again, and now and then they dam it: a new pond beside the river in a restored region (more fish, more water for pumps).
- Fair warning first: 3 days ahead a card explains it and the tiles that will flood show in blue in the world, on the map and in the hover tip. Anything built there goes back in your backpack. Hold right-click on the dam site with the Shovel to break it up, and they move on for a while.

versions.title: Valley museum
versions.notes:
- The Valley Museum (research, $600; 20 bricks, 20 planks, 4 glass panes): a 3×3 hall that shows off your Collection trophies, county fair ribbons and journal pages by itself, and one Excellent dish of each kind you give it from its window.
- Visitors pay $2 for every exhibit each morning, so the fee grows as it fills. One museum is enough: a second doesn't double it.

versions.title: Decorations and beauty
versions.notes:
- Decorations: benches, flower borders and stone paths (drag to lay a line), a 2×2 fountain and a statue. Each 8×8 block of land gets a beauty score from its decor (plus a little for flower patches and fruit trees), shown in Alt view.
- Families in cottages in a beautiful block get happier each morning (up to +15%). Decor shows in a warm colour on the map and in the time-lapse.

versions.title: Beeswax and candles
versions.notes:
- Beehives give a lump of beeswax with every 3 honey. A Chandler (6 planks, 2 iron plates, no power) dips 4 candles from 2 beeswax and a flax or cotton yarn wick.
- Lamps take up to 10 candles and burn one on a night they have no power, so they work off the grid. Candles are a cottage comfort too.

versions.title: Farmhands
versions.notes:
- Farmhands: a well-fed village lends you helpers, one for each cottage at tier 2 or more (up to 3). Each works from a Farmhand's Post (6 planks): in the 9×9 square round it, it carries items on the ground and wild plants it forages back to the post's chest, and takes fuel from the chest to burner buildings running low.
- Slower than drones, but there from the early game. Hands walk about in blue smocks; the post's window says whether it has one.

**Limitations:** Hands don't check claimed plots.

versions.title: Supply contracts
versions.notes:
- Supply contracts: each season a neighbouring town offers a deal on the farmhouse's orders board, say 12 bread a day for the season at a fixed price the market glut can't touch. Accept it and fill a Contract Crate (a crate and 2 planks): they collect each morning.
- The board and the crate count the days met and missed. A short morning costs a point of reputation, and 3 of them end the deal. A card explains this the moment you take a contract, and from the evening before each collection the crate, the board and an alert say if you're short.

**Limitations:** One contract at a time.

versions.title: Daily cravings and harvest festivals
versions.notes:
- Daily cravings: each morning one cottage craves one dish you can make (on the morning report and its hover). It takes up to 5 of it on top of its basket today, paying 3× the price for each, on the spot.
- Harvest festivals (worlds with seasons): one day near the end of each season, shown in the forecast a week ahead. That day one in-season dish sells for 3× at the dock; sell 30 and every family is happier, and you earn the Festival hat.

versions.title: Hedgerows
versions.notes:
- Hedgerows: a sapling and 2 wood make two hedges, dragged out in a line like belts. They grow in two days, then green their line (it counts toward regions and green corridors), feed bees like flowers, and shelter beds within 2 tiles in a dry spell (3/4 speed instead of half).
- Deer, once they're back, like to graze beside them. A living alternative to stone walls.

**Limitations:** Storms don't hurt beds, so the shelter is from dry spells.

versions.title: Rain barrels
versions.notes:
- Rain Barrels (4 planks, 1 iron plate, no research): a barrel fills on rainy and snowy days, then keeps the beds within 2 tiles watered for the next 3 dry days. Early watering far from lakes and ditches, and a reason to read the forecast.
- Its hover says how many dry days of water it has left. In worlds without weather it fills every 4 days.

versions.title: Footsteps by ground
versions.notes:
- Footsteps: a dry crunch on barren dirt, soft steps on green grass, a splash in water and ditches, a clack on roads and bridges, so walking from ruined land into restored land sounds different.
- They're quiet, and have their own Footsteps slider in Settings (it follows the Sounds slider too). Only your own farmer makes them, and riding a belt doesn't.

versions.title: A 5×5 farmhouse that grows
versions.notes:
- The farmhouse is 5×5 now: a small house at the back of a fenced yard, with room to grow. It gains a porch once you fill a villager order, a kitchen garden once a family moves into a cottage, a little windmill once a region is restored, and a wall of ribbons at 3 county fair ribbons. Its hover says what it has and what's still to come.
- Old worlds: your farmhouse grows round where it stood, picking the spot that's on land and in the way of the least. Anything it still covers goes back in your backpack with what it held, and a note says how many.

versions.title: First-time building cards
versions.notes:
- The first time you place each kind of building, a small card shows what goes in and what comes out (an icon row: in > building > out), what it needs (power or fuel), and its most common mistake.
- Cards are remembered per player, not per world, so a new world doesn't repeat them. Settings can switch them off or show them all again.

**Limitations:** Belts, pipes, poles, roads, walls, rails, ditches, bridges and saplings have no card.

versions.title: The wood wide web
versions.notes:
- The wood wide web: an old-growth tree's roots reach 4 tiles under the soil. Garden Beds in reach grow 20% faster and saplings 50% faster, so keeping an old grove next to a farm pays off.
- Alt view draws the fungal threads faintly from each old tree to the beds and saplings it feeds; their hover says when they're under the web.

versions.title: Co-op county fair
versions.notes:
- Co-op county fair (own backpacks): each player enters their own dish and crop, and each is judged against the rival farms, prizes to whoever entered.
- With two or more dishes in, the village votes for its favourite: the winner gets a Village Choice ribbon, tallied per player in the farmhouse window, and wears it on their name tag until the next fair.

versions.title: Claimed plots
versions.notes:
- Claimed plots (co-op with own backpacks): a Signpost (2 planks) claims the square around it for whoever put it up. Other players' construction drones, take-apart and upgrade plans, and pasted blueprints skip it, so friends can build side by side.
- Building by hand still works anywhere. Open the signpost to make the plot bigger or smaller (4 to 16 tiles each way) or share it; holding or hovering a signpost shows its square. A card explains plots the first time one goes up.

versions.title: Bottleneck finder and idle map layer
versions.notes:
- Bottleneck finder: a new Bottlenecks tab in the Production window (P). Pick a dish and it looks at every machine and Farm Tower in its chain, naming the one that's idle most (with why) and the one whose output backs up most, each with a Show on the map button.
- Idle map layer: tick Idle on the map (M) to mark every machine and tower that's been idle for a minute, coloured by why: red no power, yellow no input, blue output full, grey anything else.

versions.title: Morning report and next ideas
versions.notes:
- Morning report: a small card each morning with yesterday's money in and out, your three best sellers, how happy the village was, the region closest to restored, and today's weather and events. Turn it off in Settings.
- Next ideas: the Journal tab (J) suggests one or two things you haven't tried yet, based on what you do (crafting by hand: try an Assembler; animals: try the Biogas Digester; and so on), with a Help button and the lesson that teaches it.

versions.title: Smart Farm Towers
versions.notes:
- Smart Farm Towers: in a tower's window, wire it to a chest and give it a rule: grow one crop while the chest has under some amount of an item, another once it's stocked (say tomatoes while the tomato chest is under 200, else wheat).
- The tower keeps seeds of both crops and switches by itself. Copy/paste and blueprints carry the rule.

versions.title: Conditions read machines and belts
versions.notes:
- Conditions read more than chests: wire an inserter, belt or sluice gate to a machine (its output or its input), a Farm Tower (its products), or a belt tile (items passing a minute).
- Stop feeding an oven when its output backs up, or run a line only while another belt is busy. Pick what it reads in the condition's Reads: list.

versions.title: Bulk Inserter
versions.notes:
- Bulk Inserter (research it after the Fast Inserter): moves up to 5 of the same item each swing. Into a crate or machine it drops them all at once; onto a belt one by one as there's room. Made from a Fast Inserter, 5 gears and 5 iron plates.
- Inserter tooltips show how many items the arm is holding.

versions.title: Green corridors
versions.notes:
- Green corridors: two side-by-side restored regions are linked when a strip of green land at least 3 tiles wide crosses the border between them. The map draws a green line between linked regions, and the first link earns the Green corridor achievement.
- Linked regions share their wildlife: deer show up more often there and wander across toward the next region. Every other seed the birds drop lands along a corridor as a wildflower patch.

**Limitations:** Only regions that touch can link; a corridor through an unrestored region doesn't count.

versions.title: Migrating geese
versions.notes:
- Migrating geese: one morning each autumn (every 12 days without seasons) a flock flies over the valley and lands only on lakes with clean air over every tile.
- Each lake they rest on gets 4 feathers on its shore. Feathers and cloth make Pillows, another home comfort for a cottage.
- The first landing adds Migrating geese to the Wildlife page of the collection book (a page you'd already finished keeps its trophy and isn't paid twice).

versions.title: Old-growth trees
versions.notes:
- Old-growth trees: a planted tree left standing 12 days becomes old-growth: it grows bigger, soaks up twice the smog, and greens the land 7 tiles out instead of 5. The tooltip counts down the days.
- In the cold pines, an old-growth tree grows a truffle at its roots every 3 days: click the tree to dig it up. Truffles make Truffle Pasta at the Prep Table.
- Foresters leave old-growth trees standing unless you tick "Cut old-growth trees too" in their window.

versions.title: Herb garden and drying rack
versions.notes:
- Herb garden: thyme, mint and chamomile sprout wild on green land in restored regions. Pick them by hand; their seeds grow in beds.
- The Drying Rack (planks and flax yarn) dries herbs in the sun: no power or fuel, but only by day when it isn't raining.
- Dried herbs make Herb Tea (Roaster) and Seasoning (Prep Table). Give Seasoning to an Oven, Assembler or Prep Table: each batch uses one and comes out a quality point better.
- A flower pot and a sprig of mint make a Potted Herb, another home comfort for a cottage.

versions.title: Sourdough starter
versions.notes:
- Sourdough starter: a Fermenting Crock can make a starter from 2 flour. It lives in the crock, which then makes Sourdough Dough from flour; ovens bake it into Sourdough, worth three times bread. The gentry now want a loaf a day.
- A starter is alive and has to eat: every morning it takes 1 flour from its crock. A morning with no flour and it's hungry (news, and the crock says so all day); a second morning in a row and it goes flat.
- A warning card explains this the moment your first starter comes alive.

versions.title: Sugar beets and the Sugar Refinery
versions.notes:
- Sugar beets: a new crop (seed packs in the shop) that grows best in summer and autumn, on loam.
- The Sugar Refinery (research "Sugar" after the Canning Line): a 3×3 machine that boils 4 beets into 2 Sugar and 1 Molasses.
- Sugar makes Candy (Prep Table, with milk), Frosted Cake (Oven, from a cake) and Jam with sugar (Canning Line, from fewer strawberries). The old cake and jam recipes are unchanged.
- Molasses feeds a Biogas Digester, or a Dairy Barn, which then gives an extra milk per batch.

versions.title: Sand and glass
versions.notes:
- Sand and glass: put sandy soil (dig it with the Shovel) in a furnace and it melts into glass, 2 for 1.
- Glass makes Glass Panes and Bottles by hand. Panes are a second, cheaper way to build Greenhouses (8 panes, 4 iron plates, 6 planks) and Solar Panels (3 panes, 3 copper plates, a gear); both show up in the crafting menu.
- Bottles on the Juicer and Cider Press make Bottled Juice and Bottled Cider, which sell for half as much again.

versions.title: Clay and the kiln
versions.notes:
- Clay and the Kiln (research it after the Shovel): a 2×2 burner kiln fires the clay the Shovel leaves behind into bricks (2 clay for 1), jars (1 clay for 2) and flower pots.
- Jars on the Canning Line: strawberries and a jar make 2 jam instead of 1.
- A flower pot on a cottage's doorstep is a home comfort, like curtains and quilts: the family is a little happier and thanks you a little more.

versions.title: Letters from old valleys
versions.notes:
- Letters from old valleys: after you move to a new valley, the farm you left keeps going. Each season (every 4 days without seasons) a crate from it waits in your farmhouse mailbox.
- A crate holds 10 each of the old valley's three best sellers, some of its best dish and 10 seeds of its biggest crop, with a letter. The postcard is the old valley's last time-lapse picture, if it's on this computer.
- The last three valleys you left all keep writing.

**Limitations:** What a crate holds is fixed when you leave (from what that valley sold most), not worked out from its machines.

versions.title: Heritage wing
versions.notes:
- The Heritage wing: after the Great Seed Vault opens, it has three optional stages more, in its window. Each gives the whole valley a perk.
- The tasting hall (Excellent bread, pizza, cheese and cake only): bees range 6 tiles from their hives instead of 4.
- The far gardens (every far-biome crop): fruit trees bear twice in autumn.
- The river room (fish and preserves): the merchant visits every 3 days.

versions.title: Valley climate
versions.notes:
- Valley climate (worlds with weather): each morning, the share of the explored valley that's green sets the climate, from Harsh to Gentle, a step per quarter.
- Each step brings a little more gentle rain, fewer dry spells, and fewer storms and floods. From the Mild step, winter thaws a day early (two days when Gentle): those days feel like spring for weather and crops.
- The forecast shows the climate meter: the current step, how green the valley is, and what the next step brings.

**Limitations:** A new climate step can change the forecast for the days after it.

versions.title: Bring back the river
versions.notes:
- Bring back the river: a dry riverbed now winds from far up the valley down to near your farm. Nothing can be built on it, and a card explains it the first time you stand by it.
- Its headwaters are a chain of regions (the map marks each "River headwater 1 of N"). Restore them from the far end in, and the river flows again region by region; once every one is restored it reaches the Home Meadow.
- Flowing riverbed is real river: barges, water wheels, fish traps and ditches all work on it. Anything an older save had built in the bed goes back to your backpack when the water comes.

**Limitations:** The headwaters are far out (up to 300 tiles), so most of the chain is in land you haven't explored yet.

versions.title: Field guide and cloth goods
versions.notes:
- Field guide: wildflower patches now come in five kinds (pink campion, buttercup, violet, oxeye daisy, poppy), each its own colour. Walk by one in full bloom to add it to the new Meadow page of the collection book (J).
- The Meadow page also asks for a spot where crops, trees, fruit trees, wildflowers and wild plants all grow together. Finish it for $400 and the Botanist's hat.
- Cloth goods: the Loom makes Curtains (3 linen) and Quilts (3 cloth, 2 flax yarn). Give a cottage one of each: the family is a little happier every morning and thanks you a little more.

versions.title: Ditch gates
versions.notes:
- Sluice Gates (3 planks and a gear): set one on an irrigation ditch. Open, water flows through; closed, the ditch past it runs dry, and so does the land beside it. Send water down one ditch or another.
- Click a gate to open or close it, or wire it to a chest (like inserters and belts) so it opens only while the chest has less, or more, than some amount.

versions.title: Barge schedules
versions.notes:
- Barge schedules: a Send dock can have a list of stops (other docks on the same river). Each barge goes to the next stop in turn instead of the nearest Receive dock.
- Leave rule per dock: a full load or 20 seconds (as before), only a full load, or every 20 seconds with whatever is there.
- Before a forecast flood, from the evening no barge leaves, and barges out on the river turn for home with their loads (the barge card says so).
- Benchmark fix: the big test factory builds its farm towers again, so the benchmark measures farming and greening.

versions.title: Region quests
versions.notes:
- Region quests: every named region except Home Meadow has one wish, shown on a card the first time you walk in: plant 20 trees there, green its lake shore, bring its old mill back (build a Mill there), or clear its ruins and wrecks.
- A done quest pays $400 (plus $100 for each quest done before) and 6 seed bombs, on top of the reward for greening the region.
- Quest progress shows in the hover tip and under the region's name on the map (M).

versions.title: No more beeping, metal inserters, soil favourites
versions.notes:
- The beeping near miners is gone. It was the greening sparkle: smog from miners wilted the grass around them, the grass grew back, and every time it turned fully green again it sparkled and chimed. Grass regrowing under smog is quiet now; land turning green in clean air still sparkles.
- The factory sound near working machines no longer ticks (it had a fast high click); it's a soft hum and clank now, with its own Factory hum slider in Settings (0 turns it off).
- Inserters are made from 2 gears and 1 iron plate instead of a plank (Burner Inserters still use planks).
- Soil: every crop grows 25% faster on its favourite soil and at normal speed on the others, so loam is no longer best for everything. Wheat, tomatoes, lettuce, corn and flax like loam; potatoes and berries like sandy soil; rice, cranberries, mushrooms and cabbage like clay. Fertilized harvests turn a bed's soil into its crop's favourite.

versions.title: Rename a save, Fast Inserter
versions.notes:
- Rename a save: every save in the Save and Load lists has a Rename button. Type the new name and press Enter (Esc cancels); its picture moves with it, and if it's the farm you're playing, it keeps saving under the new name.
- Fast Inserter (research it in the shop after the Long Inserter): swings more than twice as fast as an Inserter, for busy ovens, smelters and docks. Made from an Inserter, 2 gears and 2 copper plates.

versions.title: Sawdust and mulch
versions.notes:
- Crafting planks now also leaves sawdust (a weak fuel). Assemblers making planks pile it on the side, so it never ends up on the plank belt: take it by hand or with an inserter filtered to Sawdust.
- Mulch (4 sawdust make 2): put it on a garden bed and the bed stays watered for 3 harvests, through dry spells too.
- Mushroom Logs (wood and sawdust) sprout 6 mushrooms each in a dark Mushroom Cellar, which needs no power.

versions.title: F3 overlay and save sizes
versions.notes:
- F3 shows a performance overlay: how long a sim tick and a frame take, buildings, belts and belt items, machines, drones, carts, barges, bugs, the world's size, and chunks generated, so slowdowns in big factories are easy to report and find.
- The load menu shows each save's size and, at the top, how full storage is.
- When storage is nearly full (80%: the browser's own estimate on the web, otherwise 50 MB of saves), a card warns you after a save, and the load menu offers to clear old autosaves (all but the newest of each world); Export saves anything you want to keep.

versions.title: Night ambience and graphics presets
versions.notes:
- Night on green land: fireflies blink over green meadows, glowing mushrooms light up the green pines, and crickets sing, louder the more green, clean land is around you. Barren and smoggy land stays dark and silent, so you can hear the difference between restored and ruined land.
- Graphics presets in Settings: Low (no shadows, wildlife, water ripples, or swaying grass, and a lower render scale), Medium, and High.
- On first launch the game watches the frame rate for a few seconds of play and picks a preset for you (it says so if it picks Low or Medium).

versions.title: Recipe pins and drag-to-set crops
versions.notes:
- Pin a recipe to the screen: Ctrl-click it in the crafting grid (or press Pin in the item lookup). Its ingredients show at the top right with how many you have, turning green as you gather them, and the recipe says when it's ready to craft. Up to three pins; Unpin removes one.
- Drag to set crops: hold a seed and drag across Garden Beds and Farm Towers. Empty beds are planted with it and every tower you pass is set to grow that crop.

versions.title: First-day checklist, idle reasons, item lookup
versions.notes:
- First-day checklist: on a new world (not a tutorial), a small list on the left walks you through the real game in place (salvage scrap, craft and place a bed, plant wheat, sell a crop, build a burner, lay a belt), ticking off each step. Hide it for the world with its Hide button, or turn it off for new worlds in Settings.
- Why is this idle? Every working building's window starts with one plain sentence: working, no power, low power, out of fuel, no recipe, missing flour, output full, no seeds, needs feed, out of season, or too much smog. Its Show button looks up the missing item, or opens the map at the building with the power overlay on.
- Item lookup: middle-click (or Ctrl-click) an item in the inventory or the crafting grid to see every recipe that makes it and every recipe that uses it, with the machine. Click any item there to look that one up (Back returns).

versions.title: Valley journal and field notes
versions.notes:
- Valley journal: ten pages of an old diary and letters turn up, in order, while you salvage ruins and wrecks, telling why the valley dried up and what the old farm grew. Read them on the new Journal tab of the collection book (J).
- Some pages teach a lost recipe (cornbread, the tart, cheese), and one marks an overgrown greenhouse on your map.
- Field notes: a Research Desk studies samples (crops, dishes, and parts like gears and plates), one a second, by hand or inserter, earning field notes worth about a quarter of each sample's price. Shift-click a research card in the shop to pay for it in field notes instead of money (one note pays for $5), so an automated sample line feeds the tech tree without flooding the market.

versions.title: Named regions and greening ripple
versions.notes:
- The valley is split into named regions (64×64 tiles: Home Meadow where you start, then names like Dry Creek, Ashen Flats, or Old Mill Hollow), each with a restoration %: how much of its land is green. The map (M) shows their borders, names, and %, and the hover tooltip says which region you're in.
- Restoring a region (60% green) pays a reward that grows with each one, with a little scene: a ring of sparkles, a chime, and a card.
- Returning wildlife now follows the regions: birds come back when a region is a quarter green, deer when one is restored, and the white stag after three.
- Greening ripple: a soft flash and sparkle (and a faint twinkle) where a tile turns fully green near you.

versions.title: Irrigation ditches and river barges
versions.notes:
- Irrigation Ditches: with the Shovel, dig channels (lined with ditch boards, 1 plank makes 4) and drag to dig a line. A ditch joined to a lake or river, directly or through other ditches, fills with water, and the land beside it counts as watered: thirsty crops grow at full speed and dry spells don't slow them. Belts, pipes, and poles can cross ditches; hold right-click to fill one in.
- River barges (research after Cart Stations): a Barge Dock on a river bank is a crate set to Send or Receive. Put Barges in a Send dock and they float loads along the river to the nearest Receive dock on the same water. Rivers flow away from where you started: fast downstream, slow coming back.
- Hazard, with a warning card the first time you have a dock or barge: on a spring flood day barges stay moored, and a barge already out on the river when the flood comes sinks with its load. Floods are forecast the evening before.

versions.title: Reed beds and returning wildlife
versions.notes:
- Reed Beds (shop, after the Fish Trap): place one on a lake or river shore and its reeds slowly clean the smog out of the water and air around it, with no power or filters, so fish come back to polluted lakes. They green the shore too.
- Wildlife comes back as the valley greens: birds (at 1,500 green tiles), then deer (5,000), then a rare white stag (12,000). Each arrival is news and an entry on a new Wildlife page of the collection book.
- Birds fly over green land and now and then drop wild seeds where the green thins out, and wildflowers grow there: slow, free greening. Deer graze on green land, and once it's back you may spot the white stag.

**Limitations:** Wildlife milestones count green tiles across the whole valley for now.

versions.title: Seed bombs and biodiversity
versions.notes:
- Seed Bombs (2 wheat seeds and a stone make 2): hold one and click bare ground within 8 tiles to throw it. Wildflowers grow there over a couple of minutes and slowly green the land around them: weaker than a tree, but a fun way to green places you won't build on, and bees visit them.
- Seed Spreader (shop, after the Composter): fill it with seed bombs and it throws one every 20 s onto bare ground up to 6 tiles away.
- Biodiversity bonus: land greens a little more strongly where several kinds of plant grow close together (crops, trees, orchard trees, wildflowers, wild plants): +8% for each kind past the first, up to +32%. The hover tooltip names the kinds near a tile, and Alt view shows the bonus over the land.

versions.title: Fermenting Crock
versions.notes:
- New Fermenting Crock (no research, stone and planks): it needs no power or fuel but takes about half a day a batch. Cabbage becomes Sauerkraut, milk Yogurt, and grapes Vinegar.
- Ferments never spoil and sell for half again as much in winter, a cheap early alternative to the Canning Line.
