- Rainy Day (+40): rain and puddles that slow everyone, and footsteps that squelch loud enough for nearby critters to hear.
- Fireworks Night (+60): it's dark, but every firework lights up the critters around you for a moment, even behind walls.
- Big Sale (+30): more loot in containers and on the ground, and more raccoons after it.

versions.title: Paid exits
versions.notes:
- Paid exits: some raids, an exit wants something to let you through. The Ice Cream Van wants 150 crumbs' worth of loot, the Duck Boat a Car Battery, and in the suburb the Storm Drain wants 100 crumbs' worth and the Back Alley Gate some Car Keys.
- The price is on the exit's sign, in the exit list, on the map, and in the opening banner. Payment comes out of your backpack as you leave, cheapest loot first.

versions.title: The Golden Picnic
versions.notes:
- The Golden Picnic: with 3 minutes left, a golden box parachutes into the map (banner, and a gold square on the minimap and map). It's packed with 5 to 7 rare things.
- Only the few critters close to where it lands (the 3 nearest within 30 m) come to look, so the rest of the map isn't left empty.

versions.title: Music
versions.notes:
- Music! All of it made in code like the sounds: a cosy plucky loop on the title and in the Nest, a calm park tune in raids, and a tense beat with drums whenever a critter is fighting you.
- Music: On/Off on the title screen and in the pause menu, separate from Sound, and remembered.

versions.title: Import and export saves
versions.notes:
- Save Data on the title screen: copy your save as a text code (or download it as a file in the browser) to back it up or move it to another computer.
- Paste a code (or load a file) to bring a save back. It shows what you'd be replacing and asks before it does.

versions.title: Melee weapons
versions.notes:
- Melee weapons that need no ammo: the Rolled Newspaper (quick swats), the Baguette Bat (long reach), and the Frying Pan (slow, huge BONG that dizzies what it hits).
- A swing hits every critter in an arc in front of the goose, and it's quiet: only critters close by hear it.
- Find them in crates (and newspapers in bins), or buy them in the Nest. They swish and bong.
- Fixed: weapons you found and carried out in your backpack now go in the stash (they used to vanish).

versions.title: View cone
versions.notes:
- A view cone: everything outside a 110-degree cone toward the cursor (and beyond how far you can see) is darkened, with a small bright circle around the goose.
- Critters outside your cone are hidden, just like ones behind walls. Turn to look! They can still hear you.

versions.title: Bigger stash
versions.notes:
- The stash has a size now: 40 slots to start, one per stack (125 Foam Darts take 3). The Stash column shows how full it is, and each item says how many slots it takes.
- Bigger stashes in the Nest's shop: 60 slots for 500 crumbs, 90 for 1500, and 130 for 4000.
- Extracting always banks everything, even past the limit, but an overflowing stash has to be sold down (or upgraded) before the next raid.

versions.title: Sharper maps
versions.notes:
- Sharper maps: the map screen (M) and the minimap are drawn at 4 and 3 pixels per meter instead of 1, so they're no longer stretched and blurry.
- Walls, hedges, cars, and the pond get a dark outline on the map, so shapes read at a glance.
- Area names on the map step aside for nearby exit labels instead of overlapping them.

versions.title: The Suburb Cul-de-sac
versions.notes:
- A second map, the Suburb Cul-de-sac: a turning circle, The Big House you can walk into, a garage, a paddling pool behind a fence, a veggie patch, a playhouse garden, front lawns, a back alley, and a tree house.
- Its own exits: the Mail Truck where you arrive, plus two of the Storm Drain, the Back Alley Gate, the Cat Flap, and the Tree House Rope.
- A map picker in the Nest. The suburb unlocks after 3 extractions from Picnic Park (old saves count the extractions they already have).
- The Nest's Bringing column is more compact (weapons and the secure pouch side by side), and Repack moved up next to the Lost Gosling button.

versions.title: Lost Gosling runs
versions.notes:
- Lost Gosling runs: a free raid from the Nest with a random cheap kit (a Foam Blaster or Pea Shooter, some ammo, a snack or two). Nothing from the Nest comes along, so nothing is at risk.
- Extract and the haul (and the kit's weapon) goes in the stash. Get bonked and you lose only the free kit.
- One every 20 minutes; the button counts down, and the wait is remembered.

versions.title: Secure pouch
versions.notes:
- A secure pouch: two small slots (1 kg) that always come home, even if you're bonked, locked in, or give up.
- Pack it in the Nest with To pouch, or move things in and out of it from the backpack screen (Tab) during a raid.
- Bigger pouches in the Nest's shop: 3 slots and 2 kg for 400 crumbs, then 4 slots and 3 kg for 1000.
- The results screen shows what the pouch saved.

versions.title: Polish
versions.notes:
- Sound! All of it made from scratch in code: honks, squawks when you're hit, foam dart pffs, pea pops, balloon splashes, slingshot thwips, a cartoon boing when a critter goes down, rummaging, loot bloops, reloads, munching, footsteps, a happy chime when you extract, and a sad wah-wah when you don't.
- Sound On/Off on the title screen and in the pause menu (remembered).
- A minimap in the top right, turned like the camera, with the open exits (far ones pinned to the edge pointing the way).
- You can only see critters that are in your line of sight: walls, hedges, cars, and bushes hide them (and you). Hide in a bush!
- The camera shakes when you get hit or honk, and the Nest jingles when you buy and sell.

versions.title: The Nest
versions.notes:
- Enter the Nest from the title screen: your stash on the left, what you're bringing in the middle, the shop on the right. Click anything to see it and what you can do with it.
- Sell loot for breadcrumbs (or sell all junk and valuables at once). Buy weapons, ammo packs, and snacks; buying costs twice what selling pays.
- Pack your raid: two weapon slots (slot 1 starts in hand) and the backpack. Weapons start the raid loaded from the ammo you pack.
- Bigger backpacks: 16 slots and 25 kg for 300 crumbs, then 20 slots and 30 kg for 800.
- Whatever you bring is at risk. Extract and it all comes home (weapons straight back to their slots); get bonked, locked in, or give up and it stays in the park. Repack copies last raid's backpack from the stash.
- A new save starts with 100 crumbs and a Foam Blaster kit. Broke with no weapon? Mom Goose slips you a spare.
- The pause menu's Quit is now Give Up, which costs your backpack.

versions.title: Combat
versions.notes:
- The park fights back. Garden Gnomes guard spots with slingshots; Raccoons roam the park with acorn poppers, strafe, and more of them wander in as the day goes on.
- They notice you when you're in front of them and in sight (walls and hedges hide you), hear your shots, and come looking where they last saw you.
- You start each raid with a Foam Blaster and 36 darts. Click to shoot (hold for the blaster), R to reload, 1/2 or the mouse wheel to switch.
- Find the Pea Shooter (six peas per shot) and the Balloon Lobber (arcs over cover and splashes) in crates and on raccoons, plus ammo all over. Equip them from the backpack.
- Space dodge rolls through shots (costs puff). Q honks: stuns everything in front of you, alerts everything nearby, then needs to recharge.
- 100 health. H eats the snack that best fits how hurt you are (or use Eat in the backpack); food now heals.
- Bonked critters fall over and drop loot. Get bonked yourself and you lose your backpack and weapons.

**Limitations:** Every raid starts with the same free kit until the Nest arrives.

versions.title: Getting out
versions.notes:
- The park closes in 10 minutes. The clock is in the top right, and the sun sets as closing time nears.
- Ways out: the Bus Stop where you came in is always open, plus two of the Duck Boat, the Ice Cream Van, the Drain Pipe, and the Hole in the Fence, different each raid.
- Open exits glow green with a light column and a sign. Stand in one for 5 seconds to extract; stepping out cancels. The HUD lists each open exit and how far it is.
- M opens a map of the park, turned to match your view, showing the areas, the open exits, and where you are.
- Extract and everything in your backpack goes to your stash, saved between visits. Still in the park when it closes? The ranger confiscates your backpack.
- A results screen shows what you brought out (or lost) and your stash; the title screen shows the stash too.

**Limitations:** The stash can't be opened or spent yet: that's the Nest, coming later.

versions.title: Grabbing loot
versions.notes:
- Loose loot lies all over the park: walk up to anything bobbing on the grass and press E to grab it. Uncommon and better items glow with a beam in their rarity color.
- Tab opens your backpack: click an item to read about it, then Drop it (or Drop One from a stack) at your feet. Dropped things stay on the ground to grab again.
- Heavy new finds: Lawn Flamingo, Bowling Ball, Watermelon, Garden Gnome, and the very valuable, very heavy Car Battery.
- The backpack has a 20 kg limit. Go over it and you waddle slower (down to 60% at 30 kg, a crawl beyond) and can't sprint. The HUD warns you when you're too heavy.
- If your backpack is full, you only pick up what fits.

**Limitations:** Loot still doesn't leave the park: extraction is next.

versions.title: Looting chests
versions.notes:
- Picnic baskets, coolers, trash bins, and supply crates all over the park, each with its own kind of loot. Every raid rolls fresh contents.
- Walk up to one (it gets a glowing ring) and press E to search. Items turn up one at a time; rare things take longer to find, so keep the panel open.
- Click an item to move it into your backpack, or Take All. Click a backpack item to put it back.
- 26 items to find, from Bottle Caps and Soggy Fries to Gold Rings and the legendary Golden Bread. Hover for a description, weight, and worth in breadcrumbs.
- The backpack holds 12 slots; stackable things stack. The HUD shows what you're carrying and a feed of what you just grabbed.

**Limitations:** Loot doesn't leave the park yet: extraction comes in a later release.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- You are a goose in a tiny tactical helmet. Press Raid on the title screen to waddle into Picnic Park from the bus stop.
- WASD waddles (up is up on the screen), the goose faces your cursor, and Shift sprints until you run out of puff.
- Picnic Park: a duck pond, the Snack Shack, restrooms, a parking lot, a playground, a picnic meadow, and a fountain plaza, all hemmed in by hedges.
- The camera follows from an isometric angle and leans toward the cursor. Walls, trees, and cars in front of the goose turn see-through.
- The HUD shows which part of the park you're in.

**Limitations:** Nothing to loot or shoot yet: this release is the park and the goose.

versions.title: Run replays
versions.notes:
- When a Deploy or campaign run ends, a map beside the end screen replays your route over the arena, with icons popping up where you destroyed robots (K), picked up salvage (S) and repair kits (+), cleared waves (W) and went down (X). Click it to skip to the end.
- Every run's replay is saved (the last 30). Replays on the title lists them to watch again or delete.
- Export turns your replays into a line of text (and copies it); paste one in and press Import to add someone's runs.
- The title's Pilot, Leaderboard and Replays buttons share a row.

versions.title: Leaderboard
versions.notes:
- A Leaderboard on the title: the best Deploy runs with pilot, score, wave, chassis and loadout, filtered by version (this version first, or all of them).
- The end of a Deploy run has a name box and Submit score. Your name is remembered.
- For now scores are kept on this machine: the online board is wired up (the same service as Puyo's Revenge) but not switched on yet.

**Limitations:** Online scores are off until the leaderboard backend is set up; the screen says so.

versions.title: Guided training
versions.notes:
- Training now opens with a short guided course: walk, aim the torso, put a laser on a dummy, fire every group, reload, dash, vent, and duck out of a turret's sight behind cover.
- One prompt at a time on a checklist, ticked off the moment you do it.
- K skips the course. Once it's done (or skipped) Training goes straight to free practice.

versions.title: Paint and emblems
versions.notes:
- Paint your mech in the hangar: a primary colour, a secondary (trim) colour, a glowing accent, and an emblem on top of the torso.
- Six paints, five accents and two emblems are free. Arctic, Jungle, Crimson and Gold paint and the Star, Bolt, Skull and Crown emblems come from pilot challenges.
- Co-op friends see your paint and emblem, and you see theirs.

versions.title: Run stats and pilot ranks
versions.notes:
- The end screen shows how the run went: your loadout, damage dealt by each weapon, accuracy for each weapon group, and how many times you overheated.
- Pilot challenges: eight small goals like destroying 20 drones with energy weapons, reaching wave 10 in a Scout, or bringing down the Foundry. Each pays salvage plus a paint or an emblem (to wear from the next update).
- A Pilot screen on the title shows your rank (Recruit up to Legend), lifetime numbers, and every challenge with its progress.
- A banner pops up the moment you complete one.

**Limitations:** In co-op, wave records and spider shake-offs count only for the host for now.

versions.title: Missiles and mods
versions.notes:
- Missile Rack (shoulders only): hold its button on a robot to lock on (a diamond closes in, the weapon list counts up to LOCKED), let go to fire four missiles that climb over cover and dive onto it. Without a lock they go for the aim point.
- Rocket Pod (shoulders only): three dumb-fire rockets with a big blast, then a reload.
- Weapon mods: one per weapon, picked beside it in the hangar. Extended magazine, cooling jacket, long barrel and incendiary rounds. Buy each once with salvage, then fit it to any weapon it suits.
- The hangar's group picker is shorter (just the number and button) to make room.

versions.title: Artillery and the Foundry
versions.notes:
- New robot from wave 6: artillery crawlers. They hang back 22-40 m and lob shells; a red circle fills on the floor where each one will land, so keep moving.
- Every fifth wave, a boss: the Foundry, a giant four-legged walker. A Warning: large signature banner, then it drops onto a marked circle.
- Its glowing legs are weak points (double damage). Knock two out and it slumps, stunned, for 4 seconds.
- It telegraphs everything: a red sight line before a turret salvo, a big circle round its feet before a stomp, circles round you before a barrage.
- A health bar across the top while it's out. Each later Foundry has 40% more armor than the last.

versions.title: Spiders and shield drones
versions.notes:
- New robot from wave 4: spider walkers. Small and fast, they climb straight over cover and grab your legs; each one slows you and nibbles your armor. Dash (Shift) to throw them off.
- New robot from wave 5: shield drones. They hang over the other robots and throw a glowing bubble over everything near them. Hits on a covered robot go into the bubble; energy weapons pop it fastest, and the drone itself is never covered.
- The first time you meet each robot, a tip card names it and says what hurts it. Settings can turn the cards off.
- Spiders and shield drones get a warning banner the first wave they turn up, and briefings and the minimap know them.

versions.title: Extraction
versions.notes:
- Every mission now ends with extraction: once the goal is done the waves stop, a dropship hovers over a pad some way off, and the last robots rush you.
- Get onto the pad and hold it for 5 seconds to clear the sector. The count drains while you're off it.
- In co-op every pilot still standing has to be on the pad together.
- The music stays at full tilt until you're out.

versions.title: Uplinks and briefings
versions.notes:
- New mission goal, Hold the Uplink: stand inside the pad's ring for 90 seconds in all while the robots come at you. Signal Spire is now an uplink mission.
- A briefing before each mission: the goal, a picture of every robot you'll meet with how to beat it, and NEW on the ones you haven't been briefed on.
- Each briefing suggests a loadout for the job; one click fits it (anything you haven't unlocked falls back to what you have).

versions.title: Campaign
versions.notes:
- Campaign on the title: a map of eight sectors held by the machines, played in order. Clearing one opens the next, and your progress is saved.
- Missions have goals: survive a number of waves, destroy a relay tower, or escort a supply truck across the arena (it only drives with a mech beside it, and the robots shoot at it).
- Each sector has its own arena and starts a few waves in. The goal shows under the top bar and the objective on the minimap.
- The end screen has Retry and Campaign Map. Deploy stays endless.
- In co-op, friends ride along on the host's mission.

**Limitations:** Only the host's campaign progress is saved in co-op.

versions.title: Arena themes
versions.notes:
- Four arenas, picked beside Deploy (Random by default), each with a fresh layout every run.
- City Block: tall buildings with lit windows that you can knock down, with streets between them.
- Foundry: glowing lava channels. A 'Hot floor' warning shows when you step in and the first second is harmless, then it burns. Robots walk around them.
- Frozen Yard: sheets of ice where your legs slide. A tip shows the first time you step on one.
- The minimap shows lava and ice. In co-op everyone fights in the host's arena.

versions.title: Breakable cover and barrels
versions.notes:
- Cover can be destroyed: it cracks as it takes damage, then crumbles into rubble you can walk over. Tanks and robot mechs path through the gaps you open.
- Plasma and explosions are best at it; bullets barely chip it and fire does nothing.
- From wave 3, red-and-yellow fuel barrels stand around the arena and are restocked every wave. Shoot one and it bursts, hurting every robot and pilot nearby (you too) and setting off any barrel beside it. A warning shows the first time they appear.
- A barrel glows while it's in your aiming laser. Training has barrels to practise on.
- Each new run starts with the arena whole again.

versions.title: Music
versions.notes:
- A soundtrack, synthesized like the sound effects: a soft pad, bass, drums, and an arpeggio.
- It builds through each wave: bass as the robots warp in, drums once a quarter of them are down, and the arpeggio for the last stretch. Between waves it drops back to the pad.
- Settings > Music sets how loud it is (under the main Volume).

**Limitations:** The music is built while the title screen is up, so it starts a few seconds after the page loads.

versions.title: Marks and momentum
versions.notes:
- Guns kick out brass shell casings that bounce and lie where they land.
- Explosions leave scorch marks; lasers burn the floor and cover; bullets leave pocks. The oldest fade away once there are too many (fewer on Low graphics).
- Each chassis has its own weight: Scouts start and turn on a dime, Wardens take a moment, and the Juggernaut takes a step or two to get going and turns its legs slowly.
- Mechs leave footprints that fade, and the Warden's and Juggernaut's footsteps shake the camera a little.

versions.title: Wrecks and damage
versions.notes:
- Destroyed drones and tanks stay on the floor as dark, smoking wrecks for a while. Drones crash where they fall.
- Robot mechs topple over and explode a second later, and leave a wreck too.
- Killing a mech or a tank freezes the action for a split second. In co-op the camera kicks instead.
- Your mech shows its damage: the paint darkens as armor drops, sparks fly under half armor, and smoke trails under a third.
- Under a quarter armor an alarm beeps and the screen edge glows red until you patch up.

versions.title: Salvage
versions.notes:
- Destroyed robots drop salvage: drones 5, tanks 15, mechs 25. Walk near it and it flies to you; anything left lying around is collected when the wave ends. Your total shows top left.
- Spend salvage in the hangar: locked weapons and chassis show their price, and picking one unlocks it if you can afford it.
- New pilots start with the autocannon, the pulse laser, and the Warden. If you already played, everything in your saved loadouts stays unlocked.
- Settings > Unlock everything skips all that, for people who just want to play.
- In co-op everyone gets the salvage from every robot.

versions.title: The hangar bay
versions.notes:
- The hangar is a lit bay now: your mech stands on a slowly turning platform under two spotlights.
- A stat line under the hardpoints shows armor, speed, dash charges, damage per second, heat per second, and reach, and updates as you swap parts.
- Each hardpoint has a Test button: your mech fires that weapon at a dummy down the bay for a moment, with the real weapon, before you take it into a fight.

**Limitations:** Test fire is silent.

versions.title: Strider and presets
versions.notes:
- New chassis, the Strider: a fast, slim walker with one arm and one shoulder hardpoint. Its Shift is a jump that hops over low barriers. Robot pilots may bring Striders from wave 6.
- Four loadout presets across the top of the hangar: click one to swap your whole mech, and name it in the box beside them. Between waves, H then one click changes your loadout.
- Your old loadout is kept as preset 1.

versions.title: Utility hardpoints
versions.notes:
- Shield Projector: hold its button to raise an energy wall in front of the torso. Robot shots stop on it and turn into heat instead of damage.
- Repair Drone: press its button to launch a little drone that circles you and patches 8 armor a second while you run warm. Press again (or overheat) to recall it.
- Smoke Launcher: lobs a canister that bursts into a big grey cloud for 8 seconds. Robots can't see or aim through it; your shots go straight through.
- Any hardpoint can carry them, in any weapon group. The weapon list shows UP/READY and ON/OFF for them.

**Limitations:** In co-op, shots a friend's shield stops on the host don't add heat to the friend's mech.

versions.title: Dash and vent
versions.notes:
- Shift dashes the way you're walking (or the way the torso faces, standing still), for some heat. Scouts have two charges, Wardens one, and each comes back after a few seconds; the blue pips beside the heat bar show them.
- The Juggernaut's dash is a slow shove that knocks drones aside and dents them.
- V vents: heat drops fast and steam pours off the mech, but every weapon is locked for a second.
- Running hot (above 70 heat) slows the legs. The heat bar is always shown now, has a mark at 70, and flashes as you near 70 and as you near overheating.

versions.title: Graphics quality
versions.notes:
- Graphics setting: Low, Medium, High, or Auto. Lower levels turn shadows down or off, render the 3D view at a lower resolution, and use fewer sparks.
- Auto (the default) watches the first few seconds of each run and steps down a level if the game runs under 45 frames a second, with a banner saying so.
- Shots and effects reuse their pieces instead of building new ones, so busy fights stutter less.

versions.title: Minimap
versions.notes:
- Minimap in the bottom-right corner: the cover, you (white arrow), friends, robots in red (dot: drone, square: tank, triangle: mech), and repair kits in green. Settings can hide it.
- When only three robots are left, each one gets a red marker with its letter and distance, and the edge arrows for robots out of view show how far away they are.
- Fixed: a wave could say "1 left" with nothing to find. A robot that ends up outside the arena, or (with few left) goes 20 seconds unseen and unhurt, now warps back into the fight.

versions.title: Zoom and Tab
versions.notes:
- Zoom: the mouse wheel (or - and =) pulls the camera in or out while you play. Your zoom is remembered.
- Tab pauses and resumes, so you don't have to let go of the mouse with Esc. Esc and P still work, and Tab can't be a weapon button.
- The title screen shows the version and the name of this release next to the game's name.

versions.title: Co-op
versions.notes:
- Fight the waves together in the browser: during a run, Pause > Host Co-op opens a room and copies an invite link. Friends open the link, or type the room code under Join Co-op on the title screen.
- Everyone brings their own loadout. Friends' mechs wear their own trim color with a name and armor tag, and you see their shots.
- The robots go after whoever is nearest. Kills, the score, and repair kits are shared.
- If you go down, the run goes on: you're back up at half armor when the wave is cleared. The run ends when everyone is down, and the host can redeploy the whole team.
- Pausing in co-op doesn't stop the fight; your mech just stands still.

**Limitations:** Co-op needs the web build. The host's tab must stay visible, or the fight slows for everyone.

versions.title: Flamethrower
versions.notes:
- Flamethrower: hold its button to pour a short cone of fire. No ammo, but it runs warm.
- Anything caught in the flames burns for three seconds, taking damage the whole time; more fire keeps it burning.
- Its reticle is a translucent cone on the floor showing exactly what it will reach. Cover blocks the flames.
- Drones burn easily; tank armor shrugs off some of the heat. Enemy mechs may carry flamethrowers from wave 7.

versions.title: Plasma weapons
versions.notes:
- Plasma Gun: slow glowing bolts that burst on impact, splashing anything nearby.
- Plasma Cannon: hold its button to charge, release to fire. A full charge hits four times as hard and bursts wider; the reticle and weapon list show the charge.
- Plasma Mortar: lobs plasma over cover. Its reticle is a circle on the floor showing where it lands and how wide it bursts, with a dotted arc.
- Plasma uses cells and a little heat, and melts tank armor for extra damage.
- Enemy mechs start carrying plasma from wave 5. The hangar shows splash and charge details.

versions.title: Energy weapons
versions.notes:
- Three energy weapons, no ammo needed: Beam Laser (a continuous beam while held), Pulse Laser (rapid instant pulses), and Lance (a long-range energy spear).
- Heat: energy weapons warm your mech. Max it out and they lock until it cools; kinetic weapons keep working.
- A heat gauge sits under the reticle and under your armor bar, and flashes OVERHEATED when locked.
- Each energy weapon has its own reticle shape, and the hangar shows damage, heat, and range for every weapon.
- Drones take extra energy damage; enemy mechs resist it a little and start carrying lasers from wave 4.

versions.title: Loadouts and weapon groups
versions.notes:
- Three chassis: Scout (2 hardpoints, fast), Warden (arms plus a shoulder), and Juggernaut (all four hardpoints, slow and tough).
- Hangar (title screen, or H between waves and in training): pick a chassis, put a weapon on each hardpoint or leave it empty, and put each hardpoint in weapon group 1 to 4. A turning preview shows your mech.
- Each weapon group fires on its own button. Settings lets you choose them: click a group, then press any key or mouse button (defaults: left click, right click, Space, F).
- Lasers, reticle arcs, and the weapon list are colored by group and show the button that fires each weapon.
- Your loadout and settings are saved. Settings also has a volume slider.
- Enemy mechs come in Scout and Warden frames, and Juggernauts from wave 6.

**Limitations:** Q / E arm swapping is gone; use the hangar.

versions.title: Enemies
versions.notes:
- The machines fight back. Deploy starts waves of robots that warp in at the arena edges; each wave is bigger than the last.
- Drones: fast fliers that circle above the cover and peck with slow red bolts you can sidestep. Weak to energy weapons.
- Tanks (from wave 2): slow and armored, they path around cover, paint you with a red sight line, then fire a heavy shell. Armor blunts kinetic hits.
- Enemy mechs (from wave 3): the same mech as yours with a robot pilot and random arm weapons. They strafe and fire in bursts.
- Your mech can be destroyed: game over shows your wave, kills, and score, with Redeploy.
- Destroyed robots sometimes drop green repair kits.
- Training on the title screen keeps the old practice dummies with nothing shooting back.
- Damage numbers: red on you, gray when armor resists, yellow on a weakness. Red markers at the screen edge point to robots out of view.

versions.title: Kinetic weapons
versions.notes:
- Four kinetic weapons: Autocannon, Machine Gun, Scattergun (nine pellets), and Railgun (instant, pierces up to three targets).
- Left click fires the left arm, right click the right arm. Weapons have magazines and reload on their own when empty, or press R.
- Q and E swap the left and right arm weapons.
- Each weapon's reticle takes its shape: the arc widens with spread, the rail is a needle, and it fills back up as you reload.
- Aiming lasers end at each weapon's range.
- Tracers, muzzle flashes, sparks, damage numbers, recoil, camera kick, and synthesized gun sounds.
- Dummies take damage, break, and rebuild.

**Limitations:** Nothing shoots back yet: enemies arrive next update.

versions.title: Foundation
versions.notes:
- Pilot a mech around a walled arena: the legs walk where you steer (WASD) and the torso turns to face the cursor.
- Aiming lasers run from each arm along the way it would fire, stopping at the first wall or target, so you can see what your shot would hit.
- The weapon reticle follows where the torso is actually pointing and meets the cursor once the torso catches up.
- Practice dummies stand around the arena to aim at.
- Title screen, pause menu (Esc), and this Version Log.

**Limitations:** No weapons yet: they arrive next update.

versions.title: Self-directed iteration run
versions.notes:
Self-directed iteration run, version 2 of the roadmap (per Josh's 2026-10-14 mandate) - enemies arrive; the sandbox is no longer peaceful:

- **Biter nests:** 5 nests at deterministic map-edge cells (200 HP, health bars), each spawning a biter every 30 s (max 10 alive); waves every 2 min after a first wave at 5 min, size min(2 + wave, 10), HP scaling +10 percent per wave (all first-guess balance).
- **Biters:** seek the engineer or the nearest building, chew through blocking buildings (walls are real blockers); buildings have HP (wall 200, turret 120, others 60) and are destroyed without refund. Biters show health bars; kills are counted.
- **Gun Turret (new building, select with U):** range 6.5 tiles, 12 damage per shot, consumes Ammo Magazines (buffer 5), 10 shots per magazine. Craft cost 8 iron plate + 4 iron gear.
- **Ammo Magazine (new item):** hand-craft for 2 iron plates, deliberately NOT research-gated (BeltAndSteam lesson); the assembler does not make it in this version (see TODO). Starting kit gains 1 turret + 2 magazines.
- **Engineer combat:** 100 HP, left-click shoots the nearest biter/nest within 7.5 tiles when nothing is selected (auto-loads magazines, 1 = 10 rounds); death respawns at the map centre with full HP.
- **Victory:** destroying all nests shows a victory message and the sandbox continues. Nests, biters, HP, rounds, and wave state are stored in saves; nests and biters appear on the minimap; the top bar shows HP / nests / wave.
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: import clean, 300-frame run clean, feature harness 92/92 (68 prior + 24 new enemy checks), single-threaded Web export verified (GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false).

versions.title: Self-directed iteration run
versions.notes:
Self-directed iteration run, version 1 of the roadmap (per Josh's 2026-10-14 mandate) - coal finds a job, plus crafting depth:

- **Coal Generator (new building, select with G):** burns coal from its buffer - 1 coal = 10 s burn, contributes 25 generation while burning or while coal is buffered (first-guess balance). Craft cost 6 iron plate + 2 iron gear + 4 stone. Feedable by belt + inserter (accepts coal only, buffer 10); hover readout shows coal count and burn time; generator fuel state and the crafting queue are saved.
- **Timed hand-crafting queue (replaces instant crafting):** the C panel queues items (cost paid up front, max 10 queued), the front item crafts over time (2.0 s for buildings, 0.8 s for items - first-guess timings) and is delivered with a message; clicking a queued item cancels it with a full refund. An instant `craft_hand` helper remains only as an internal shortcut.
- **Hand mining:** hold left-click on a resource patch with nothing selected to mine by hand (0.7 s per item, mining progress percentage on the hover line).
- **TODO reconciled:** the v0.1.0 export-binaries P1 is Done - the zip-link watcher verified the binaries in git (commit 6577c4df).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: import clean, 300-frame run clean, feature harness 68/68 (see the export README), single-threaded Web export verified (GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false).

versions.title: Initial playable build
versions.notes:
Initial playable build - a new Factorio-like with 3D graphics on a 2D grid, built as a separate game next to BeltAndSteam (brighter, cleaner art, peaceful sandbox):

- 48x48 world, flat ground with a painted grid, deterministic resource patches (seed 12345): iron ore, copper ore, coal, stone.
- Engineer avatar (WASD), angled top-down perspective camera that follows the engineer, mouse-wheel zoom, R rotates the selected building.
- Mouse-ray grid cursor with a green/red placement ghost and a hover readout; left-click places, right-click hold (0.4 s) deconstructs with a full refund, X toggles demolish mode.
- Buildings (all 1x1): Miner, Conveyor Belt, Inserter, Furnace, Assembler, Chest, Lab, Solar Panel, Power Pole, Stone Wall - chunky BoxMesh visuals in distinct colours, with spinning parts on working machines and a visible item cube on belts.
- Items: iron ore, copper ore, coal, stone, iron plate, copper plate, iron gear, copper cable, red science.
- Simulation: belts hold 1 item and forward it when the next cell accepts; inserters swing items from the cell behind to the cell in front; miners output to their front cell or buffer; furnaces smelt ore to plate (powered, no fuel in v0.1.0); assemblers craft gears, cable, and red science.
- Solar power: panels generate 10, poles project coverage (radius 4), consumers draw Miner 5 / Furnace 5 / Assembler 8 / Inserter 1 / Lab 10, and satisfaction (generation / consumption, capped at 1) scales machine speed.
- Hand crafting (C) is instant with a cost check; research (T) has 3 techs fed by red science in labs - Logistics (belt/inserter speed x1.5), Efficiency (power use -30 percent), Advanced Automation (assembler speed x1.5). Completing all three shows a goal message; the sandbox continues.
- HUD: hotbar (1-0), inventory line, power and research readouts, version label, hover readout, message line, live minimap.
- Pause menu (Tab/Esc) with Help, the embedded Version Log, and named Save/Load; F5 quicksave / F9 quickload; saves are JSON at user://saves/.
- No enemies in v0.1.0 (see TODO.md P1).
- Validated with Godot 4.7.2 headless: import clean, 300-frame run with no script errors, feature harness (see the export README for the final count), single-threaded Web export verified (GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false).

versions.title: Fair enemy hitbox fix
versions.notes:
Fair enemy hitbox fix, from Josh's playtest report ("enemies hit me before they should; I can't swing over them once they're below my crowd"):

- **Root cause in v0.1.0:** contact was a fixed rectangle — an enemy triggered when its center was still 60 px above the crowd and up to 78 px to either side (wider than a small crowd really is), and the test had no lower bound, so it kept triggering for as long as the enemy was on screen, including after it had scrolled below the crowd.
- **Circle contact, sized by the crowd:** contact now requires the enemy's center within `contact_distance` of the crowd's center — the enemy radius and the crowd's actual formation radius, both shrunk to 85% of the drawn size, with the crowd radius capped at 64 px. Small crowds are far harder to clip; hits always look like hits.
- **Passed enemies are harmless:** an enemy whose center scrolls past the crowd's line (`PLAYER_Y + 6`) without touching is marked passed, drawn faded, and can never damage the crowd — swinging over or across it afterwards is safe.
- Harness grew from 49 to 61 checks: crowd-radius and contact-distance values, a grazing enemy inside the old rectangle that must not hit, an enemy scrolled past in another column that must not hit when the crowd swings onto it, and a dead-center enemy that still costs its remaining HP.
- Validated: headless import clean, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness 61/61, single-threaded Web export verified (`GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false`).

versions.title: Initial playable build
versions.notes:
Initial playable build — a mobile-ad style endless crowd runner, phone-first:

- Portrait 540x960 (9:16) playfield, touch drag steering (mouse drag and A/D / arrow keys also work), large tap-to-start and run-again buttons, GL Compatibility renderer.
- Crowd auto-runs upward forever and auto-shoots upward; bullet damage scales with crowd size (1 + 1 per 8 members).
- Gate pairs: steer through one gate per row — `+5` / `+10` / `+15` / `+20`, `x2` / `x3`, negative gates `-3` / `-5` / `-10` / `-15`, and `/2`. The first gate pair is a gentle `+10` vs `+5`.
- Numbered enemies block the track; an enemy that reaches the crowd alive damages the crowd by its remaining HP and is destroyed. Dodging an enemy avoids the damage entirely.
- Boss enemy every 5th event; run speed (255 to 430 px/s) and enemy HP scale with distance.
- HUD with crowd count, distance, and kills; floating gate/collision feedback; game-over screen with run stats; best distance saved to `user://`.
- Validated: headless import clean, 300-frame run with 0 script errors, feature harness (see SPENDING.md / export README for the count), single-threaded Web export verified (`GODOT_THREADS_ENABLED = false`).

versions.title: Harvest the swelling
versions.notes:
- Cutting a sprouting body with the machete while it swells (its last 15 s) now gives a sure spore sample.
- If it finishes sprouting first, it bursts into a small spore cloud as well as the new clump. The corpse tip says both.

versions.title: Infection forecast
versions.notes:
- A white tick on the infection bar shows where your infection would be if you walked straight to the exit now: the infected ground on the shortest way out, at walking pace, with your party, Resist and a respirator counted. So "can I afford one more crate?" has an answer.
- Hovering (or tapping) the infection bar says the number too.

**Limitations:** It assumes the shortest way and walking pace; sprinting, detours and a fresh bloom change it.

versions.title: Radio relay cache
versions.notes:
- Calling in a swap at a radio post: after picking who comes out, tick up to 3 things the outgoing survivor leaves in a cache crate at the post (arrows, a filter...) for the one coming in. The rest goes home as before.
- The cache is a quick search right by the radio.

versions.title: Rested bonus and camp jobs
versions.notes:
- A survivor who sits out 2 or more runs deploys Fresh for one run: stamina comes back 1.5x faster and searching is quicker. Their card shows how rested they are, and the deploy screen says when they're Fresh.
- Camp jobs: pick a job on a survivor's card for the runs they sit out (cook +1 food, mend +1 cloth, train +20 XP, guard +1 morale). The camp line after each run says what the bench did.

**Limitations:** Only ready survivors work; wounded ones rest (and count toward Fresh), quarantined ones don't.

versions.title: Take point
versions.notes:
- With a party member along, Z (Take point, rebindable) swaps who you control mid-run: you take over your partner where they stand, with their pack, health, infection and perk, and the other follows.
- A party member following you now takes only half the ground infection, so trading point spreads infection between the pair instead of piling it on one. A tip explains it the first run you bring someone, and the HUD's party line names the key.

**Limitations:** No gamepad button for it yet (keyboard only).

versions.title: After the source burns
versions.notes:
- Burning out the source now ends the campaign's story with a card over the camp: the world map turns from purple to green tile by tile, with how many runs it took, zones made safe, survivors saved and lost.
- From then on the infection in every open zone recedes a little after each run (a green chevron on the map), and the tide no longer makes zones worse. Strongholds still wait to be broken.

**Limitations:** Saves that already burned the source see the card once on their next visit to camp.

versions.title: Hive hearts
versions.notes:
- In zones of difficulty 2 and up, the spore heart farthest from where you come in is a hive (an orange bulb): it grows a new shambler every 20 s, up to 4 of its own at a time, until you burn it.
- The first time you see one, the camera swings over to it and a tip explains. It's in the field guide's hazards.

**Limitations:** Region hearts and the source are never hives.

versions.title: Enemy-type hints
versions.notes:
- The first time you see each kind of infected (shambler, runner, bloated, spitter, brute, a turned survivor), a tip says how to handle it: shoot bloated from a distance, stand your ground against runners, keep moving against spitters, and so on.
- Each hint shows once per save, one at a time, never in the tutorial or practice zone, and goes in the field guide.

**Limitations:** Lurkers, shriekers and wardens keep their own tips, which come at the moment they matter.

versions.title: Suspend a run
versions.notes:
- Leave a run mid-way and pick it up later: the pause menu has Suspend and quit, and a run is also kept whenever the game loses focus or the window closes.
- Next time, the title screen offers Resume run in (zone) (who), and camp shows the unfinished run with Resume run and Give up (lose loot). Deploying someone else gives it up.
- After an update an old suspended run can't be picked up; camp says so and the survivor comes home empty-handed.

**Limitations:** Plain runs only (not the tutorial, practice, the weekly seed or expeditions). Arrows in flight, thrown rocks, spit, clouds, fire and a search in progress don't come back.

versions.title: Run snapshots
versions.notes:
- Behind the scenes: a run in progress can now be written down whole (the map, infection, what you carry, every infected, recruit and crate, the dice) and rebuilt exactly. The next version uses it to suspend a run and resume it later.

**Limitations:** Nothing to see yet: resuming arrives in the next version. Arrows in flight, thrown rocks, spit, clouds, fire and a search in progress aren't kept.

versions.title: Pause when the tab hides
versions.notes:
- Losing focus in a run (switching tabs or apps, a call, closing the lid) pauses it at once, and the pause menu says why.
- Settings: Pause when the tab hides (on by default).

versions.title: No-hover fallbacks
versions.notes:
- On a touch screen every tooltip also opens with a tap: headings and labels with a tip show (?) and open it when tapped; buttons with a tip get a small ? button beside them (camp, deploy screen, field guide).
- Camp and deploy buttons get a 40 px minimum tap height on touch.
- Tapping the infection bar in a run pins its breakdown open; tap it again to close.
- Fix: a personal goal in a zone that was made safe some other way is swapped for a new one.

**Limitations:** Touch mode turns on when the device reports a touch screen or the first touch arrives; it stays on for the session.

versions.title: Item wheel
versions.notes:
- Hold Tab (keyboard) or LB (gamepad) to open the item wheel: a ring of the tools you carry this run (rock, lure, mask, injector, flare, torch, lantern, flashlight, pouch) with counts. The run slows while it's open.
- Point with the mouse or a stick and let go to use that tool; let go in the middle to use nothing.
- A quick Tab tap still pauses, and a quick LB tap still throws a rock.

**Limitations:** The single-key shortcuts still work; the wheel is an extra way to reach every tool.

versions.title: Personal goals
versions.notes:
- Every survivor carries a goal of their own, tied to a zone: find what's left of their family's place, burn a heart where they grew up, or see a zone made safe again. Their card shows it, and the world map marks the zone with a gold star.
- Meet it with them on the run (leading or as the partner) for a skill point, a line in their story and the chronicle; then they pick up another.

**Limitations:** Goals in zones that aren't open yet show on the card but not on the map until the zone opens.

versions.title: Region end card
versions.notes:
- Clearing a region heart now shows a card for that act over the camp: how many runs it took, how many of its zones are safe, survivors saved and lost while it was open, the best haul out of it, and which region opens next.
- Continue closes it; it waits for you if you leave camp before reading it.

**Limitations:** For saves from before this version, a region already open counts from now.

versions.title: Campaign chronicle
versions.notes:
- New at camp (Camp tab): the Campaign chronicle, the save's story as a timeline by run: who pulled whom out of where, hearts burned, zones reclaimed, the lost put to rest, who turned (out there or at camp), who joined or left, regions cleared, strongholds broken, the source burned.
- Copy as text puts the whole chronicle on the clipboard.

**Limitations:** The chronicle starts with this version and keeps the last 300 lines.

versions.title: Survivor stories
versions.notes:
- Each survivor keeps a short story written by their runs: "Pulled Ines out of the Subway", "Burned a spore heart in Old Market", "Reclaimed Orchard", "Put Rook to rest in Rail Yard", "Opened the strongroom in Clinic Row", "Burned out the source".
- A partner on the run gets the same lines. Their card shows the last three, and a memorial ends with their last line.

**Limitations:** Stories start with this version; earlier runs aren't written up.

versions.title: Loadout presets
versions.notes:
- The deploy screen lists what the run would take with a tick box each: untick what this survivor should leave in the stash.
- Save the ticks as a named preset (up to 3 per survivor, like "Quiet"), and pick a preset or Everything with one click next time. Arrows always come.

**Limitations:** A preset picks which kinds of gear to take, each up to its usual limit, not exact counts.

versions.title: Heart cores and region projects
versions.notes:
- Every spore heart you destroy now drops a heart core (a region heart's zone gives one more when it's reclaimed).
- Spend cores on region projects in the World tab, once per region: a Filter tower (the tide moves half as fast there), a Relay mast (distress calls there wait a run longer) or a Beacon (safe zones there hold out a run longer without supplies).

**Limitations:** Hearts destroyed before this version didn't drop cores.

versions.title: Kind first loss and the Courier perk
versions.notes:
- The first lost run on a save (brought back hurt or overrun) keeps its loot once: a patrol finds the body and brings the pack home, with a note on what normally happens.
- New perk, Courier (rescues and newcomers can have it): when they're brought back hurt, their pack comes home too. At level 5 they pick Retriever (even when overrun) or Light feet (searches 20% faster).
- The run summary says when a pack was brought home.

**Limitations:** Saves that already have runs count their free loss as used.

versions.title: Go back for the pack
versions.notes:
- When a survivor is brought back badly hurt, their pack stays where they fell for 2 runs. Send someone in to search it and extract to bring it home.
- The pack shows on the minimap (a brown square, even before you've seen it), as an icon on the world map and in the zone's text; a tip explains it the first time.
- Overrun survivors still turn and keep their gear, as before.

**Limitations:** Up to 3 packs wait in a zone. A pack you searched but lost on the way out is gone.

versions.title: Smell like them: docile scent and kinship
versions.notes:
- A trained docile companion within 4 m covers your scent: every infected notices you 40% slower, so a companion is a stealth tool too.
- Kinship: from Critical (75%+) infection shamblers take 30% longer to notice you; the infection bar says "Critical (they smell like you)".
- A tip explains each the first time, and both are in the field guide.

**Limitations:** Kinship doesn't stack with the spore mask (masked, they can't see you anyway).

versions.title: Zone dossier
versions.notes:
- Each zone remembers your history there: visits, the best haul brought out, who was lost there, and how the last run went (and in what weather).
- It shows under the zone on the world map and on the deploy screen.

**Limitations:** History starts with this version; earlier runs aren't counted.

versions.title: Spotted and heard on the summary map
versions.notes:
- The run summary's route replay now marks where an infected spotted you (orange A), where one heard a noise you made (a white ring) and where the zone bloomed (a purple ring), so a noisy run shows where it went wrong.
- Run log replays keep the new marks.

**Limitations:** A heard mark is only for your own noises (steps, shots, coughs); thrown rocks and lures aren't marked.

versions.title: Loot tells: the scavenger's eye
versions.notes:
- New skill, Eye (a scavenger's eye): spend points in it and unopened containers you can see glint by quality: grey for plain, gold for good (deep, cargo or a full one), blue for rare (the strongroom, the key, a pistol, a relic or a cure).
- The glint reaches 5 m with one point and 3 m more for each extra point.

**Limitations:** Glints only show for containers in your line of sight.

versions.title: Practise this
versions.notes:
- Field guide entries for things you've met that have a practice station (shambler, puffballs, lurker, spitter, shrieker, fire) get a Practise button: it starts the practice zone right at that station.

**Limitations:** Kinds and hazards without a station (runners, bloated, brutes, fog banks and so on) have no button yet.

versions.title: Map icons and a legend
versions.notes:
- The world map draws small icons under each zone instead of letter tags: radio post, contract, distress call (with runs left), herd, region heart, the source, trader, stronghold, a survivor turned there, getting worse (with runs left), outpost and conveyor belt.
- A Map legend button lists every icon; hovering a zone names its icons.

versions.title: Camp tabs
versions.notes:
- Camp's long side panel is split into tabs: World (map, expedition, trader), Workshop (stash, workbench, buildings), Lab (cure, research, quarantine, docile) and Camp (morale, memorials, requests, logs).
- Needs attention stays above the tabs, and a tab with something to fix shows a count, like Lab (1).
- The walkthrough, the camp walk and alert buttons open the right tab; the tab you were on stays open.

**Limitations:** The roster stays on the left rather than in its own tab.

versions.title: Survivor cards fit their column
versions.notes:
- A survivor's card at camp always fits its column: long buttons (inherit, cures) and notes wrap instead of pushing the roster sideways.
- The infection bar on the card and the Choose button are a little narrower.

versions.title: Tips name your keys
versions.notes:
- Tips, run prompts, the tutorial, the practice zone, the field guide, item tooltips and the camp walk now name the keys you bound in Settings instead of the defaults.
- With a gamepad in use, prompts name the pad buttons.

**Limitations:** Keys with no pad button (give, heal, seal) still name the keyboard key on a pad.

versions.title: Text and UI size
versions.notes:
- New setting, Text and UI size: 90%, 100%, 125% or 150% for the HUD, camp, menus, deploy screen and run summary.
- At the larger sizes the camp panel wraps long lines and buttons, the controls hint wraps, long menus (like Settings) and the deploy screen scroll so their buttons stay on screen, and the summary's route map gets smaller.

**Limitations:** The 3D view isn't scaled, only text and panels. At 150% the camp side panel wraps long buttons, and long menus and the deploy screen scroll.

versions.title: Colour-blind friendly infection
versions.notes:
- New setting, Colour-blind infection: infected ground turns orange and clean ground leans blue, instead of purple and green.
- Infected tiles also get diagonal stripes, so they read without colour at all.
- It applies to the ground in a run, the minimap, the route maps on the run summary and deploy screen, and the infection bar.

**Limitations:** Off by default. Mushroom clumps, spore clouds and the fog bank keep their colours; the setting is about reading the ground.

versions.title: Tooltips on camp numbers
versions.notes:
- Hover any item in the camp stash to see what it's for and where to find more (for example: Chemicals, used for medicine, ammo, filters...; from cabinets and cars, most in flooded subways).
- Every Make button at the workbench shows what the item does and its recipe; the camp headings (Stash, Workbench, Cure, Research, Buildings, Requests, Memorials) explain themselves on hover.

**Limitations:** Mouse hover only. Buildings and research already had their descriptions as tooltips.

versions.title: Infection breakdown on hover
versions.notes:
- Hover the mouse over the infection bar during a run to see where your infection came from over the last 30 seconds, by source, biggest first (for example: Infected ground +4.2%, Spitter +3.0%).

**Limitations:** Mouse only; the box lists the sources the game tracks (infected ground with party members included, drifting spores, spore fog, searching bodies, and hits by kind of infected).

versions.title: First 5 runs paced
versions.notes:
- A new save no longer opens with every camp section at once: the workbench opens after your first run, buildings after the second, requests and camp morale after the third, and research with your first spore sample.
- Each time something opens, the run's summary line says what's new at camp and what it's for; the bottom of the camp panel says what opens next.

**Limitations:** Saves from before this version with 3 or more runs keep everything open; younger saves open things on the same schedule. The camp walkthrough and the rest of the camp (stash, cure, ward, world map) are there from the start.

versions.title: Sound cues on screen
versions.notes:
- New setting, Sound cues on screen: small markers at the screen edge (or over the spot, when it's in view) point to important sounds, for playing muted or hard of hearing.
- Marked: shrieks, a giant's roar, an infected spotting you, your own cough coming, and footsteps of infected close by that you can't see. Each fades after a second and a half.

**Limitations:** Off by default. Footstep markers are for infected within 7 m that you can't see and that are on the move.

versions.title: Toggle options and aim assist
versions.notes:
- Settings has four new options: Hold to crouch (crouch only while the key is held), Toggle sprint (tap to run; it stops when you stop moving), and Hold to search (letting go of interact stops a search).
- Aim assist: when the reticle is within a metre of an infected you can see, it is pulled most of the way onto it, for steadier focused shots.

**Limitations:** All four are off by default. On a gamepad, the left trigger still sprints while held.

versions.title: Weekly spore seed
versions.notes:
- Camp has a Weekly spore seed button: one fixed zone a week (the same layout, weather and wind for everyone), one try per save.
- You go in as a stand-in with a fixed loadout (12 arrows, a medicine, a respirator and filter); nothing comes home and nothing at camp changes.
- At the end you get a short score card (time, loot, hearts burned, infection taken, score) with a Copy button to compare with friends; camp keeps your last card on the button's tooltip.

**Limitations:** The week turns over on Monday (UTC). The try is used up as soon as you start, so quitting the game mid-run doesn't give a second go. Copying needs the browser to allow clipboard access.

versions.title: Expedition mode
versions.notes:
- Once the source is burnt, camp has an Expedition section: send a survivor through the three farthest open zones in a row, with no camp in between.
- Each leg you extract from carries everything you have, and your infection, into the next zone; no radio swaps. Fall on any leg and everything carried is lost.
- Finish all three for a score (10 an item brought home, 50 a spore heart burned, minus 2 per point of infection taken) and a relic in the stash; camp shows your best score.

**Limitations:** The route is fixed by the map (the three farthest open zones), so it needs three open zones. No partner or trained companion comes along. If the game is closed between legs, camp has a button to carry on.

versions.title: Camp rooms: people and buildings
versions.notes:
- The walkable camp now shows your people: survivors at camp gather round the campfire, the wounded lie by it, and anyone in quarantine lies on a ward cot.
- The ward has a cot for every bed you've built; bought buildings (greenhouse, lab, watchtower, decon shower, storeroom) stand in the yard and block your way like the stations.
- Docile infected you keep are in a fenced pen, veterans' memorials are stones with their names, and your chosen camp banner flies by the gate.

**Limitations:** Survivors stand still for now; people out on supply lines or settled elsewhere aren't shown. The pen shows up to 6 docile infected.

versions.title: Camp rooms: the scene
versions.notes:
- Camp has a new Walk the camp button: walk your survivor around a small isometric camp yard.
- Each station opens its part of the camp menu: the gate opens the deploy screen, then the radio and map, stash, workbench, research table, ward, campfire (morale) and notice board (records).
- Esc goes back to the camp menu; the menu stays the quick way to do everything.

**Limitations:** The camp scene is plain blocks for now; survivors, buildings and memorials come next. Keys are the move keys and interact (E) as bound; the gamepad's interact button and Start work too.

versions.title: Survivor legacy
versions.notes:
- Veterans (level 8 and up) who are lost, turn, or leave camp now leave a memorial at camp and one legacy point.
- A level 8+ survivor at camp can retire from their card (press Retire twice); they leave for good with a memorial and a legacy point.
- Any survivor's card can take an unspent legacy point with Inherit: +1 skill point to spend like any other.
- The camp side panel lists the memorials (name, level, runs, and how they left).

**Limitations:** A Story-mode revive takes back the memorial and its point if the point wasn't spent yet. Retiring needs at least one other survivor at camp.

versions.title: Difficulty choice
versions.notes:
- Starting a new game now asks for a difficulty, shown on the save slot. Story: infection builds 40% slower, and anyone who turns can be cured back once (a cure; they return at 60% with a cure scar). Standard: the game as before. Hard: no sealed pouch, and zones you leave alone worsen twice as fast.
- On Story, a turned survivor's card has a Cure (revive, once) button.

**Limitations:** Saves from before this version are Standard. The difficulty can't be changed after the save starts.

versions.title: Extraction moment
versions.notes:
- The last 3 seconds before pickup (in the green ring, or at the end of a flare hold) now count down 3, 2, 1 with rising beeps, and a ring fills under the prompt.
- After you extract, the screen fades to black over a second and a half, showing the zone's name and what you carried, before the run summary.

**Limitations:** Runs that end any other way (abandoned, hurt, overrun) still go straight to the summary.

versions.title: Spotted moment
versions.notes:
- When an infected stops searching and starts chasing you, it now reads clearly: a sharp sting, a red ! over its head for a second, and a fifth of a second of slow motion.
- The slow motion can be turned off in Settings (Slow motion when spotted).

versions.title: Bow feel
versions.notes:
- Drawing the bow now creaks, rising in pitch as the string tightens.
- Perfect release: let go within a quarter of a second of reaching full draw. The reticle flashes white and grows during that window. A perfect shot flies straight even when your aim wobbles, flies 10% faster and hits 15% harder.
- Arrows that land stay visibly stuck where they hit, in walls or angled into the ground, until you pick them up. Up to 3 also show sticking out of an infected that survives the hit.

versions.title: Spore fog banks
versions.notes:
- New late-run hazard: after a zone's second spore bloom, a purple spore fog bank rolls in from one edge, never the one nearest the exit.
- You get a warning and a tip first, and the minimap shades the side it's coming from. 30 s later it starts creeping across the zone (a quarter of a tile a second), and the HUD says how far away it is.
- Inside the fog you see half as far and infection builds fast: 8% a second, halved by a working respirator. The death recap lists it as Spore fog. It pushes you toward the exit rather than ambushing you.
- Fog banks are in the field guide.

**Limitations:** The fog doesn't change the infected ground or the infected themselves.

versions.title: Mycelium tendrils
versions.notes:
- New hazard in zones of danger 1 and up: mycelium tendrils, purple roots across doorways and narrow gaps on infected ground.
- They glint once you're near and can see them, and the first time you do, a tip explains them. They can't catch you before you've seen them.
- Walk into them and they hold you for 2 seconds, and the struggle makes noise that infected hear. With the machete out, F cuts you free.
- The machete or fire clears them for the rest of the run. They're in the field guide.

versions.title: Spore lures and masks
versions.notes:
- Spore samples now have uses in the field, made at the lab (the camp building). A spore lure (1 spore sample, 1 cloth: makes 2) is thrown with N like a rock. It lies where it lands and pulls infected toward it with a pulse every second for 10 s.
- A spore mask (2 spore samples, 1 cloth) is put on with K. For 5 s infected can't see you, and anything chasing you loses track. They still hear you.
- A run takes up to 2 of each. N and K can be rebound in Settings.

**Limitations:** Lures and masks are keyboard-only for now, like give, heal and seal.

versions.title: Pistol worth carrying
versions.notes:
- The pistol now has an 8-round magazine and a 1.4 s reload. It reloads by itself when empty. The HUD shows the magazine, the rounds left and a reload bar, and the reticle greys out while you reload.
- Two new kinds of rounds from the workbench. Hollow-points (parts, scrap, chemicals) hit 50% harder and knock infected back further. Subsonic rounds (parts, cloth, chemicals) do a little less damage but make half the noise. Press R with the pistol out to switch (the new type loads).
- A suppressor (parts 2, scrap 2, cloth 1) halves the pistol's noise. A subsonic round through a suppressor is a quarter as loud as a plain shot.
- Runs take up to 12 of each special round and the suppressor along with the pistol.

versions.title: Recruits with personality
versions.notes:
- Every survivor you rescue now has a trait, shown when you recruit them, on the HUD party line, on their camp card and on the deploy screen.
- Brave: keeps holding when ordered even under attack, and has 20 more health.
- Jumpy: shoots anything in sight, even sleeping infected, a little faster, but every shot is loud.
- Quiet: crouches when you crouch (and holds fire while crouched), and only shoots infected that are closing in.
- Recruits without a trait now leave sleeping infected alone, and stop holding and come to you when clawed.

**Limitations:** The starting four survivors and anyone rescued before this version have no trait.

versions.title: Route pins on the deploy screen
versions.notes:
- Camp now remembers each zone's layout: every tile you've explored on any run there.
- The deploy screen shows that map under Plan a route. Click to drop up to 3 numbered pins (click one again to lift it).
- On the run, each pin stands as a tall numbered marker you can see over walls, and the minimap shows it too. Pins are used up by the run.
- Walls, spore hearts and the strongroom stay put between runs; containers move, so pin places, not loot.

**Limitations:** Zones you visited before this version have no map until you go back.

versions.title: Overstay warning and exit pointer
versions.notes:
- A small arrow at the edge of the screen now points to the way out, with how far it is, whenever the exit isn't on screen.
- When heading home is clearly the right call, a warning says so once and the arrow pulses green with the reason: past 80% infection, carrying a story note or the strongroom haul, every spore heart down, or the warden down. That way a good run isn't thrown away by accident.
- Fixed: after a mycelial sense run, the next zone could log errors about rings that no longer existed.

versions.title: Camp goals strip
versions.notes: - A gold Next line under the camp title always says what to do next, picked from where the campaign stands: an urgent alert first, then burning out the source once you know where it is, the spore hearts left in a half-cleared zone, your first safe zone, the region heart that opens the next region, the story notes still to find, and strongholds after that.

versions.title: Supply alerts at camp
versions.notes:
- Camp now opens with a Needs attention list when something is about to go wrong: a safe zone that falls within 2 runs without supplies, a distress call running out, a Critical survivor outside the ward, the trader leaving after the next run, or morale about to break.
- Each alert has a button that deals with it: Restock sends supplies, Deploy there picks the zone and opens the deploy screen, Quarantine moves the survivor to the ward, and Trade scrolls to the trader.

**Limitations:** Zone contracts never expire, so they don't raise alerts.

versions.title: Music and ambience
versions.notes:
- Each biome has its own quiet ambient bed on runs: wind in the ruins, crackling in the fungal forest, dripping in the flooded subway, a thin hum in the hospital and gusts over the farmland. It plays a little lower at night.
- When an infected starts chasing you (or a shrieker rears), a tense pulsing layer swells in. It drops back a few seconds after the last one loses you.
- A short camp theme plays at camp and on the title screen.
- New Music volume slider in Settings.

**Limitations:** All music is made in code. Each loop is generated the first time it plays, which can cause a short hitch on slow machines.

versions.title: Camp records and milestones
versions.notes:
- Camp records (a new button beside the field guide): lifetime stats such as runs, extractions, zones reclaimed, infected cured back, strongrooms opened, the longest run home, the biggest haul and how many runs in a row nobody was lost.
- Nine named milestones, such as First one home, Cured 5 infected back and No one lost in 10 runs. The camp line says when you reach one.
- Each milestone you reach unlocks a banner colour. Pick one on the records page and it flies under the camp title.

**Limitations:** Records count from this version; runs before it only show in the totals (runs, kills, subdues).

versions.title: Turn them back
versions.notes:
- A trained docile infected can be cured: press Cure next to it at camp (1 cure). It becomes a survivor again, with a new name and a random perk, still weak at 30% infection and with a cure scar.
- So the loop runs all the way: subdue, sedate, train, then cure. Each cure spent this way is one you don't use on your own people.

versions.title: Mycelial sense and cure scars
versions.notes:
- Mycelial sense: from 50% infection a survivor senses spore hearts and hidden lurkers within 14 m, shown as purple rings even through walls. A tip explains it the first time. A reason to push a badly infected survivor one run further.
- Cure scars: every cure (and experimental cure) leaves a scar, up to 3. Each one means 10% less infection gain for good, but 5 less max health. The survivor's card shows them.

**Limitations:** Cures from before this version left no scars.

versions.title: Spore wind
versions.notes:
- Most runs now have a spore wind, shown as an arrow across the minimap. A tip explains it at the start, before any cloud.
- Spore clouds from bloated bursts and puffballs drift downwind for a moment, leaving infected ground behind them and infecting you if they pass over you (a respirator halves it). Approach from upwind.

versions.title: Gamepad support
versions.notes:
- Play with a gamepad: left stick moves, right stick aims, the right trigger draws and fires, the left trigger sprints. A searches and recruits, B crouches, X shoves, Y switches arrows, LB throws a rock, RB switches weapon, the D-pad works the flashlight, lantern, torch and flare, Back uses an injector, Start pauses.
- While you use a pad the prompts and the controls hint name pad buttons; touch the mouse or keyboard and they switch back. The pause menu and Settings > Controls list the pad buttons.
- Menus can be driven with the D-pad and A.

**Limitations:** Pad buttons can't be rebound yet. Giving arrows, healing recruits and sealing the pouch stay on the keyboard.

versions.title: Day and night
versions.notes:
- Pick Day or Night for your next run on the world map (Next run: Day / Night); the deploy screen says which.
- Night is darker and you see a quarter less far, but about half the infected are asleep: slumped, blind and still until a noise, a hit or you walking right up to them wakes them. Good for sneaking and takedowns.
- By day you see well, but 10% more infected are about and all of them awake. A tip explains night on your first one.

versions.title: Locked rooms
versions.notes:
- Zones of danger 1 and up have a locked strongroom with a well-stocked crate inside. Once you've seen its door, a padlock marks it on the minimap.
- Its key is in the container farthest from the door. Or make a crowbar at the workbench (3 scrap, 1 parts) and force the door: 3 seconds standing still, loud every second, and a hit stops you.

versions.title: Set pieces
versions.notes:
- Every zone now has a landmark that stays put from run to run, named in its zone text on the world map.
- A crashed supply truck, with a cargo crate full of loot beside it. A barricaded house with one door, clean ground inside and a survivor holding out. A collapsed overpass: a long wall of rubble across the zone that you have to go round.

**Limitations:** Zones' layouts change a little where the landmark now stands.

versions.title: Docile kinds play differently
versions.notes:
- A sedated infected keeps its kind, and once trained it fights like one. The camp list names the kind and says what it does.
- Runners scout a few metres ahead of where you aim and mark the infected near them, so you see those through walls for a moment. Spitters stay back and spit at infected from range.
- Brutes have 200 health and their blows shove infected back and stun them. Shamblers and the rest follow and claw as before.

**Limitations:** Docile infected from older saves count as shamblers.

versions.title: Migrating herds
versions.notes:
- From your third run a herd of infected wanders the world map (HERD on its zone), moving to a neighbouring open zone or staying put after each run.
- The herd's zone has twice the shamblers, and they all move as one group. A noise any of them hears draws the whole herd, so a rock or noise arrow thrown far away can lure it off your path.
- A tip explains the herd when you arrive; the zone text and the deploy screen warn you before you go.

versions.title: Corpse sprouting
versions.notes:
- In zones of danger 1 and up, the infected you kill leave their bodies behind. After a minute a body sprouts into a new mushroom clump and the ground around it turns purple.
- For the last 15 seconds the body swells, twitches and glows. Slash it with the machete or burn it to stop it. A tip explains this with your first kill there, and the field guide keeps it.

**Limitations:** Bloated infected burst as before and leave no body.

versions.title: Trader caravan
versions.notes:
- Every 4 runs, if you have a safe zone, a trader caravan stops at one of them for 2 runs (TRADER on the world map).
- At camp the Trader section lists 4 swaps at the trader's own rates (scrap for parts, food for medicine, sticks for arrows...) and one rare item such as a pistol, a cure, a vaccine or a respirator. Each swap can be made once, paid from the stash.

versions.title: Settlers and defences
versions.notes:
- Settle a ready survivor in a safe zone (world map, zone selected): they live there and rest, the zone makes 1 more of its goods a run, and it holds one more run without supply. Recall them from their card.
- Defences for safe zones, up to 3 of each: barricades (3 scrap, 1 parts) hold one more run without supply; lantern posts (scrap, parts, fuel) light the zone and push the infection in the zones beside it back 25% faster.
- On later visits you see the extra fences, the lantern posts and your settlers. A zone that falls loses its defences and sends its settlers home.

**Limitations:** Someone always stays ready at camp: you can't settle your last ready survivor.

versions.title: Zone roles
versions.notes:
- Safe zones get a role: pick it on the world map with the zone selected (the first pick is free; changing it later costs 3 scrap).
- Farm: food each run. Workshop: scrap and parts by turns. Clinic: medicine, and every supplied clinic makes quarantine 3% a run faster. Watch post: no goods, but shows what waits in the zones beside it, like the watchtower.
- Until you pick, a zone makes what it always made. The map shows each safe zone's role, or pick a role.

versions.title: Post-game strongholds
versions.notes:
- Once the source burns, the three hardest zones become strongholds (STRONGHOLD on the world map): danger 3 higher, even if you had made them safe.
- Each stronghold is held by a named warden, a giant infected that is very tough and hits hard. A tip names it when you arrive; the deepest containers hold extra loot.
- Put the warden down (kill or subdue) and extract to take its relic home and break the stronghold. Each relic lifts camp morale by 5.

**Limitations:** Saves where the source already burned get their strongholds when they load.

versions.title: Camp morale
versions.notes:
- Camp has a morale meter (0-100) in the side panel, with what is raising or lowering it: food in the stash, safe zones, survivors lost lately and requests you filled lately.
- After each run morale moves part of the way towards where those point. At 70 or more quarantine works 25% faster and research costs a spore sample less.
- Below 30 an extra request comes in. Below 20 camp warns you; if it is still that low after the next run, someone who isn't on the run leaves for good (never your last survivor).

**Limitations:** Morale starts at 60 in older saves; losses and requests count from this version.

versions.title: The tide
versions.notes:
- Open zones you leave alone get worse: every 4 runs (6 if a safe zone is next to it) a zone's danger goes up by 1, up to 3 above where it started. More and tougher infected come with it; its spore hearts stay the same.
- The world map shows worse in N runs on zones about to tip, and a purple border on zones that have already worsened. The zone text gives the details.
- The first time a zone worsens, camp explains the tide.

**Limitations:** The count starts with this version: zones in older saves begin their first 4 runs now.

versions.title: Regions
versions.notes:
- The world map is split into three regions, one per row: the City, the Outskirts and the Farmland, each with a heading on the map.
- Safe zones open the zones beside and above them, but the next region only opens once you clear its region heart zone (Water Works for the City, Mill District for the Outskirts; RH on the map). Its spore hearts are bigger and tougher.
- Clearing a region heart zone opens the region below every safe zone in that row. Camp: building and research buttons are shorter, with their description underneath, so the side panel no longer runs off the screen.

**Limitations:** Saves where a lower row was already open keep it open.

versions.title: Experimental cures
versions.notes:
- New research: Experimental cure (3 spore samples). Then brew cheap cures at the workbench: 1 spore sample and 1 medicine.
- Using one clears infection like a cure, cleanly 70% of the time. Otherwise the survivor is cured but has a side effect for 3 runs: slow stamina, or a cough that won't stop (it coughs even when Clean). The odds and effects show next to the button.
- The survivor's line at camp shows the side effect and how many runs it has left.

versions.title: Decon shower and field injector
versions.notes:
- Field injector: craft one at the workbench (medicine, chemicals, a spore sample); a run takes up to 2. Press J on a run and stand still for 4 seconds: infection drops by 15%. Getting hit stops it (you keep the injector).
- Decon shower: a new camp building (5 scrap, 3 parts). When you extract, it spends 1 chemicals to wash off 30% of the infection you gained on the run; the summary shows how much.
- J can be rebound in Settings > Controls like the other keys.

versions.title: Strains
versions.notes:
- Each zone's infection is one of three strains. Creeping: blooms come every 75 s and spread twice as far. Airborne: spore clouds from bursts and puffballs spread 40% wider. Rooting: infection caught there comes out at half speed in quarantine for 2 runs.
- Bring home a spore sample from a zone to learn its strain: the world map shows it and a tip explains it when you go back.
- Once a strain is known, research a targeted cure for it: curing someone that strain infected gives back a spore sample and leaves them resistant 2 runs longer.

versions.title: Death recap
versions.notes:
- The run summary now says what hurt you: damage and infection by source (each kind of infected's claws, spitter globs, bloated bursts, puffballs, fire, infected ground, searching bodies), worst first.
- On a lost run it's shown larger, so you can see what did it.

versions.title: Practice zone
versions.notes:
- A Practice zone you can play any time from the title screen or from camp: a strip of stations, each with a prompt, for crouching past a cone, throwing a rock, sealing a find in the pouch, puffballs, a lurker clump, a spitter, a shrieker, burning a patch with the torch and calling a flare.
- You get a free loadout (arrows, fuel, medicine, a respirator) and nothing is saved. Each station moves on when you do it, or when you walk past it.
- The guided first run for new players is unchanged.

versions.title: Field guide
versions.notes:
